structured_extraction.program_description: A legal assistance program that provides free lawyers to renters facing eviction who meet income requirements.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free legal representation provided to renters living in Maryland facing eviction who have a household income at or below 50% of Maryland's median income. Access to Counsel representatives help determine if applicants qualify.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Renters facing eviction with household income at or below 50% of Maryland's median income
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal representation in eviction proceedings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Household income at or below 50% of Maryland's median income
Facing eviction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Access to Counsel program to determine eligibility and connect with a free lawyer.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides zero percent interest, deferred loans for up to 30 years or grants to help seniors make their homes accessible. Eligible improvements include grab bars, railings, ramps, widened doorways, accessible showers, and other modifications that help older residents remain independent in their homes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest, deferred loans for up to 30 years with loan amounts up to $50,000 maximum. Loans are based on applicant income and ability to repay, with interest rates ranging from 0% to 6%. Loans over $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage. For households with incomes at or below 50% of the statewide or Washington DC MSA median income, deferred principal and interest payments may be available if necessary for project feasibility. Grants up to $25,000 are available for seniors who do not qualify for loan funding. All closing costs are included in the loan. Loans must be repaid upon sale, transfer, or refinance of the property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 55 or older who own and occupy their home as their principal residence and meet income requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessibility improvements to make homes functional for seniors, including grab bars, railings, ramps, widened doorways, accessible showers, lever handles, first floor bathrooms and laundry rooms on a case-by-case basis, and other modifications to support independent living.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Applicants must be Maryland residents. Income limits vary by household size and region: Washington DC PMSA (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's counties) vs. Rest of State.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident with at least one household member age 55 or older
Own and occupy the home as principal residence (seniors living with relatives considered case by case)
Reside in a structurally sound home free of health and safety hazards
Have no outstanding federal or state tax liens, open bankruptcy, or foreclosure
Household income cannot exceed 80% of statewide or Washington DC MSA median income (specific limits vary by household size and region as of July 1, 2025)
Provide proof of home ownership (deed and current mortgage statement)
Provide valid photo identification
Submit most recent property tax bill and homeowner's insurance declaration page
For pre-1978 homes, acknowledge receipt of lead-based paint hazard information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available at local County Housing Offices or Maryland Access Point Agencies. Applicants can submit applications by email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or by mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Assistance in completing the application is available at the agency, and in-home appointments can be scheduled. Required supporting documentation includes income verification (paystubs, tax returns, bank statements, award letters), proof of home ownership, property tax bill, homeowner's insurance declaration, and flood insurance if applicable. Once submitted, the application is processed by the department and the applicant will be contacted.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI) demonstrates how strategic investment in local housing and businesses can lead to healthy, sustainable communities with a growing tax base and enhanced quality of life. The program focuses on areas where modest investment and coordinated strategy will have meaningful neighborhood revitalization impact. It provides competitive capital project funding for revitalization efforts in the Baltimore region to further community development goals, with projects required to be located within Sustainable Communities boundaries and aligned with approved community revitalization plans.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant and loan funding for community development projects located in Sustainable Community Areas in Baltimore City and the inner beltway of Baltimore and Anne Arundel counties. Projects may include down payment assistance for homebuyers, acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant or blighted properties, improvements to residential and business properties, energy efficiency programs (weatherization and energy retrofits), mixed-use development combining housing, retail, and office space, community open space or public infrastructure development, workforce and employment development, strategic demolition, and operating costs for community enhancement projects. Applications are submitted through the Project Portal after organization registration.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY26 Application Round is closed
structured_extraction.contact_name: Regional Project Manager (Kevin Baynes / Jessica DeGaine)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Organizations with an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan may apply. Cross-jurisdictional partnerships including Community Development Financial Institutions are eligible and encouraged. Baltimore region communities seeking to revitalize neighborhoods and support community development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for homebuyers, acquisition and rehabilitation of vacant or blighted properties, improvements to residential and business properties, energy efficiency through weatherization and energy retrofits, mixed-use projects combining housing, retail, and office space, community open space or public infrastructure development, workforce and employment development programs, strategic demolition, operating costs for community enhancement projects, and capital projects supporting neighborhood revitalization, community development, and placemaking in the Baltimore region.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Sustainable Community Areas in Baltimore City and the inner beltway of Baltimore and Anne Arundel counties. Specific eligible addresses can be verified using the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper. Regional Project Managers are assigned by geography: Region 1 (Northwest Baltimore City/County), Region 2 (Northeast Baltimore City/County), Region 3 (Southeast Baltimore City/County), Region 4 (Southwest Baltimore City/County and Northern Anne Arundel).
requirements_list: Applicants must have an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan. If a plan is not yet approved, it must be submitted with the application.
Projects must be targeted in a specific neighborhood or set of neighborhoods.
Projects must be part of the approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan.
Projects must capitalize on the strengths of the community.
Projects must be located in Sustainable Community Areas in Baltimore City or inner beltway of Baltimore and Anne Arundel counties.
Projects must align with community revitalization goals and help achieve outcomes identified in community action plans.
Applying with partner organizations, like Community Development Financial Institutions, is strongly recommended.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Project Portal after organization registration. Community Development Organizations that do not have an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan must submit one at the time of application along with their projects. The strategic neighborhood revitalization plan must be approved by the Department prior to any funding awards. The typical application timeline includes training, application opening, organization registration cutoff, application closing, review period, and award announcement. Contact your assigned Regional Project Manager if you have questions about whether a specific address is eligible. For more information, visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative (formerly known as Project C.O.R.E.) provides capital to Baltimore City, the Maryland Stadium Authority, and Baltimore City's community-based development organizations to redevelop vacant properties. The program focuses on scaling the renovation of vacant buildings on clusters of contiguous blocks, and may also support the redevelopment of vacant lots for housing, mixed-use projects, and green space. Grant funding is provided to eligible public and nonprofit partners for acquisition, stabilization, demolition, and pre-development activities related to vacant properties in Baltimore City. The initiative aims to move at least 5,000 vacant properties into homeownership or other positive outcomes over five years. Projects must be located within Sustainable Community Areas in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FY27 BVRI funds are provided as partially forgivable subordinate loans from Maryland Community Investment Corporation (MCIC). Forgiveness is based on Net Sale/Refinance Proceeds and project appraisal gap. Grants and loans finance: acquisition, stabilization, and renovation of vacant buildings (prioritizing those with city-issued vacant building notices); acquisition and aggregation of vacant lots for new infill housing construction, mixed-use projects, and community-managed open space; urgent demolition of vacant buildings posing community health risks or furthering near-term redevelopment; predevelopment activities including architectural, engineering, and site infrastructure work. BVRI loans are available for acquisition and pre-development soft costs, construction financing gaps, and closeout appraisal gap coverage. Forms of financial assistance include renovation and new construction loans or lines of credit to be repaid through home sales or refinance into permanent financing for rental projects, grant funds to fill gaps between total development costs and sale prices, and credit enhancement to leverage private capital.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community development organizations (CDOs) that are nonprofits with a track record of completing rehabilitation of vacant property and/or infill new construction projects, operating to improve the physical, economic, or social environment of their geographic areas of operation in Baltimore City. CDOs may have sub-recipients including development partners. Also eligible: public organizations and nonprofit partners in Baltimore City working to address vacant properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, stabilization, and renovation of vacant buildings (prioritizing those with city-issued vacant building notices); acquisition and aggregation of vacant lots for new infill housing construction, mixed-use projects, and community-managed open space; urgent demolition of vacant buildings posing community health risks or furthering near-term redevelopment; predevelopment activities including architectural, engineering, site infrastructure, and site development; residential rehabilitation, residential infill new construction, modular infill construction, commercial/mixed-use projects, and open space projects with community-managed stewardship. Primary investment priority is renovation of residential properties with emphasis on homeownership outcomes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Activities must be located in Sustainable Community Areas in Baltimore City. Special consideration will be given to projects in the Baltimore City Vacancy Reduction Priority Geographies, which includes the Impact Investment Areas. Applications may include ENOUGH areas and Just Communities areas for bonus considerations. Target areas should include contiguous clusters of whole blocks where the organization can directly abate or facilitate abatement of all vacant property, particularly buildings with Vacant Building Notices.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a community development organization (nonprofit) with a track record of completing rehabilitation of vacant property and/or infill new construction projects
Organizational mission must include community development work with a service area in Baltimore City
Activities must be located in clusters of contiguous blocks within identified target area
Applicant must demonstrate capacity and a plan to address all vacant property over time in target area
Projects should achieve whole block outcomes where every property on a block has a productive use
Applications without completed property pipeline spreadsheet will not be considered for funding

Applications must include all required organizational documents: By-Laws, Articles of Incorporation, Board Roster, Annual Report, IRS Letter of Determination, Financial Audit, Operating Budget, Profit & Loss Statement, Balance Sheet, and signed Public Disclosure Authorization
CDOs may be required to provide government resolution, corporate board resolution, and charitable registration if funded
All required partner letters and supporting documentation must be included with application
Target area should be approximately 5 blocks by 5 blocks and be walkable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application exclusively through Survey123 online portal. Applications open February 18, 2026 at 10:00 AM and close April 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM. Paper applications will not be accepted. Application is automatically saved in browser; no account creation needed. Maryland DHCD cannot see application until submitted. Key application components include: (1) Identified Target Area with map and justification; (2) Vacant Revitalization Strategy narrative describing blocks, remediation strategies, prioritization, and 6-month outcomes; (3) Vacant Property Pipeline spreadsheet listing all potential properties with characteristics, proposed strategies, remediation costs, and post-remediation uses; (4) Additional Project Types sections for residential infill, modular infill, commercial/mixed-use, and green space placemaking projects. Application requires uploading organizational documents, property pipeline spreadsheet, partner support letters, sources and uses budgets, site plans, designs, and evidence of site control. Training webinar held 2/25/2026; recording and step-by-step instructions posted on BVRI website. Application scoring: Organization Experience and Development Capacity (30 points), Whole-Block Redevelopment Strategy and Program Alignment (30 points), Vacant Property Pipeline and Production Readiness (25 points), Budget and Financing (15 points). Projects in ENOUGH and Just Communities areas receive up to 10 bonus points each. Site visits and follow-up discussions may occur during review.

structured_extraction.program_name: BeSMART Energy Efficiency Loan for Homeowners
structured_extraction.program_description: The BeSMART Home Loan Program provides financing to improve the energy efficiency and comfort of your home. Homeowners can replace and upgrade appliances, heating, ventilation and cooling systems, and make whole house envelope improvements to save on utility bills.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unsecured loan with a 6.99% APR. Up to $30,000 in financing is available for energy efficiency measures for a term of up to 10 years. Minimum loan amount is $5,000. Based on verification of credit and ability to pay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners looking to improve energy efficiency and comfort of their homes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements including insulation and air sealing, ENERGY STAR heating and cooling systems, ENERGY STAR hot water heating equipment, ENERGY STAR appliances, windows and doors, lighting and controls, programmable and smart thermostats, ceiling fans and ventilation fans, geothermal heat pumps, solar photovoltaic (capped at 1:1 match to energy efficiency measures), health and safety costs related to energy improvements (up to 25% of energy measure costs), and other improvements identified in a certified energy audit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Maryland homeowner
Credit score of 640 or greater
Debt to income ratio that does not exceed 50%
BeSMART cannot finance projects or upgrades that are already purchased or already completed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online BeSMART Loan Application or email to request a paper application. Email all required income documentation to get pre-approved on a financial basis. Submit project specifications including scope of work, contractor estimates, and ENERGY STAR equipment specifications. Complete loan documents provided by DHCD that must be signed and notarized. Project kicks off with an initial draw of funds. Upon completion, you and your contractor confirm work has been completed to specifications, contractor submits photos, and both sign a Certificate of Completion for final draw to be issued.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Business Boost Microgrant provides funding to support small businesses seeking to expand, establish a new location, or transition home-based businesses to their first commercial location outside of the home. Offered through the Neighborhood BusinessWorks program, it prioritizes businesses in Sustainable Communities areas and those that demonstrate potential for economic growth through job creation, capital investment, or increased business square footage.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers up to $2,000,000 in microgrants ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 per business. Applicants must provide a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount. Funds can be used for capital and operating expenses that support revenue growth from September 23, 2024, through March 23, 2025, including salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, and professional services. Only new expenses are eligible; existing expenses cannot be covered.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Monday, October 14th, 2024, at 5 PM EST. NOTE: The round may close sooner if grant requests exceed available funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses with more than 2 and no more than 50 full-time equivalent employees as of September 23, 2024, and annual revenue between $50,001 and $999,999 seeking to expand, establish a new location, or move from home-based operations to a commercial location within a Sustainable Communities area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and operating expenses that support revenue growth from September 23, 2024, through March 23, 2025. Eligible uses include salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, and professional services. Only new expenses are eligible; increases in existing rent and payroll can be covered but not the existing base amounts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in a Sustainable Communities area in Maryland. Applicants can use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper at https://portal.dhcd.state.md.us/GIS/revitalize/index.html to verify if their business location qualifies.
requirements_list: Be a for-profit business
Be located in a Sustainable Communities area
Have greater than 2 employees and 50 or fewer employees (full-time equivalent) as of September 23, 2024
Have an annual revenue of at least $50,000 but no more than $1 million
Be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Have a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount
Professional services and sales-based businesses (including Insurance, Accounting, Real Estate, Legal, and Finance) are not eligible

Non-profit organizations, cannabis-based businesses, pawn shops, gun shops, massage parlors, adult video/book shops, adult entertainment facilities, rental real estate businesses, Insurance companies, tanning salons, check-cashing facilities, gambling facilities, tattoo parlors, and liquor stores are not eligible
Previous award winners of an NBW Opportunity Zone grant and an NBW Business Boost grant are not eligible
Submit Articles of Organization for the business
Submit By-laws for the business
Submit most recent annual tax return for the business filed (Tax year 2023)
Submit organization's financial statements as of August 31, 2024
Submit screen-shot showing the business is in an eligible location
Submit proof of matching funds equal to or greater than the grant request amount
Submit screen capture of Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Submit IRS W-9 Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification
Business name on application must EXACTLY match SDAT's Good Standing Certificate and W-9
DHCD awards must be approved by a local resolution from the applicant's governing executive body
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application round opened on Monday, September 23, 2024, at 12:00 noon and closed on October 14, 2024 at 5 PM EST. Applicants submit an online application at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/NBWOZGrant/account/login providing a brief description of the organization, answers to questions about the business, and a budget table showing how grant funds and matching contributions will be used. Only fully completed applications at the time of submission are considered; incomplete applications are returned. Applications are evaluated based on meeting eligibility requirements, the location of the business, the impact of the business's expansion (new employees to be hired, capital investment, additional square footage), and presentation of the business's financials and supporting documents. Priority consideration includes innovative small businesses driving innovation or technology, businesses growing in new industries, businesses focused on regional strengths, businesses leveraging partnerships with educational institutions, and Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs). Award announcements are made on a rolling basis during December 2024 to January 2025, with grant funds expected to be paid in February-March 2025. Awardees must submit a final report by March 31, 2026, documenting how funds were used, and will be contacted nine months after receiving funds to complete a questionnaire and provide a one-page summary of the grant's impact.
