structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery Assistance - Grant #2 ($20M, Multiple Disasters: Sandy, Irene, Tropical Storm Lee, and Derecho)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal funding provided to Maryland to support recovery activities related to multiple disaster events: Hurricane Sandy, Hurricane Irene, Tropical Storm Lee, and the Derecho. The State received $20 million through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development's CDBG-DR Program for necessary expenses related to disaster relief, long-term recovery, restoration of infrastructure and housing, and economic revitalization in the most impacted and distressed areas. At least 80% of funding ($16 million) was directed to Somerset County as the most impacted county. Funds were distributed through five phases with HUD-approved action plan amendments, covering counties across Maryland that received Presidential Disaster Declarations for one or more of the covered disaster events. All project activities were required to be completed by August 2019.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $20 million in CDBG-DR funds distributed through five phases: Phase 1 ($7,578,000, approved May 23, 2014); Phase 2 ($2,350,000, approved December 22, 2015); Phase 3 ($4,872,000, approved February 22, 2016); Phase 4 ($745,000, approved March 31, 2017); Phase 5 ($4,455,000, approved August 4, 2017). At least 80% ($16M) directed to Somerset County. 50% of total award must benefit low and moderate income persons. Eligible projects include infrastructure flood protection, housing activities, economic development, public facilities, public services, blight removal, and planning. Projects must meet at least one CDBG national objective. All activities completed by August 2019.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: All project activities must be completed by August 2019; phases approved by HUD between May 2014 and August 2017.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties and municipalities affected by Hurricane Sandy, Hurricane Irene, Tropical Storm Lee, or the Derecho; residents and entities in counties that received Presidential Disaster Declarations for these events; low and moderate income persons and households
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Necessary expenses related to disaster relief, long-term recovery, restoration of infrastructure and housing, and economic revitalization. Specific eligible activities include: infrastructure projects for flood protection (dikes, jetties, drainage improvements, dredging); public facilities (generators for shelters, water treatment plants, fire stations, county offices); housing activities (elevation, acquisition and demolition of properties in floodplains); economic development; public services; blight removal; planning and feasibility studies; wastewater system improvements. Projects must incorporate mitigation and resiliency measures and address floodplain management and sea level rise.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Counties with Presidential Disaster Declarations for Hurricane Sandy, Hurricane Irene, Tropical Storm Lee, or the Derecho. Hurricane Sandy: Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester. Hurricane Irene: Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester. Tropical Storm Lee: Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Cecil, Charles, Harford, Howard, and Prince George's. Derecho: Baltimore City, Calvert, Charles, Kent, Montgomery, and St. Mary's. At least 80% of funding directed to Somerset County.
requirements_list: Projects must be eligible under the CDBG Program
Projects must meet at least one CDBG national objective: benefit to low and moderate income persons, prevent or eliminate slums or blight, or meet an urgent need
50% of total award must benefit low and moderate income persons

For urgent need designation (Hurricane Sandy projects only), applicants must provide documentation demonstrating initial damage resulted from the storm and that no other funding is available in a timely manner
Applicants must comply with Citizen Participation Plan requirements
Applicants must conduct minimum of two public hearings prior to submission
Applicants must pass local resolution authorizing submission of application
Applicants must adopt and maintain Residential Anti-Displacement and Relocation Assistance Plan
Applicants must conduct comprehensive countywide needs assessment
Projects must incorporate mitigation and resiliency measures
Projects must address structural and environmental vulnerabilities related to flooding and/or sea level rise
Regional approaches to project planning were encouraged
All projects must be implemented within two-year grant agreement periods
All project activities must be completed by August 2019
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The State of Maryland solicited applications from county governments and Baltimore City. Counties were required to conduct comprehensive countywide needs assessments related to unmet recovery needs. Counties had to include projects from municipalities and could include projects on behalf of subrecipients, housing developers, or businesses. The application process included: (1) Adoption of current Citizen Participation Plan; (2) Conduct minimum of two public hearings - first hearing initiated needs assessment process with notice published 5+ days prior; second hearing held prior to application submission sharing findings and project list; (3) Passage of local resolution authorizing application; (4) Adoption of current Residential Anti-Displacement and Relocation Assistance Plan; (5) Submission of comprehensive needs assessment addressing impact and recovery needs. State reviewed and rated projects on 150-point scale considering: Benefit (75 points) - infrastructure flood protection projects prioritized highest; Readiness to Proceed (50 points); Leveraging (25 points). State submitted Action Plan to HUD for 30-day public comment, then submitted amendment to HUD for approval. Projects implemented through multiple grant agreement phases with specific timelines and spending requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery Assistance - Hurricane Sandy Grant #1 ($8.6M, Somerset County)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal funding provided to Maryland in response to Hurricane Sandy (October 28, 2012) to support recovery activities in Somerset County. The State was awarded $8.6 million through the Disaster Relief Appropriations Act from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development for housing and economic recovery activities. Funds were distributed across three phases: Phase 1 ($4.4 million) for housing recovery, economic recovery, and state administrative costs; Phase 2 ($1.1 million) for a countywide housing study and Housing Authority of Crisfield repairs; Phase 3 ($3.14 million) for housing recovery, economic recovery, public services/job training, and state administrative costs. All funds restricted to Somerset County, which experienced the most significant Sandy impact including 927 impacted housing units, mandatory evacuations in Crisfield and Smith Island, and a seven-foot storm surge.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $8.6 million in CDBG-DR funds distributed across three phases: Phase 1 ($4.4M): housing recovery program ($3.15M), economic recovery program ($1.05M), state administrative costs ($200K). Phase 2 ($1.1M): countywide housing study ($100K), Housing Authority of Crisfield repairs ($1M). Phase 3 ($3.14M): housing recovery ($2.68M), economic recovery ($160K), public services/job training ($100K), state administrative costs ($200K). Housing assistance provided as deferred loans repayable upon sale or transfer of property. Economic recovery provided through grants and loans to businesses. Expenditure deadline was October 1, 2022.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1, 2022 (expenditure deadline for remaining funds)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents and entities in Somerset County affected by Hurricane Sandy, including homeowners, renters, businesses, and public housing residents with unmet recovery needs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing recovery activities including rehabilitation, replacement, and elevation of damaged homes; economic recovery through business loans and grants; public services including job training; infrastructure improvements including broadband extension, dredging, generators, and strategic economic analysis; state administrative costs. All funds must be used for recovery activities in Somerset County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All $8.6 million must be used for recovery activities in Somerset County, which experienced the most significant impact from Hurricane Sandy with 927 impacted housing units, mandatory evacuations in Crisfield and Smith Island, and seven-foot storm surge from Chesapeake Bay.
requirements_list: Applicant household income cannot exceed 80% of area median income for Somerset County as determined by HUD for housing assistance
Proof of hurricane damage required
Proof of homeownership or business ownership required
Housing assistance recipients required to obtain minimum 8 hours of housing counseling from HUD-approved housing counseling agency
For housing assistance, homebuyers mortgages must be for fixed rate minimum 30 years
Homebuyers cannot acquire subprime or adjustable rate mortgages
Must use PART 5 income calculation process for income qualification
Housing assisted with CDBG funding must be brought up to livability code
All activities must include mitigation and resiliency measures to protect against future hazards
Public Housing Authority must carry sufficient insurance and flood insurance on all units and improvements assisted with CDBG funding in perpetuity
No duplication of benefits - unmet need calculated after accounting for insurance proceeds, FEMA assistance, SBA loans, and other funding sources
Applications processed on first come/first served basis regardless of race, national origin or protected class status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants for housing recovery assistance apply through Somerset County Department of Technical and Community Services. County staff conduct damage assessments and income verification. Housing assistance provided as deferred loans with repayment upon sale or transfer of property. Economic recovery assistance administered through Somerset County Economic Development Commission providing business loans and grants. Public services and job training coordinated through Somerset County Board of Education and other entities. County responsible for procurement, payment, inspections and approval of all required work. Planning and feasibility studies conducted by qualified consultants hired by the County. Broadband and infrastructure projects managed through County technical services department.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides funding to help strengthen Maryland's communities by expanding affordable housing opportunities, creating jobs, stabilizing neighborhoods, and improving overall quality of life. Funds support housing, public facilities, and economic development projects. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development and provides public funds for activities that meet at least one of three national objectives: benefit persons of low and moderate income, eliminate slum and blight, or address urgent community needs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funds are provided annually to non-entitlement counties and small cities through two funding categories: Community Development (competitive, applications accepted once per year with awards based on a competitive rating process) and Special Projects (planning, economic development, and special projects, applications accepted year-round on a first-come, first-served basis after written approval). For State Fiscal Year 2026, the State received $7,416,560 allocated as follows: State Administration (2% + $100,000) = $248,331; Technical Assistance (1%) = $74,165; Community Development (82% - $100,000) = $6,000,000; and Special Projects (15%) = $1,094,064. Funds serve as gap funding for projects selected by jurisdictions. Eligible subrecipients include governmental agencies, non-profit organizations with 501(c)(3) status, for-profit businesses in good standing for economic development projects, Community Based Development Organizations (CBDOs), and Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) certified by the State HOME Program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Community Development applications accepted once per year; Special Projects applications can be submitted at any time after written approval
structured_extraction.program_audience: Units of general local government in non-entitlement counties with populations less than 200,000 and non-entitlement cities and towns with populations less than 50,000. Multiple jurisdictions may jointly apply. Other public or private entities may be sub-recipients of eligible local government.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects must be eligible activities under program regulations and meet one of three national objectives: benefit persons of low and moderate income, eliminate slum and blight, or address an urgent need of recent origin threatening public health and safety. Eligible projects include: acquisition of real property; public works facilities (water/sewer, streets, childcare centers, senior or community centers, shelters); code enforcement; demolition and rehabilitation of buildings; ADA accessibility improvements; public services; relocation assistance; planning; housing activities including new construction, rehabilitation, renovation and resale, downpayment assistance, and housing counseling; economic development projects; and energy conservation initiatives. Over a three-year period, the state must cumulatively use 70% of funds to benefit persons of low and moderate income. Housing-specific requirements include: maximum CDBG funding of $200,000 per house for acquisition and renovation projects; affordable rent standards tied to HUD Fair Market Rents with affordability terms of 10-20 years depending on funding amount; homeownership assistance requires liens of 5-10 years depending on assistance amount; housing rehabilitation programs limited to county governments; and broadband infrastructure required for multi-family rental housing with more than 4 units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Non-entitlement counties with populations less than 200,000 and non-entitlement cities and towns with populations less than 50,000. Ineligible: Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties; Annapolis, Baltimore, Bowie, Cumberland, Frederick, Gaithersburg, Hagerstown, and Salisbury cities. Eligible jurisdictions are listed in the attachment document 'List of Eligible State Non-Entitlement CDBG Jurisdictions.' Project locations must be in a Maryland Priority Funding Area, except for public services, single family housing rehabilitation, acquisition/renovation/sale of existing houses, downpayment assistance, or where the Secretary of DHCD determines an exception is warranted.
requirements_list: Unit of general local government located in non-entitlement county or city
Population under 200,000 for counties or under 50,000 for cities
Projects must be for eligible activities under Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974
Projects must meet one of three national objectives: benefit low/moderate income persons, eliminate slum and blight, or meet urgent need
Proposed subrecipient or business must be eligible
For housing rehabilitation: limited to county governments except for active municipal programs or where county administers
For construction projects over $200,000 with HUD funding: Section 3 requirements apply (25% of labor hours by Section 3 workers, minimum 5% by Targeted Section 3 Workers)
For multi-family rental housing or government facilities: generators required with capacity for lighting in common areas
For projects involving construction or substantial rehabilitation of buildings with more than 4 rental units: broadband infrastructure required
Build America, Buy America (BABA) requirements apply to infrastructure projects unless under $250,000 or housing rehabilitation under $250,000 per house
Environmental review required; no activities begin until Release of Funds issued
Compliance with National Environmental Policy Act, Uniform Relocation Act, Fair Housing, Equal Opportunity, and federal civil rights laws
Single Audit required if grantee spends over $750,000 in federal funds in a fiscal year
Written Conflict of Interest Policy required
Citizen Participation Plan required
Public hearings required for grant applications
Anti-Displacement and Relocation Assistance Plan required
Over three-year period, minimum 70% of funds must benefit low and moderate income persons
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The State notifies eligible localities of fund availability and conducts training sessions. For Community Development funding: applicants submit applications through a competitive process once each year; applications are rated based on established criteria and compared to other applications; awards are determined through the competitive selection process. For Special Projects funding: applicants submit applications at any time after receiving written approval from CDBG program staff; awards are made on a first-come, first-served basis. All applicants must submit a local resolution, citizen participation plan, public hearing notices, and certifications regarding debarment and suspension. For projects meeting the urgent need national objective, applicants must contact CDBG program staff to determine eligibility before submitting an application. Planning applications and project applications require submission of required exhibits and documentation as specified in the CDBG Program Policies and Procedures Manual.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that provides targeted investments in the physical environment to improve the livability and economic potential of Maryland communities, with a focus on health and safety.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants to improve community health, safety, livability, and economic potential through investments in the physical environment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Closed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Physical environment improvements that impact health and safety in communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are currently closed. Prospective applicants are encouraged to sign up for DHCD news and alerts to stay informed about future application periods.

structured_extraction.program_description: Awards tax credit allocations to 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations to help attract charitable contributions from individuals and businesses for approved community projects and services. Donors who contribute $500 or more receive Maryland state tax credits equal to 50% of their contribution value (money, goods, or real estate).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The CITC program awards up to $1.75 million annually in Maryland state income tax credits. The maximum award request is $50,000 in tax credits. Donors making contributions of $500 or more to qualified nonprofit projects receive tax credits equal to 50% of the contribution value (money, goods, or real estate). Organizations must raise double the amount of tax credits requested (e.g., $100,000 in donations to receive $50,000 in credits). Tax credits reduce Maryland tax liability for the year the contribution was made and cannot be used retroactively. Credits are in addition to federal and state charitable contribution deductions. All CITC award contracts have a 24-month life. For FY26 awards, the contract period runs from January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2027. Tax credits are issued to donors electronically by the organization after receiving eligible gifts. Organizations must submit Tax Credit Certification Requests within 30 days of receiving each donation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 19, 2025 at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: IRS designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations applying for tax credit allocations. Individuals and businesses making charitable donations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects must support initiatives in or serving Priority Funding Areas. Eligible project expenses include staff costs, rent, utilities, program supplies, training, travel, and construction soft costs (planning, design, engineering, permitting). Allowable project activities include education and youth services, housing and community development, job and self-sufficiency training, neighborhood and business district enhancement, arts and culture, historic preservation, economic development, tourism promotion, technical assistance and capacity building, and services for at-risk populations. Projects may be capital projects, operating projects, or a combination of both.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA) as shown on the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper. For capital projects, the primary project site must be located within a PFA boundary. For operating projects, organizations must document that clients served reside within a PFA and maintain records of the total number and percentage of clients residing in designated PFA areas. Priority consideration given to ENOUGH areas and Just Communities.
requirements_list: Applicant must be IRS designated 501(c)(3) organization with current IRS 501(c)(3) Determination Letter
Organization must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Organization must be registered as a charity with the Office of the Maryland Secretary of State or hold a religious exemption
Project must be located in or serve Priority Funding Area (PFA)
Donors must contribute $500 or more
Donors must have personal tax liability in Maryland (individuals) or conduct trade or business in Maryland and be subject to state income tax (businesses)
For capital projects, organization must demonstrate site control via deed, lease with owner permission to alter property, real estate settlement documents, or similar evidence
Organization must maintain current charitable registration and good standing status throughout award period
Organization must complete and submit Tax Credit Certification Requests within 30 days of receiving eligible donations
Organization must submit four Semi-Annual Reports during the two-year award period (due July 10 and January 10)
Organization must maintain records related to CITC award for seven years following award completion
Real property donations require prior contact with nonprofit
Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws must be current and in force at time of application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations must register as users in the Department's IGX DHCD Project Portal at https://dhcd.maryland.gov/Communities/Pages/programs/CITC.aspx. New users should click 'New User? Register Here' and complete the registration form, noting interest in the FY26 CITC application round. Registration may take up to 72 hours for approval. Before creating an application, organizations must complete all Organization Uploads including Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, IRS 501(c)(3) Determination Letter, list of current Board of Directors and Officers, current Charitable Registration or Exemption Letter from Maryland Secretary of State, and current SDAT Good Standing status screenshot. Applications are submitted online through the portal during the designated application period (May 19 - June 19, 2025). Applications must include a completed Priority Funding Area (PFA) map for each address where project work will occur, created using the Department's Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper 4.0. For capital projects, documentation of site control must be provided. All applications require an executed Corporate Resolution, tasks and timeline table covering the entire 24-month award period (January 1, 2026 - December 31, 2027), detailed budget table, and budget narrative. Only fully completed applications with all required legal documents will be reviewed. Award announcements will be made in Fall 2025. Once awarded, organizations may not accept donations prior to January 1, 2026 or prior to the award agreement being fully executed, whichever occurs last.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides local governments and community development organizations with capital project funding for essential projects aimed at strengthening communities through activities such as business retention and attraction, encouraging homeownership, and commercial revitalization. Funds support expenses associated with capital projects that result in lasting physical improvements with at least a 15-year shelf life, with preference for projects that connect to community Sustainable Community Action Plans. Projects may include mixed-use development, business retention and attraction initiatives, streetscape improvements, homeownership and home rehabilitation programs, façade improvements, and real estate acquisition including land banking and strategic demolition.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital project funding provided through competitive grant applications. Projects must be located within Sustainable Communities boundaries or in Opportunity Zones located in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties, and must contribute to outcomes in the community's Sustainable Communities Action Plan. Projects resulting in lasting physical improvements with at least a 15-year shelf life are prioritized. Eligible uses include upper story redevelopment for residential dwellings, commercial façade improvements, adaptive reuse of vacant buildings, neighborhood parks, arts and cultural amenities, small business incubators, community open space development, acquisition/rehabilitation of vacant residential properties, mixed-use development with residential/commercial/open space components, streetscape improvements, homeownership increases and home rehabilitation, and real estate acquisition including land banking and strategic demolition. The FY26 Application Round is closed; check the program page for future rounds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY26 Application Round is closed; check program page for future rounds
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and non-profit community development organizations including county councils, community development corporations, main street organizations, and downtown partnerships seeking to revitalize commercial and residential districts within designated Sustainable Communities areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects including upper story redevelopment for residential dwellings, commercial façade improvements, adaptive reuse of vacant buildings, neighborhood parks, arts and cultural amenities, small business incubators, community open space development, acquisition/rehabilitation of vacant residential properties, mixed-use development with residential/commercial/open space components, business retention and expansion, streetscape improvements, homeownership increases and home rehabilitation, residential and commercial façade improvements, and real estate acquisition including land banking and strategic demolition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Community Legacy funding can only be used in Sustainable Communities areas or in Opportunity Zones located in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine specific geographic eligibility. Projects must be located within the boundaries of a Sustainable Community and help achieve outcomes identified in that community's Sustainable Communities Action Plan.
requirements_list: Project must be located in a Sustainable Community or an Opportunity Zone in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico Counties
Project should capitalize on community strengths while addressing revitalization challenges
Project should help achieve the local government's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Project should aim to stabilize a community, reverse decline, or encourage sustainable growth
Projects must result in lasting physical improvements with at least a 15-year shelf life
Applications submitted through the Project Portal after organization registration
Applicants must upload required organizational documents before applying
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Project Portal after organization registration. The typical timeline includes training, application opening, organization registration cutoff, application closing, review period, and award announcement. Applicants must upload required organizational documents before applying. For more information and application instructions, refer to the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Schools Rental Assistance Program (CSRAP) provides emergency financial support to families and students enrolled in community schools who are struggling with rent, facing eviction, or experiencing homelessness. The program helps eligible households secure stable housing and avoid homelessness by offering assistance with past due rent, utility bills, moving costs, deposits, and future rent and utility payments. Available in participating jurisdictions across Maryland, the program is administered through local nonprofit organizations, government agencies, and quasi public-private organizations.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CSRAP provides financial assistance to pay past due rent or utility bills including late fees and court fees related to eviction; moving costs and deposits needed to rent a new home such as security deposit, first month's rent, or utility deposit; and future rent and utility assistance related to current housing instability. Eligible households may receive up to 3 months of prospective rent and/or utility assistance at a time, with a maximum total assistance period of 15 months per household. Assistance is provided based on need and availability of funds through local providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and students enrolled in community schools who are experiencing housing instability, homelessness, at risk of eviction, or behind on rent or utility payments. Households must have at least one student currently enrolled in a community school in a participating jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Past due rent or utility bills including late fees and court fees related to eviction; moving costs and deposits needed to rent a new home such as security deposit, first month's rent, utility deposit, and application fees; future rent and utility assistance related to current housing instability; and relocation costs for households living place-to-place or in emergency shelters.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Frederick County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Washington County, and Wicomico County. Funding is nearly exhausted in all jurisdictions - most locations are interest-only or waitlist-only.
requirements_list: Have at least one student enrolled in a Community School living in your home
Have the student enrolled in one of the participating jurisdictions
Be renting your home or trying to rent a new home (homeowners are not eligible)
Be experiencing housing instability such as homelessness, at risk of eviction, utility shut off, or be behind in paying rent or utilities
Be responsible for paying rent or utilities in a qualifying rental unit
Provide proof of student's community school enrollment, proof of rental agreement, and invoice or proof of missed rent or utility payments. Proof of citizenship is not required.
Eligible households may receive repeat assistance contingent on availability of program funds and qualifying circumstances, up to a maximum of 15 months total per household
Households receiving prospective assistance must recertify eligibility every 3 months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the local nonprofit organization, government agency, or quasi public-private organization serving your county. Applications can be obtained from the local agency supporting your county or accessed online. If unable to complete the application online, contact the agency to request a paper copy. Each jurisdiction has its own local application process. Contact your local provider or the state office for specific application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide anti-poverty program that provides funds to seventeen Community Action Agencies across Maryland. These agencies use the money to offer a range of direct services that help low-income individuals and families achieve self-sufficiency, addressing the causes and conditions of poverty in each agency's service area.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Community Action Agencies receive 90 percent of federal funds allocated to Maryland to operate programs and services. The state may utilize 5 percent of the federal allocation as discretionary funding to support activities and programs conducted by Community Action Agencies or other non-profit organizations. An additional 2 percent may be used for training and technical assistance. Funds may support direct services to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization; training and technical assistance; and coordination among Community Action Agencies. For FFY 2025-2026, total planned allocation to eligible entities is $9,786,612.00 per year (93% of total CSBG funds).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The FY25 application round is closed. Check this page for information about future funding rounds.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Angela Fraser, Assistant Director, Division of Homeless Solutions
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals and families seeking assistance with self-sufficiency. Community Action Agencies, non-profit organizations, and units of local government serving individuals and families at or below 200 percent of poverty.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct services to help low-income individuals and families achieve self-sufficiency, including programs for employment, education, housing, and health. Activities and programs conducted by Community Action Agencies or other non-profit organizations to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization. Training and technical assistance. Coordination and communication among Community Action Agencies. Programs must address the causes and conditions of poverty in each agency's service area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All twenty-three Maryland counties and Baltimore City. Seventeen Community Action Agencies serve every jurisdiction in Maryland. See attachment for specific agency contact information by county.
requirements_list: Community Action Agencies must have a board of directors in which one-third are elected public officials currently holding office or their designees
At least one-third of the board must be chosen by a democratic selection method designed to assure they represent low-income persons in the community
The remainder of the board must be officials or members of business, industry, labor, religious, welfare, education, or other major groups and interests in the community
Services target individuals and households with incomes at or below 200 percent of federal poverty guidelines
Proposed programs must display measurable outcomes that help families and individuals move toward self-sufficiency
Eligible entities must meet COE CSBG Organizational Standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Pursuant to the federal CSBG Act, the Department utilizes federal funds allocated to Maryland. Applications are accepted in periodic funding rounds. The state's allocation formula uses FFY20 as a base and adjusts individual awards based on poverty, unemployment data, and whether the agency serves a rural community. Poverty and unemployment data are updated every two years in conjunction with development of a new CSBG State Plan. Contact the Division of Homeless Solutions for information about current application opportunities. Community Action Agencies seeking to apply should contact the appropriate CAA serving their area or the state CSBG point of contact.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to local governments, community-based organizations, non-profits, and anchor institutions to create or upgrade computer labs and centers providing public internet and device access for vulnerable populations.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $65,000 covering up to 100% of costs for creation, upgrade, and retrofit of computer labs and centers. Internet service subscription costs are funded for up to 3 years, with a maximum of $10,000 for internet subscription. Majority (50% or higher) of those served must be individuals with disabilities, unhoused individuals, veterans, or incarcerated and returning citizens. Two million dollars is available. Funding source is the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (ARPA State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds). Eligible uses include computer equipment (desktops, laptops, keyboards, mice, monitors, webcams, headphones, microphones), networking equipment (routers, switches, cables, Wi-Fi access points, firewalls), internet service subscription, marketing and outreach (up to 10% of budget), operational expenses (up to 15% of budget including staff salaries and general maintenance), administrative expenses (up to 15% of budget including training and security monitoring), software (operating systems, office productivity suites, educational software, antivirus protection), audiovisual equipment (projectors, screens, smartboards for training, speakers), and assistive technology (screen readers, magnifiers, adaptive keyboards, accessibility features). Ineligible uses include routine operational costs (utilities, rent), building construction or renovation, furniture (desks, chairs, ergonomic accessories), printers and photocopiers, Wi-Fi hotspots, entertainment items, personal devices, travel and hospitality, and duplicative projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications deadline extended to November 29, 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, incorporated municipalities, local government agencies, non-profit organizations, and community anchor institutions creating computer access for vulnerable populations including individuals with disabilities, unhoused individuals, veterans, and incarcerated and returning citizens.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creation, upgrade, and retrofit of computer labs and centers providing public internet and device access. Funds may be used for computer equipment (desktops, laptops, peripherals), networking equipment, internet service subscriptions (up to 3 years), marketing and outreach, operational expenses, administrative expenses, software, audiovisual equipment, and assistive technology.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local jurisdiction, incorporated municipality, local government agency delegated by Maryland jurisdiction, not-for-profit IRS-approved 501(c) entity providing services in Maryland, or community anchor institution within Maryland
Majority (50% or higher) of those served must be individuals with disabilities, unhoused/homeless individuals, veterans, or incarcerated/returning citizens
Grant maximum: $65,000 per application for computer equipment; Internet service subscription maximum: $10,000
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2026
Applicant must provide proof of non-profit status (501(c) documents) or local jurisdiction documentation
Applicant must provide Federal EIN Number and UEI (SAM.gov) Number
Applicant must provide Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Majority of computer lab population served must fall into at least one covered population category
All federal rules regarding ARPA funding must be adhered to by applicant
Applicant must comply with all grant terms including reporting requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible organizations submit complete grant applications by 11:59 PM ET on November 29, 2024. Applications may be submitted electronically via email to osb.de@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Computer Labs Program Application – [Organizational Applicant name]', or submitted by mail/hand delivery to Ronnie Hammond, Office of Statewide Broadband, Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Paper applications must show proof of mailing via USPS postmark, USPS mail receipt, or commercial carrier receipt dated on or before the deadline. Hand-delivered applications accepted 8:00 AM-4:00 PM ET Monday-Friday (excluding holidays). All files except those with specific format requirements should be converted to PDF. Applications must include: completed application form (with original signatures for paper submissions), executive summary and scope of work with timeline, project budget with itemized breakdown by category (operations, contracted services, travel), Federal W-9 form, 501(c) documents (for nonprofits), and Certificate of Good Standing (if applicable). Technical assistance available prior to November 22, 2024. The OSB intends to award funds beginning in December 2024. Successful applicants will be chosen based on qualifications and evaluation of responses, and may be subject to possible interview. All awardees must execute a Memorandum of Understanding outlining obligations of awardee and State to the project.

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY23 Network Infrastructure Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to local jurisdictions or their internet service provider partners to construct new broadband networks serving unserved households in Maryland. The program utilizes $95 million in Federal Coronavirus Capital Projects Funding from the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) to support broadband infrastructure expansion into unserved areas. Program is now closed.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of 70% to 90% of capital construction costs for major broadband infrastructure projects, with matching fund requirements of 10% to 30% depending on project density. For wired infrastructure, match percentages are determined by premise density per mile: fewer than 8 premises per mile = 10% match; 8-14 premises per mile = 20% match; 15+ premises per mile = 30% match. For wireless infrastructure, match is determined by premises per tower: fewer than 40 premises per tower = 10% match; 40-69 premises per tower = 20% match; 70+ premises per tower = 30% match. Grant range: $800,000 to $4,500,000. Matching funds must be in cash and cannot be used for operational costs. Eligible uses include outside plant construction (last mile and middle mile), electronic equipment (cabinets, switches, routers, wireless radios, antennas), customer drops, customer premises equipment, tower construction/upgrades (when treated as match), and engineering costs tied to funded capital assets. Ineligible uses include operating expenses, land and building purchases, tower purchases or leases, customer devices, bandwidth/spectrum costs, and costs incurred prior to application submission.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 5, 2022 at 11:59pm ET
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and their internet service provider partners building broadband networks to serve unserved areas. Eligible applicants include Maryland local jurisdictions, incorporated organizations recognized as partners by local jurisdictions, cooperatives legally formed in Maryland, limited liability companies, and other legal entities organized on a for-profit or non-profit basis that are recognized as partners by local jurisdictions. Individuals and partnerships are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband networks serving unserved homes and businesses, including: outside plant (fiber, coaxial, copper infrastructure for both last mile and middle mile), electronic equipment (cabinets, switches, routers, wireless radios, antennas, equipment shelters), customer drops (fiber to premises), customer premises equipment (ONTs, CPE), tower construction and structural improvements (when treated as match), and engineering costs directly tied to funded capital assets. Network must be capable of delivering minimum 100 Mbps downstream/100 Mbps upstream with 50 millisecond latency maximum (or 100 Mbps down/20 Mbps up if scalable to symmetrical speeds under specific geographic/topographic circumstances).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; areas receiving past state grant funding are ineligible for additional funding. Proposed Funded Service Area (PFSA) must be entirely within an eligible area with no existing broadband service. Areas with Broadband Service (defined as 100 Mbps downstream/20 Mbps upstream minimum) are ineligible. PFSA need not be contiguous but all premises within must be offered service at Broadband Grant Speed.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction, incorporated organization recognized as a local jurisdiction partner, cooperative legally formed in Maryland, limited liability company, or other legal entity (for-profit or non-profit) recognized as a partner by a local jurisdiction
Individuals and partnerships are not eligible applicants
Project must serve entirely unserved areas where broadband service does not currently exist, verified by OSB prior to award
All premises within the Proposed Funded Service Area (PFSA) must be offered service at Broadband Grant Speed (100 Mbps down/100 Mbps up, or 100 Mbps down/20 Mbps up if scalable)
Areas with past state grant funding are ineligible for additional funding
Grant request range: $800,000 to $4,500,000
Match requirement: 10% to 30% of eligible capital construction costs, determined by density calculation (wired: premises per mile; wireless: premises per tower)
Matching funds must be available as cash at time of award; cannot be used for operational costs except in specific circumstances
Applicant must have legal capacity and authority to own and operate broadband facilities, enter into contracts, and comply with applicable federal and state statutes and regulations
Project must comply with all ARPA requirements and federal rules regarding Coronavirus Capital Projects Funding
Applicant must obtain all necessary federal, state, and local approvals, permits, and licenses prior to project commencement
Applicant must not have been debarred by any federal, state, or local government entity in past four years
Applicant must not be subject to civil claims for non-payment with potential value of $30,000 or more
If incorporated, must be in good standing with State of Maryland, have filed required annual reports and fees, and paid all required taxes
Applicant must have Unique Entity ID from SAM.gov
Project must commence by September 1, 2023 and be completed by August 31, 2026
At least 50% of grant funds must be expended by second anniversary of effective date
All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated
Costs incurred before application submission are not eligible for reimbursement
Grant funds cannot supplant other federal funding; may only supplement previously awarded federal funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted by December 5, 2022 at 11:59pm ET via one of three methods: (1) Postmarked or shipped paper copy with original signatures accompanied by electronic version on USB Flash Drive to Kenrick M. Gordon, P.E., Director OSB, DHCD, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706; (2) Emailed as zipped files to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Network Infrastructure Grant Application – your company name'; (3) Paper applications must show proof of mailing via USPS postmark, mail receipt, or dated shipping label from commercial carrier. Applications submitted after deadline will not be considered. Required components include: completed Broadband Grant Application Form (Schedule A-1), IRS Form W-9, evidence of legal existence and good standing, jurisdictional partnership documentation (if applicable), Executive Summary, Scoring Criteria documentation, System Design with network diagram, Service Area Demographics and map, Scope of Work including construction milestones and project budget, Financial Information including historical and pro forma statements (Schedule G-1), Statement of Experience, Evidence of funding commitments (Exhibit D), and Project Budget (Schedule F-2). Prior to submission, applicants could request technical assistance from OSB before November 18, 2022. Once approved, applicant must enter into grant agreement with Department, with funds disbursed on reimbursement basis. Applicant must submit interim progress reports quarterly and final report within 45 days of project completion.

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY24 Network Infrastructure Grant Program – Smith Island
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants specifically for constructing new broadband networks to serve unserved households on Smith Island, Maryland. The program provides financial assistance to construct broadband infrastructure necessary to provide service at the Broadband Grant Speed (100 Mbps download/100 Mbps upload) to all residents, businesses, and anchor institutions on the island where broadband service does not currently exist.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $3,000,000 covering up to 90% of capital construction costs for broadband network development on Smith Island. Minimum grant request of $1,000,000. Match requirement of at least 10% of total construction costs (11.11% of the grant amount). Match must be in cash and available upon grant agreement execution. Eligible uses include construction of last mile and middle mile outside plant infrastructure, electronic equipment (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, wireless radios, antennas, equipment cabinets), customer drops, and related capital costs directly necessary to provide broadband service. Ineligible uses include tower purchases/leases, building purchases/renovations, operating expenses, and customer premise equipment beyond the ONT. Funding source is American Rescue Plan Act Capital Projects Fund. Grantees must expend at least 50% of grant funds by the second anniversary of the effective date and complete projects by August 31, 2027.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 11:59pm ET on January 31, 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland local jurisdictions, incorporated organizations recognized as partners by local jurisdictions, cooperatives, limited liability companies, and other for-profit or not-for-profit legal entities (excluding individuals and partnerships) building broadband networks on Smith Island to serve unserved households, businesses, and anchor institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband networks on Smith Island, including outside plant infrastructure (fiber optic cabling, conduits, poles), last mile and middle mile deployment, electronic equipment (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radios, antennas, equipment cabinets, shelters), customer drops, and other capital expenses directly necessary to provide broadband service at 100 Mbps download/100 Mbps upload speeds to all unserved premises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Smith Island, Somerset County, Maryland. The Identified Service Area (ISA) includes all locations on Smith Island as identified by latitude/longitude coordinates. Any proposed service area already receiving broadband service at 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload is ineligible.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local jurisdiction, incorporated organization recognized as a partner by the local jurisdiction, cooperative, limited liability company, or other legal entity (excluding individuals and partnerships) that is recognized as a partner by the local jurisdiction
Applicant must be in good standing with the State of Maryland and have legal capacity and authority to own and operate broadband facilities
Applicant must have a DUNS Number and Unique Entity ID from SAM.gov
Applicant must provide IRS Form W-9 and evidence of legal existence and good standing
Project must serve the entire Identified Service Area where broadband service does not currently exist

Project must be capable of providing minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum 50 millisecond latency, unless certified exemption is granted for geography/topography/excessive cost reasons
Project must serve all unserved premises and offer minimum connectivity or higher to all subscribers
Grant range: Minimum $1,000,000, Maximum $3,000,000
Match requirement: Minimum 10% of total construction costs (11.11% of grant amount) in cash available at grant agreement execution
All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated
Grantee must commence project by September 1, 2024
Grantee must complete project by August 31, 2027
Grantee must expend at least 50% of grant funds by second anniversary of effective date
Grantee must obtain all necessary federal, state, and local permits and approvals
Grantee must comply with federal American Rescue Plan Act requirements and Treasury regulations
Grantee must provide service data to state for broadband mapping purposes
Grantee must maintain records for five years following project completion
Grantee must provide interim progress reports quarterly and final report within 45 days of project completion
Grant funds cannot supplant other federal funding already awarded for broadband in the service area
In-kind contributions are not eligible as match; match must be cash from allowable sources
Applicant may not have been debarred by any federal, state, or local entity in past four years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted by 11:59pm ET on January 31, 2024 in one of the following ways: (1) Postmarked or shipped paper copy with original signatures accompanied by electronic version on USB Flash Drive to Kenrick M. Gordon, P.E., Director, OSB, Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706; or (2) Electronic submission via email to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Network Infrastructure Grant Application – Smith Island – [company name]'. All files should be converted to PDF unless otherwise specified. Paper applications must show proof of mailing (USPS postmark, dated mail receipt, or dated shipping label from commercial carrier). Completed applications must include: Broadband Grant Application Form (Schedule A-1), IRS Form W-9, evidence of legal existence and good standing, local jurisdiction partnership letter (if applicable), Executive Summary covering project description/needs/benefits, applicant qualifications, and system overview, Scoring Criteria Documentation, System Design with network diagram, Service Area Demographics, Scope of Work with construction milestones and project budget, Financial Information including historical and pro forma financial statements, Statement of Experience, and evidence of funding commitments. Technical assistance is available until January 19, 2024. Applications not meeting the deadline will not be considered. A sample grant agreement is available at https://dhcd.maryland.gov/broadband.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to local community-based organizations, non-profits, anchor institutions, and local governments to create gap networks and community networks that address internet affordability for low to moderate income households. The program aims to close the digital divide by ensuring affordable broadband access for covered populations including low to moderate income households, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, and members of racial or ethnic minority groups. Grants cover up to 100% of costs for construction, deployment, expansion, or continuation of community-based gap networks. Funding was provided through the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (ARPA). Program is now closed.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants ranging from $25,000 to $250,000 covering up to 100% of costs for construction, deployment, expansion, or continuation of community-based gap networks and community networks. Five million dollars was available for FY2022. Projects must provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps down and 100 Mbps up with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds at subscriber location, or 100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up if scalable to symmetrical 100 Mbps. Eligible uses include equipment, instrumentation, networking capability, hardware and software, digital network technology, optical line terminals, optical network terminals, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennas, access points, modems, equipment shelters, and operations/maintenance of networks. Funding source is the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (ARPA) Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted through March 31, 2022; application submission opened February 15, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities), non-profit organizations (501(c) entities), community-based anchor institutions, and other community-based organizations creating networks to address internet affordability for low to moderate income households and other covered populations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building and deploying new gap networks or community networks; upgrading or expanding existing gap networks or community networks; operating and maintaining new or existing gap networks or community networks. Eligible capital uses include equipment, instrumentation, networking capability, hardware and software, digital network technology, optical line terminals, optical network terminals, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennas, access points, modems, and equipment shelters. All projects must provide a minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Projects must be in areas identified as having a need for additional broadband investment, including areas lacking access to connections reliably meeting symmetrical 100 Mbps download and upload speeds, lacking affordable broadband access, or lacking reliable broadband. Applicants must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government, non-profit 501(c) entity, community-based anchor institution, or other community-based organization
Must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation

Project must address affordability challenges for covered populations including individuals with household income at or below 150% of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, or members of racial or ethnic minority groups
Grant range: $25,000 to $250,000

Projects must provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps down and 100 Mbps up with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds at subscriber location, or 100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up if scalable to symmetrical speeds
Project completion deadline: December 31, 2023
Applicants must provide W-9 form and Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
All awardees must execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining obligations
Projects funded through ARPA must comply with all federal rules and requirements
Applicants responsible for overall funding, implementation, and operation of the project

Submit a complete application with all required attachments including project summary, statement of experience, network design, community profile, subscriber cost information, potential barriers analysis, partners and local engagement plan, intended outcomes and metrics, schedule, and funding scope and budget
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were submitted via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov with subject line 'MD-GAPS: Name of Applying Organization' by March 31, 2022. Application submission opened February 15, 2022. Required components included applicant information, project information, estimated funding details, project summary addressing all required criteria, project budget, W-9 form, and Certificate of Good Standing. The Office of Statewide Broadband reviewed applications for completeness and eligibility. Successful applicants were chosen based on qualifications and evaluation of responses, with possible interviews. Funding announcements were scheduled for on or before April 15, 2022, with award notification and fund disbursement intended to begin in May 2022. All awardees must execute an MOU prior to receiving funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides internet-enabled devices to counties and municipal governments for distribution to eligible low-income households that lack necessary technology for internet access. The program distributes HP Chromebook 14 G7 or similar devices to qualifying households in Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of internet-enabled devices (HP Chromebook 14 G7 or similar) to counties and municipal governments for distribution to eligible households. Device specifications include minimum 13" screen, Chrome OS, SD card reader, dual band Wi-Fi, 2 USB ports, headphone and video output jacks, and one-year manufacturer's warranty. One device per address/MDU unit maximum. A $6 per device stipend is provided for distribution costs including secure storage, distribution venue costs, and personnel costs. Round one awarded 91,300 devices; round two provides remaining allotment to new eligible applicants with priority. All devices must be distributed within six months of first shipment delivery. Devices not distributed must be returned at awardee's cost.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for 2nd round accepted through September 29, 2023 by 11:59pm ET
structured_extraction.program_audience: Counties and municipal governments distributing devices to low-income households lacking internet access. Eligible distribution partners may include libraries, local education agencies, municipalities, 501(c)(3) nonprofit entities, and community-based anchor institutions working with local jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internet-enabled devices provided to eligible households; stipend available to support secure storage of devices, cost of distribution venue, and personnel costs associated with distribution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all Maryland counties and municipalities eligible. All requested devices will be delivered within five months of execution of Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Department, with maximum one shipment per month over a five-month period.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local jurisdiction (county or incorporated municipality) as recognized by the Maryland Manual On-Line website
Eligible household income must be at or below 200% of Federal Poverty Guidelines OR enrolled in federal Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP)

Households participating in government assistance programs qualify: SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance, Veterans Pension and Survivors Benefit, Free/Reduced-Price School Lunch Program or School Breakfast Program, or received Federal Pell Grant in current award year
One device per household address or recognized MDU (multi-dwelling unit) only
Applicant must be registered in System for Award Management (SAM) and provide valid unique entity identifier before submitting application
Applicant must provide Federal EIN Number and DUNS Number
Applicant must develop documented eligibility verification process for recipients
Applicant must ensure bulk shipment receiver has secure storage and loading/unloading capabilities for multiple shipments
Applicant must inspect devices upon receipt and notify OSB immediately of damaged products
Applicant must develop outreach program to inform eligible community of program terms and eligibility
Devices must be received at maximum rate of one shipment per month over five-month period with specified delivery schedule
Performance period is six months from delivery of first device shipment; all devices must be distributed by end of performance period
Applicant must use Department Device Tracking Portal for address verification during distribution to ensure no duplicate devices per household
Record keeping of distribution must be maintained; household-level data and verification documentation must be provided if requested
Municipal applicants must coordinate with county applicants to ensure complementary and non-conflicting distribution efforts
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: County or municipal governments apply for device allocations by submitting completed application form with required attachments. Applications accepted electronically via email to OSB.MD@maryland.gov or by USPS/shipping mail to Ronnie Hammond at DHCD office. Applications must be submitted or postmarked by September 29, 2023 at 11:59pm ET. Required application materials include: (1) completed application form with EIN, DUNS, and SAM.gov unique identifier; (2) written project narrative (including executive summary not exceeding 2 pages); (3) scope of work detailing partnerships, data collection, storage, distribution method, eligibility verification, and one-device-per-household methodology; (4) project schedule with milestones; (5) monthly device delivery request schedule; and (6) Federal Form W-9. Technical assistance available prior to September 22, 2023. OSB reviews applications for completeness and suitable distribution methodology and may coordinate with other State agencies to verify information. Successful applicants selected based on qualifications and evaluation of responses, with possible interview. Priority given to first-time applicants and jurisdictions that did not receive devices in Round 1. If requested devices exceed available supply, equal percentage reduction applied across all applications. Awardees must execute Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining obligations of awardee and State. No reimbursement provided for application development costs.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development makes single family properties available for purchase by homebuyers, non-profit organizations, and public housing authorities through real estate sales.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Properties are made available for purchase by eligible homebuyers, non-profit organizations, and public housing authorities. The properties are listed and sold through contract real estate agencies: Homesource Real Estate Solutions or Atlantic Auctions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homebuyers, non-profit organizations, and public housing authorities seeking to purchase single family properties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of single family properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Properties are listed and sold through two contract real estate agencies: Homesource Real Estate Solutions or Atlantic Auctions. Interested purchasers can view available properties through these agencies.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to local jurisdictions, non-profit organizations, and community-based anchor institutions to support digital inclusion planning and implementation projects that increase digital access and skills across Maryland. The program addresses the digital divide by enhancing internet access, implementing digital literacy programs, and expanding digital opportunities. It supports both the development of digital inclusion plans and the implementation of digital inclusion activities, training programs, and public access computing centers, facilitating broadband adoption for educational and employment opportunities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two funding tracks: (1) Digital Inclusion Planning grants provide up to 50% of planning costs with a minimum of $5,000 and maximum of $30,000 per application; (2) Digital Inclusion Implementation grants provide up to 100% of implementation costs with a minimum of $10,000 and maximum of $75,000 per application. Grant amounts may be reduced based on applicant impact and ability to deploy funds responsibly. Two million dollars is available total for FY2022. Funding source is the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA), Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds administered by the US Treasury. Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023. Budget categories may include: Operations (payroll, supplies, materials), Contracted Services (payments to independent contractors or external organizations), Travel (related to program deployment), and Equipment (such as computers/devices).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are due on or before Thursday, March 31, 2022
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ronnie Hammond / Office of Statewide Broadband
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (counties and municipalities), non-profit 501(c) organizations, foundations, corporations, institutions, associations, coalitions, and community-based anchor institutions providing services in Maryland. Priority populations include individuals with household income at or below 150% of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers or low literacy, racial or ethnic minorities, and individuals in rural areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Digital Inclusion Planning: Development of Digital Inclusion Plans. Digital Inclusion Programming: Implementation of digital inclusion activities including enhancing understanding of internet service, assisting households with internet service applications, providing digital skills training, enhancing access to jurisdiction services and educational opportunities, researching populations with low adoption rates, constructing or operating public access computing centers, implementing training programs (basic, advanced, and applied skills) or workforce development programs, facilitating broadband adoption for educational and employment opportunities, and other qualifying digital inclusion or equity goals. Cannot be used for construction of broadband infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All communities in Maryland are eligible, with priority given to covered populations most in need.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government (County or Municipality), a foundation/corporation/institution/association/coalition that is a 501(c) entity providing services in Maryland, or a community-based anchor institution
Planning track: minimum $5,000 and maximum $30,000 request
Implementation track: minimum $10,000 and maximum $75,000 request
Application must be completed in its entirety with all required attachments
Must submit: Executive summary, Project budget, and Federal Form W-9
Include executive summary with project overview, population needs, potential barriers, partners, local engagement, intended outcomes and metrics, and statement of experience and past accomplishments
Provide IRS Determination Letter of nonprofit status if applicable
Submit online verification of Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Provide Dun & Bradstreet DUNS Number for organization
All awardees must execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining obligations
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023
Applicant must demonstrate capability and experience related to proposed project
Must provide a scope of work specific to the funding requested
Must identify partnerships and community engagement
Must define intended outcomes and success metrics
Compliance with all ARPA federal requirements is mandatory
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete the FY22 Digital Inclusion Grant Program Application Form in its entirety, including: Applicant Information (legal name, EIN, DUNS number, address), Contact Information, Project Information (funding amounts from various sources, project use category), and Other Required Information. Required attachments include: Executive summary of the project, Project budget showing costs in categories (Personnel, Fringe Benefits, Travel, Equipment, Supplies, Contracts, Other), Federal Form W-9, IRS Determination Letter of nonprofit status if applicable, and online verification of Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Applications and all correlating documents should be submitted via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov with subject line 'MD-DIG: Name of Applying Organization' by March 31, 2022. Only fully complete applications will be considered. The Office of Statewide Broadband will review applications for completeness and eligibility. Successful applicants will be selected based on qualifications, evaluation of responses, and possible interviews. Awards are intended to be distributed beginning in May 2022. Awardees will be required to execute an MOU with the State.
