structured_extraction.program_name: EmPOWER Maryland Limited Income Energy Efficiency Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps limited income households reduce energy use by installing energy efficiency materials and equipment at no charge. Homeowners receive an energy audit, recommended improvements are made by contractors, and a follow-up evaluation ensures the home operates more efficiently.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides energy efficiency upgrades at no charge to eligible homeowners. Services include a comprehensive energy audit to identify cost-saving opportunities, installation of materials and equipment such as attic and wall insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and tuning, refrigerator retrofit if applicable, and health and safety items. The program covers all work performed by licensed contractors at no cost to the homeowner. A follow-up evaluation ensures the home operates more efficiently after upgrades are completed. The program is administered by local agencies that schedule audits and coordinate contractor work.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Limited income homeowners who have a utility account with BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency upgrades including insulation in attics, floors and walls; hot water system improvements; lighting retrofits; furnace cleaning, tuning and safety repairs; refrigerator retrofit if applicable; and health and safety items.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for customers of participating utility companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas.
requirements_list: Household income must be at or below 250% of the federal poverty level based on household size (ranging from $72,950 for a single person to $165,050 for a household of ten or $13,750 more per additional person)
Must have a utility account with one of six participating utility companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas

Automatically income-eligible if currently receiving Utility Bill Pay Assistance through OHEP, SNAP, TANF, SSI, HUD housing assistance, Fuel Fund Assistance, DHCD Rehab Programs, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, Medicaid, MEA Energy Equity Grant, or MEEHA
Must own the home for renters, applicants must have landlord consent
Must have electricity service to the home
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can complete either a Quick Application (for those receiving eligible benefits) or a Standard Application with required documentation. Submit the completed application with all required documents to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Attn: Weatherization, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706, or call 1-855-583-8976. If currently approved for Energy Assistance payments from the Maryland Department of Human Services, contact the intake line at 1-855-583-8976. Once eligibility is determined, a local agency will schedule a home energy audit. After discussing audit results with the homeowner, a contractor will schedule and complete recommended work at no charge. A follow-up evaluation ensures the home operates more efficiently after work is completed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Net Zero Loan Program supports the construction of energy efficient homes that produce as much or more energy than they use. Eligible projects include new construction or deep energy retrofits of existing homes with a Home Energy Rating System (HERS) rating of 50 or lower. The program offers low interest construction loans and loan enhancements for private construction loans.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides low interest construction loans with interest rates ranging from 3% to 5% depending on the HERS score and whether more than 50% of residents are at or below 60% of Area Median Income. Rates are lower (2% to 4%) for projects where more than 50% are at or below 60% AMI. Closing fees include a 1% administration fee and $290 appraisal fee. Loan to value is up to 90%. The program also offers loan enhancements to applicants securing loans from private lenders. Construction period is typically 12 months with a 12 month loan repayment period for projects that are for sale. An additional fee may apply for loan funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: We are accepting applications until available funds are committed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners, builders, developers, or investors who are qualified to do business in Maryland and can demonstrate creditworthiness and repayment ability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction of new Net Zero homes or deep energy retrofits of existing homes that achieve a HERS rating of 50 or lower. Projects must be properly zoned for residential use and constructed or rehabilitated in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal building codes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Qualified to do business in Maryland
Have legal capacity and all necessary authorization to incur the loan obligation
Demonstrate creditworthiness and repayment ability acceptable to the department
Demonstrate the ability to complete the project
New construction or deep energy retrofit of existing home
Must reach low energy status with HERS rating of 50 or lower
Properly zoned for residential use
Must be constructed or rehabilitated in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal building codes
Provide organizational documents (Certificate of Good Standing, Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, Corporate Resolutions)
Provide financial statements
Provide evidence of ownership (Deed or Purchase Contract)
Provide zoning letter
Provide Property/Builder's Risk insurance with ACORD certificate noting DHCD as certificate holder and Mortgagee/Lender Loss Payable
Provide Borrower's Liability insurance with ACORD certificate noting DHCD as certificate holder and additional insured
Provide Flood Insurance proof that property is not in flood hazard area
Provide construction documents including Plans and Specifications, Budget, Draw Schedule, and Construction Schedule
Provide General Contractor's Liability Insurance (if different from Borrower)
Provide General Contractor's Certification
Provide Building Permits
Provide Home Energy Rating Score (HERS) Rating
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Energy Efficient Homes Construction Loan (Net Zero) Program paper application form. Gather and organize all required documentation including organizational documents, financial statements, evidence of ownership, insurance certifications, and construction documents as listed in the Required Documents checklist. Review the Required Documents list to ensure all necessary items are included. Submit the completed application and all supporting documents by email to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov with a copy to Thomas.Walz@maryland.gov. The Department may request additional documents during the underwriting process and applicants agree to submit these documents in a timely manner when requested.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY24 Home Stretch - Difficult to Serve Properties Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to county jurisdictions to help with costs of installing broadband service to remote properties and locations that internet service providers find difficult or uneconomical to serve. The program aims to connect unserved difficult-to-serve premises to existing broadband networks where geographic challenges or distance from infrastructure discourage ISP deployment.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $1,100,000 total provided to county jurisdictions to support sub-grant programs with internet service provider partners for broadband installation. Maximum of $8,000 per location funded. Funding is provided for capital construction costs related to deployment of internet facilities capable of delivering 100Mbps download and 100Mbps upload with maximum 50ms latency to individual difficult-to-serve premises (or 100Mbps download and 20Mbps upload with proper certification). Eligible costs include construction of service delivery facilities, equipment, and materials. Grant funds do not cover operating expenses, land purchase, tower construction, or telephone/video service expenses. A 25% cash match of eligible project costs is required from the jurisdiction, ISP partner, property owner, or combination thereof. Funding source is the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, Capital Projects Fund (Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 22, 2023
structured_extraction.program_audience: County jurisdictions developing sub-grant programs with internet service providers to serve difficult-to-reach properties. End user subscribers are responsible for ongoing internet subscription costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for broadband installation to remote or difficult-to-serve premises where geographic challenges discourage ISP deployment. Eligible uses include construction of service delivery facilities, minor extensions of ISP existing infrastructure, and electronics necessary to deliver service such as Optical Network Terminals (ONTs), routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, access points, and modems. All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated. For wireless technologies, eligible costs may include taller antenna masts, enhanced receiving equipment, or robust antenna arrays. Satellite receiving equipment for satellite providers meeting speed and latency requirements is also eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; distributed to county jurisdictions. Projects must connect unserved difficult-to-serve premises (those lacking terrestrial fixed internet service at speeds of 100 Mbps download and/or 20 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds) to existing broadband networks.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local county jurisdiction
Applicant must have entered into a partnership with one or more ISP partners prior to entering into a funding agreement
Applicant must identify the source of the required 25% cash match (can be from jurisdiction, ISP partner, property owner, or other sources such as foundations or non-profits)
Projects must connect unserved difficult-to-serve premises to existing broadband networks

Network must provide minimum 100Mbps download and 100Mbps upload with maximum 50ms latency, or with certification 100Mbps download and 20Mbps upload with maximum 50ms latency that is scalable to symmetrical 100Mbps speeds
All partnering ISPs must participate in the federal Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP)
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2025
Maximum grant per location: $8,000
Maximum grant per applicant: $1,100,000
Match requirement: 25% of eligible capital construction costs (cash only, no in-kind matches)

Applicant must develop a jurisdictional-specific funding program detailing how end users will be selected, assistance for low-income end users, ISP billing methods, acceptable ISP costs, ACP assistance, and ACP promotion
Applicant must provide an outreach component to promote the program
All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated
Applicant must identify any information considered proprietary or confidential
No duplication of existing broadband service or other state/local/federal funding for the same location permitted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: County jurisdictions must submit applications on or before December 22, 2023. Applications must include: (1) Complete Grant Application Form for FY24 Connect Maryland-Broadband for Difficult to Serve Premises Project; (2) Executive Summary describing unserved premises, selection criteria, current problems, and expected benefits; (3) Application Partnership section naming ISP partner(s) and describing cooperation; (4) Statement of experience from senior team members from both applicant and ISP partner; (5) Network Discussion describing ISP network technology, speed capabilities, and offerings; (6) Subscriber Profile with demographic data; (7) Subscriber Costs and Limitations including low/moderate options; (8) Budget estimate for capital construction costs; (9) Program Overview with details on user selection, low-income assistance, billing, ACP promotion; (10) Implementation schedule with key milestones assuming Spring 2024 start. Submit one electronic PDF copy combining all items into a single .zip file to osb.md@maryland.gov with subject line including 'Difficult to Serve Premises Grant Application' and local county jurisdiction name. If application exceeds email size limits, upload to cloud service and share link. Applications will be scored based on need for service, match contribution source and percentage, network delivery speed, and subscriber options, with awards made on a high-to-low score basis as funding permits. OSB intends to award funding in February 2024.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that evaluates the skills and determines the needs of families and individuals. The goal is to help Housing Voucher participants achieve higher education, improve employment status, and guide them onto a path of self-sufficiency through financial literacy, job training, childcare and other support services. The program is administered through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, with a dedicated service area at the Cambridge Community Engagement Center serving Dorchester County residents.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides comprehensive support including financial literacy, job training, childcare assistance, and other services to help Housing Voucher participants work toward self-sufficiency. All FSS participants are eligible for an interest-bearing escrow account where increased rent portions from earned income are credited. Participants who successfully complete the program receive all funds in the escrow account plus interest (tax-free). The contract is 5 years and can be extended for an additional 2 years with good cause. Participants may graduate early if they accomplish and complete all tasks and goals before the allotted time. The Cambridge Community Engagement Center serves participants in the Cambridge, Maryland area and the broader Cambridge service area.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Housing Voucher participants seeking to improve their employment status and education level, including disabled individuals who can designate another adult household member as head of household. Cambridge, Maryland area participants may contact the Cambridge Community Engagement Center at cec.dhcd@maryland.gov.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for pursuing higher education, job training, employment counseling, financial literacy, childcare, health services, homeownership, job retention, transportation, and other services to achieve self-sufficiency. Escrow funds can be used for down payment on a house or other purposes once contract is completed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide; the Cambridge Community Engagement Center specifically serves Cambridge, Maryland and the surrounding service area in Dorchester County.
requirements_list: Must be a Housing Voucher participant
Must be willing to set and work toward employment goals
Must aim to become free of TANF (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) benefits
Head of household must complete and submit application and sign Contract of Participation
Disabled individuals may participate if their goal is to obtain employment/earned income and be free of TANF benefits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DHCD at (410) 901-4080, email fss.dhcd@maryland.gov, visit dhcd.maryland.gov/CambridgeCEC, or ask your case manager at any meeting or redetermination. Complete an online form at dhcd.wufoo.com/forms/family-selfsufficiency-program. Cambridge area participants may also contact the Cambridge Community Engagement Center at cec.dhcd@maryland.gov or visit the center in person. You will meet with an FSS coordinator who will review and discuss your family's strengths, barriers, and goals. The applicant and program coordinator will complete a Needs Assessment outlining rights, goals, and responsibilities of both parties. An individual family plan will be created to meet your goals, including the two required long-term goals of obtaining employment and being free of temporary cash assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credit Program (LIHTC)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program that encourages private investment in the construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. The program awards tax credits on a competitive basis to qualified housing projects. Governed by Section 42 of the Internal Revenue Code and administered in Maryland by the Community Development Administration (CDA), a unit in the Division of Development Finance of the Department of Housing and Community Development.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits are awarded to for-profit and nonprofit sponsors of eligible housing projects on a competitive basis. The tax credit equals the applicable percentage of the qualified basis of each qualified low-income rental housing building. Project sponsors or their investor partners claim the tax credit on their federal income tax return. Ten percent of the state's annual allocation is set aside for nonprofit sponsors. The applicable percentage is determined at the time of allocation. Projects must remain in compliance for a minimum of 40 years following the end of the initial 15-year compliance period, with an extended use period of at least 15 additional years. During the initial 15-year compliance period, full federal tax implications apply to noncompliance. During the extended use period (years 16-30+), there may be no tax impact to the project owner in the event of noncompliance, though owners must continue to operate the project in accordance with the LIHTC Covenant and Allocation Plan requirements. Tax-exempt bonds may qualify projects for tax credits outside the competitive process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Portal opens May 16, 2025 through June 20, 2025 for calendar year 2024 end-of-year data uploads

structured_extraction.contact_email: taxcredits.dhcd@maryland.gov; For Extended Use Period: dca_mf.dhcd@maryland.gov
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit sponsors developing affordable rental housing projects for low- and moderate-income families. Developers, syndicators, property managers, and other entities involved in LIHTC project development and ongoing compliance. Eligible applicants include county governments, for-profit businesses, municipalities, and non-profit organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and rehabilitation of residential rental buildings that provide housing for low-income occupancy. The eligible basis includes acquisition, construction, and rehabilitation costs of residential rental buildings and certain common areas and facilities available on a comparable basis to all residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Projects must be placed in service in or within two years after the year in which the allocation is made. The program uses Qualified Census Tracts (QCTs) and Difficult Development Areas (DDAs) as criteria in the Qualified Allocation Plan.
requirements_list: Building must be a residential rental building

Owner must rent either 20 percent of units to households with incomes at 50 percent or less of area median income, or 40 percent of units to households with incomes at 60 percent or less of area median income (other set-asides available including 15-40 for deep rent-skewed and Income Averaging)
Building must comply with tenant income and maximum rent level requirements
Building must remain in compliance for a minimum of 40 years during the initial compliance period plus extended use period of at least 15 additional years
Owner must provide evidence of economic feasibility during application process
Owner's CPA must certify total costs for each building before IRS Form 8609 is issued
Owner must submit annual Owner's Certificate of Continuing Compliance during compliance period
Owner must maintain proper project files and resident files with required documentation
Project facilities included in eligible basis must be provided on comparable basis without separate charge to all tenants

Owner must notify CDA immediately of anticipated changes in ownership composition exceeding specified thresholds (25% for limited partnership/non-managing member interests; any change in general partner, managing member, or controlling interest)
Utility allowances must be updated at least once per calendar year

For units with 100% LIHTC coverage, exemption from annual tenant recertification available; other buildings may apply for recertification exemption after satisfactory initial inspection and zero outstanding noncompliance issues
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Projects are awarded tax credits on a competitive basis according to criteria outlined in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). Applications are reviewed and scored based on QAP selection criteria. Once approved, sponsors must complete a cost certification prepared by a CPA before IRS Form 8609 is issued. The owner completes and signs Part II of Form 8609 and submits to the IRS when filing personal, partnership, or corporate tax returns for the first year. A copy of the fully executed 8609 must be forwarded to CDA. For acquisition/rehabilitation projects, separate Form 8609s are issued for acquisition and rehabilitation credits. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible for tax credits outside the competitive process. After initial 15-year compliance period ends, monitoring transitions to the Division of Credit Assurance (DCA) with less frequent inspection requirements. Contact the program for additional information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides neutral mediation between homeowners and lenders when foreclosure proceedings have been initiated. A trained administrative law judge serves as a neutral third party to facilitate dialogue and help both sides reach a mutually acceptable solution.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides mediation services facilitated by a trained administrative law judge from the Maryland Office of Administrative Hearings. Homeowners must pay a non-refundable $50 fee to the Circuit Court to formally request mediation. Homeowners have 25 days from when the lender initiates foreclosure proceedings to submit their request. The mediation process helps the homeowner and lender find common ground and reach a mutually satisfactory solution.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 25 days from when the lender initiates foreclosure proceedings
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners living in the foreclosed property as their primary residence who are facing foreclosure
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The mediation program facilitates negotiation between homeowners and lenders to reach solutions that may help prevent or resolve foreclosure
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide. Mediation is scheduled throughout Maryland based on where the foreclosure action has been filed.
requirements_list: Homeowner must be living in the foreclosed property as their primary residence
The lender must have initiated foreclosure proceedings with the court system
Homeowner must submit the Request for Foreclosure Mediation form within 25 days of lender initiating foreclosure
Homeowner must pay a non-refundable $50 fee to the Circuit Court
The form and fee must be sent to the Circuit Court in the county or city where the foreclosure action was filed and to the lender's attorney
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Once the lender initiates foreclosure proceedings, homeowners receive a Request for Foreclosure Mediation form. The homeowner must complete this form and send it along with a non-refundable $50 fee to the Circuit Court in the county where the foreclosure action was filed. The form must also be sent to the lender's attorney. This must be done within 25 days. The Office of Administrative Hearings will then schedule the mediation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program created by the Maryland General Assembly in 2007 that provides loans to homeowners to buy out (redeem) ground leases. A ground lease is a lease for a term of years (usually 99 years) that is renewable forever and is subject to periodic payment of ground rent by the leasehold tenant to the ground lease holder.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent (0%) loans for up to 30 years to redeem ground leases. Maximum loan amount is $3,500, including transactional costs of up to $1,000. Transactional costs cover title search and loan closing expenses. The redemption amount is calculated by dividing the annual ground rent fee by a capitalization rate based on when the ground lease was established: .04 rate for leases created April 8, 1884 to April 5, 1888; .06 rate for leases created April 6, 1888 to July 1, 1982; and .12 rate for leases created July 2, 1982 or later. A lien is recorded against the property for the loan amount. The program cannot provide grants for this purpose.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners with ground leases who want to redeem or buy out their ground lease obligations. Applicant must own the subject property, occupy it as their principal residence, and meet household income limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To purchase and redeem ground leases that are renewable forever and subject to periodic ground rent payments. Funds cover the redemption amount and transactional costs associated with title search and loan closing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Ground rents are most prevalent in Baltimore City but are held in some other counties as well. Statewide availability.
requirements_list: Be a homeowner with a ground lease
Own the subject property and occupy it as principal residence
Meet household income limits (cannot exceed 80 percent of Statewide median; specific limits based on household size)
Provide copy of recorded document with ground rent
Provide evidence of ownership (copy of deed)
May apply even if behind in paying ground rent
If other names appear on deed but do not occupy property, must provide proof they live elsewhere (copy of driver's license, utility bill, notarized statement, or other evidence)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the DHCD Ground Rent Redemption Loan Application form and submit with required documentation including: most recent month of pay stubs for each employed household member over 18; most recent 2 years of federal tax returns and W-2 statements or signed Affidavit of Tax Filing Status; pension or public assistance award letter and current statement if applicable; mortgage verification form or current mortgage statement; copy of deed; copy of first page of homeowners and flood insurance policies; copy of most recent county and local property tax bill; copy of most recent bank statements; and copy of most recent Ground Rent Billing statement. Borrower selects any qualified title company to conduct title search and loan closing. Applications are available on DHCD's website or by calling the Special Loan Programs office.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Group Home Financing Program helps individuals, qualified limited partnerships, and nonprofit organizations construct, acquire, or modify housing to serve as group homes or assisted living units for people with special housing needs, including low-income seniors, people with disabilities, homeless persons, and victims of sex trafficking. It also refinances mortgages on existing group homes. The program uses state funds from the Group Home Financing Program and proceeds from tax-exempt mortgage revenue bonds under the Special Housing Opportunities Program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans to finance newly constructed group homes, acquisition or acquisition and rehabilitation of existing residential buildings, or refinance mortgages on existing group homes. Interest rates range from 0 to 7 percent depending on the funding source and project cash flow (4% is the current target rate). Maximum loan term is generally 30 years, though can extend up to 40 years. Construction term may not exceed one year. Maximum loan amounts vary by geographic location and county but cannot exceed the appraised property value. For high-cost areas (Montgomery, Prince George's, and Howard Counties), the maximum per-bedroom amount of $125,000 may increase by 15%. Nonprofit sponsors must contribute 5 percent equity; individual sponsors must contribute 10 percent. Loan funds can cover acquisition, closing costs, appraisal and inspection fees, and modification costs including repair or replacement of major systems (heating, roofing, electrical, plumbing), accessibility modifications (ramps, grab bars), lead paint abatement, general repairs and upgrades (painting, floor coverings), and minor improvements to comply with state and local occupancy codes. Loans may contain provisions for deferral of interest and/or principal (generally not permitted for more than a two-year period). Loans will be secured by either a first or second mortgage position.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications currently not being accepted; will reopen at later date
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, qualified limited partnerships, and nonprofit organizations seeking to create or modify group homes or assisted living units for people with special housing needs including low-income individuals, elderly persons, developmentally and/or mentally disabled persons, homeless persons, and victims of sex trafficking.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loan funds may be used to refinance an existing group home mortgage or for development costs including acquisition, closing costs, appraisal and inspection fees, and modification costs. Eligible modifications include repair or replacement of major systems (heating, roofing, electrical, plumbing), accessibility modifications (ramps, grab bars), lead paint abatement, general repairs and upgrades (painting, floor coverings), and minor improvements to comply with state and local occupancy codes. Properties may allocate up to 10 percent of building space for nonresidential uses that offer goods or services benefiting lower income or otherwise disadvantaged persons.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: For Special Housing Opportunities Program financing, property must be located in a Priority Funding Area unless a waiver is granted on an exceptional basis for existing construction. Priority Funding Area maps are available on the Department of Planning's website. CDA's HOME funds generally may not be used for projects in Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery and Prince George's Counties, since these counties receive their own allocation of HOME funds.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Maryland
Property must be in good repair and comply with state and local housing and occupancy codes, or be able to be made so with loan proceeds or other funds
Appraisal must be completed by an appraiser on the Department's approved appraiser list
Property must have a home inspection acceptable to the department and cannot be more than 120 days old at time of approval
All properties built prior to 1978 must have a lead paint risk assessment from a certified and accredited lead paint testing company
If lead hazard exists, sponsor must obtain bid from certified and accredited lead paint contractor
All applicants must be licensed by the appropriate Maryland licensing authority to operate the project
Sponsors must maintain 51 percent of all beds available for residents with incomes 60 percent or less of area median income
Nonprofit sponsors must have 501(c)(3) IRS designation for Special Housing Opportunities Program funding
Nonprofit sponsors must contribute 5 percent equity toward the project
Individual sponsors must contribute 10 percent equity toward the project
Sponsors must have a contract with a State agency or county government that provides operating income and/or grant funds for the project

Sponsors must demonstrate prior group home experience with comparable size and type projects, or demonstrate capacity based on other business endeavors and prior satisfactory financial and credit management
Sponsors must pass credit review with no past due accounts, open liens, judgments, prior foreclosures or bankruptcy filings
Sponsor's fund balance must be positive and stable
Current Assets to Current Liabilities ratio should generally be 1.10 or greater

Upon sale, exchange, or disposition of property financed with a Group Home Financing Program loan, sponsors must share net equity in the property with the Department at a rate determined by the Department
Properties must now or upon completion be in compliance with local zoning requirements for the property use
Federal Funds Notice must be completed by borrower and executed by seller before entering into binding sales contract if project will use HOME funds
Maximum loan amount is $125,000 per bedroom (including resident and caretaker bedrooms), with 15% increase allowable in high-cost counties (Montgomery, Prince George's, Howard)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Initial Meeting: Sponsors new to the program are encouraged to contact GHFP Manager for initial meeting to discuss proposed project and review program requirements. 2. Application Submission: Complete application and all supporting documentation must be submitted to Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, 369B, Lanham, Maryland 20706, ATTN: Group Home Financing Program. 3. Application Processing: Upon receipt, application is date-stamped and assigned case number. Acknowledgment letter is sent identifying any missing required documentation with 30-day deadline to submit. 4. Credit Report: D&B credit reports obtained for organizations; consumer credit reports for individuals. Current fee is $100 (subject to change). 5. Preliminary Review: File reviewed by GHFP Manager for initial eligibility evaluation. 6. Federal Funds Notice: If using HOME funds, Federal Funds Notice must be completed by borrower and executed by seller prior to binding sales contract. 7. Eligibility Determination: Sponsor and project eligibility reviewed; funding source determined. 8. Notification: Sponsor notified in writing of eligibility determination and estimated loan amount. Eligibility review generally completed within 90-120 days of receiving complete application. 9. Feasibility Analysis: Project viability, sponsor acceptability, and development team evaluated. 10. Commitment Analysis: Appraisal, plans and specifications reviewed; loan terms established. 11. Commitment Approval: Project submitted for approval. 12. Loan Closing: Loan documents executed and loan closed. 13. Construction Phase: Construction monitored with periodic reports. 14. Loan Servicing: Ongoing servicing and compliance monitoring.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides funding to support the development of affordable housing. The program offers grants or loans to help build, buy, or fix rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes. HOME funds may be used flexibly to address underwriting needs and can be structured as non-interest bearing deferred loans, amortizing loans, recoverable grants, or outright grants.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HOME funds are provided as non-interest bearing deferred loans, amortizing loans, recoverable grants requiring repayment when property is sold or ceases to be used for low-income housing, or outright grants at DHCD's discretion. Loan terms typically range from 20 to 40 years depending on the type of housing financed. The maximum amount of assistance to a single project generally will not exceed the amount needed to make the project viable and comply with federal HOME regulations. For rental projects, equity sharing may be required when low-income usage is discontinued. For homeownership projects, federal equity restrictions apply. HOME funds can be used as soft seconds to reduce borrowing costs, for land or development costs, or construction financing. For rental housing, HOME funds are targeted to serve households at or below 80% of area median household income. For homeownership projects, HOME funds are targeted to serve households at or below 80% of area median household income. The ratio of HOME-assisted units to total units is generally proportional to the ratio of HOME funds to total project costs, though proportionality may vary in high development cost areas or areas with low median incomes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State government agencies, local governments, local housing agencies, nonprofit organizations, Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs), and developers seeking to develop affordable housing for low- and very low-income residents. Also available for group home projects assisting income-eligible persons with special housing needs, and for rehabilitation and special purpose programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used to build, buy, or rehabilitate rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes. Funds can be used for land acquisition, development costs, construction financing, soft second mortgages, replacement housing, lead paint hazard reduction, accessibility modifications, furnace and roof replacement, and security deposit assistance. HOME funds may be used in conjunction with other DHCD housing programs including the Rental Housing Fund, Maryland Mortgage Program (MMP), Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program (MHRP), Indoor Plumbing Program (IPP), Accessible Home for Seniors Programs (AHSP), Lead Paint Programs (LHRGLP), and Special Housing Opportunity Program (SHOP). Limited tenant-based rental assistance is available.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. State government agencies automatically receive either their formula allocation or $3 million, whichever is greater. HOME funds are used primarily in non-Participating Jurisdictions (all Maryland counties except Baltimore City, Anne Arundel except Annapolis, Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties, which receive direct allocations). The State has discretion to provide funds in Participating Jurisdictions as deemed necessary.
requirements_list: For rental housing: residents must have household incomes at 50% or less of area median household income, or targeted at 80% AMI at State discretion
For owner-occupied housing: residents must have household income at 55% or less of area median household income, or targeted at 80% AMI at State discretion
Income limits are based on household size and set annually by HUD
If using HOME funds with other CDA programs, projects must meet both CDA program requirements and HOME federal requirements
Number of income-restricted units typically calculated by dividing HOME funds by total project cost, then multiplying by total units
Maximum HOME rent limits apply to all projects (High and Low HOME Rent Limits as calculated by HUD)
Maximum homeownership value limits apply (set separately for existing and new homes, updated annually by HUD)
CHDO projects must meet HUD Community Housing Development Organization requirements
Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) receive priority in special reserve fund allocations
Non-profit organizations and local governments in conjunction with non-profits receive priority consideration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible applicants may apply through the Community Development Administration (CDA). For multifamily projects, HOME funds may be requested as part of project application or proposed by DHCD staff during project evaluation; awards are made at time of Rental Housing Fund reservation. For single-family projects and special programs, applications may include requests for HOME funds or DHCD staff may propose use during underwriting. HOME Special Reserve Fund applications are reviewed and allocated on a first-come, first-serve basis with priority given to CHDOs, non-profits, and local governments in conjunction with non-profits. Special Reserve applications are recommended to the Director of CDA and HFRC for approval. Contact Dale Quisgard, HOME Program Manager, for specific application procedures and deadlines. Applications from CHDOs receive priority; other rating criteria include readiness to proceed, demonstrated ability, matching contributions, geographic distribution, and performance on prior HOME awards. DHCD may fund up to 5% of awards for administrative costs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids Lead Initiative
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative created by three state agencies to help families reduce lead exposure in homes built before 1978 by covering lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed. The program targets families with children who have elevated blood lead levels, providing services at no cost to the property owner or tenant.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, in partnership with the Maryland Department of Health, pays for lead removal from homes or apartments where children live or spend time at no cost to the property owner or tenant. The program covers lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland families with children under age 19 who have elevated blood lead levels and spend significant time in homes or locations with lead exposure
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed for homes or apartments where the child lives or spends time
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Child must be under 19 years old and live in Maryland
Child must have a blood lead test of 5 micrograms per deciliter (µg/dL) or higher
Child must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid or Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP)
Child must live in or visit the home/apartment with a lead problem for 10 hours or more per week
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Environmental Health Help Line at 1-866-703-3266 or email mdh.healthyhomes@maryland.gov for information about eligibility and how to apply. You can also contact your local health department.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Stretch - Affordable Housing Broadband Grant Program (Expanded Round, FY24)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to municipal and non-profit owners of affordable housing as well as internet service providers to install broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units in affordable housing, bridging the digital accessibility gap. This expanded round broadens eligibility beyond government-owned public housing to include non-profit housing owners and ISPs, and allocates $26.9 million in funding from the American Rescue Plan Act Capital Projects Fund.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $250,000 to $5,000,000 covering 95% of eligible project costs for broadband installation in affordable housing. A 5% match of eligible project costs is required. Twenty-six point nine million dollars allocated for this expanded round. Funding source is the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, Capital Projects Fund.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Deadline extended to February 7, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipal and non-profit owners of public housing and internet service providers working to install broadband in affordable housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units in affordable housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a municipal or non-profit owner of public housing or an internet service provider
Project must provide broadband capable wiring to individual dwelling units
Minimum match requirement of 5% of eligible project costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Municipal and non-profit housing owners and internet service providers submit applications with grant application package, forms, budget documentation, and support materials. Application deadline is February 7, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Stretch - Public Housing Broadband Grant Program (Round 1, FY24)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to owners of public housing to install broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units, addressing digital equity and inclusion needs in low-income public housing communities. The program aims to provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds to each dwelling unit, along with free WiFi service in common areas. Eligible applicants are local jurisdictions (county or municipal) and recognized jurisdictional housing authorities that own and maintain publicly supported housing for low- and moderate-income households.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $500,000 to $9,000,000 covering eligible project costs for broadband installation in public housing. Applicants must provide a cash match of minimum 5% of actual capital construction costs. Non-capital administrative costs (community engagement, ACP registration assistance, educational outreach) are capped at 3% of total project cost, not to exceed $15,000. Additional non-capital administrative costs exceeding the 1% cap must be paid by the applicant. Match funds may come from local, state, or federal sources. Funding source is the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 22, 2023
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (county or municipal), including recognized jurisdictional housing authorities, that own and maintain publicly supported housing for low- and moderate-income households.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units in public housing; extension of fiber optic facilities to public housing structures; installation of end user facilities including interior wiring, wireless access points, and necessary electronics; building modifications necessary for service delivery; community engagement and technical assistance for broadband adoption, including Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP) registration assistance; engineering and design services; broadband network equipment, installation, and provisioning costs. Ineligible uses include middle mile infrastructure (except to nearest point), major rehabilitation or construction, telephone or video service expenses, purchase of land or towers, and operating expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Eligible project areas are publicly owned housing developments identified as having need for additional broadband investment, including lack of access to connections reliably meeting or exceeding 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload speeds, lack of affordable broadband access, or lack of reliable broadband service.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction (county or municipal) or recognized jurisdictional housing authority that owns and maintains publicly owned housing
Project location must be a publicly owned housing development identified as having need for additional broadband investment

Project must provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds to each dwelling unit (exceptions allowed with ISP certificate for geographic, topographic, or cost barriers)
Common area WiFi must provide minimum 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload speeds with maximum 50 milliseconds latency
Internal wiring infrastructure must be designed to facilitate open access for multiple service providers
Installation of wireless access points in public and common areas to provide free broadband service
Minimum 5% cash match of actual capital construction costs required; match cannot be used for ineligible items
Grant funds minimum: $500,000; maximum: $9,000,000 per eligible project and application
All equipment purchased must be new and non-depreciated
Applicant must commit to maintaining and securing project equipment for at least 5 years after project completion and acquire necessary hardware warranty and service agreements
Community engagement strategies must be in place, including ACP registration assistance and educational assistance to ensure connectivity per unit
Non-capital administrative costs capped at 3% of total project cost, not to exceed $15,000

Covered populations include: individuals with household income ≤150% of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, English learners, individuals with low literacy levels, and individuals who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups
Project must be completed by June 30, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit one electronic PDF copy of their complete response to osb.md@maryland.gov by December 22, 2023, with subject line including 'Broadband for Public Housing', local jurisdiction name, and project name. Applications must include: completed application form with jurisdictional legal name, federal EIN, SAM.gov UEI number, and IRS W-9 form; project summary addressing executive summary of the public housing location and how it was selected, statement of experience with past network deployments, network design with technology type and service speeds, community profile with demographic data and resident count, subscriber cost information if applicable, discussion of potential barriers, list of community and local government partners, implementation schedule with major milestones and risks, and funding scope with detailed line-item budget using the provided Capital Budget form. Network diagram(s) must be included. Applicants must identify any proprietary or confidential information. Applications will be scored on a maximum of 40 points based on project description (15 points), community need and impact, team qualifications and experience, feasibility and sustainability, budget reasonableness, and leveraging of additional funding. Awards are intended to be made in February 2024, with projects required to be completed by June 30, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: HSP is a statewide initiative that helps communities across Maryland prevent and end homelessness by providing technical support and funding to Continuums of Care (CoCs) and Local Homeless Coalitions (LHCs). These organizations coordinate homelessness services and connect people to housing programs, shelters, and other support services. The program provides over $15 million in annual funding to deliver and organize homeless services in local communities, helping households make fast connections to permanent housing with supportive services. For SFY2026, the anticipated total available funds are $15,200,000 ($14,000,000 State HSP Funds and $1,200,000 Emergency Solutions Grant from HUD), with the grant period running 18 months (July 1, 2025 through December 31, 2026).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HSP provides grants to HUD-approved Collaborative Applicants/lead agencies of Maryland Continuums of Care (CoCs) or DHCD-approved lead agencies for Balance of State CoC Local Homeless Coalitions on behalf of homeless services providers in their community. The program provides over $15 million in annual funding. For SFY2026, the anticipated total available funds are $15,200,000 ($14,000,000 State HSP Funds and $1,200,000 Emergency Solutions Grant from HUD). A minimum of $1 million is allocated specifically for projects serving unaccompanied youth. The SFY2026 grant period is 18 months (July 1, 2025 through December 31, 2026). Funds can be used for Street Outreach, Emergency Shelter, Rapid Rehousing, Homeless Prevention, PSH Case Management, HMIS, and Administrative Costs (capped at 10%). Lead agencies must provide matching funds of at least 25% of requested funding. Funding allocations per CoC/LHC range from approximately $254,885 to $3,297,802 at level funding, with potential 30% increase scenarios available based on final state budget approval. Technical support is also provided to help CoCs and LHCs coordinate resources and services for homeless populations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application Period Closed: April 25, 2025 at 5pm
structured_extraction.program_audience: HUD-approved Collaborative Applicants/lead agencies of Maryland Continuums of Care (CoCs) and DHCD-approved lead agencies for Balance of State CoC Local Homeless Coalitions that apply on behalf of homeless services providers. Lead agencies may subgrant all or part of their HSP grant to government agencies or nonprofit organizations to provide eligible services. Ultimately serves households experiencing homelessness or housing instability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for: (1) Homeless Prevention/Shelter Diversion - rental assistance, financial assistance, and housing stabilization services; (2) Emergency Shelter - operations and services including case management, child care, supportive services, transportation, and training; (3) Street Outreach - engagement and case management services to unsheltered individuals and families; (4) Rapid Re-Housing - rental assistance, financial assistance, and housing stabilization services to move people into permanent housing; (5) Permanent Supportive Housing - case management services, benefits assistance, and project-based leasing, operating, and rental assistance costs; (6) HMIS - data collection costs; (7) Special Events - Homeless Resource Days and Point-in-Time Count activities; (8) Administrative Support Costs - staffing for CoC/LHC and Coordinated Entry personnel, training and technical assistance, conference and meeting costs, and grant management/monitoring (capped at 10% of total request). Direct cash transfers are eligible for unaccompanied youth, returning citizens from incarceration, pregnant or parenting households with children under 5, and other highly vulnerable subpopulations. Flex funds for landlord incentives and removal of tenant housing barriers are also eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across all Maryland communities through the 16 Continuums of Care and Balance of State Local Homeless Coalitions. Eligible CoCs/LHCs include: Allegany County, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll County, Cecil County, Frederick County, Garrett County, Harford County, Howard County, Lower Shore, Mid-Shore, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Southern Maryland, and Washington County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a HUD-approved Collaborative Applicant/lead agency of a Maryland Continuum of Care (CoC) OR a DHCD-approved lead agency for a Balance of State CoC Local Homeless Coalition (LHC)
Lead agencies must apply for their entire CoC/LHC (DHCD will only accept one application per Continuum of Care or Local Homeless Coalition)
Only eligible lead agencies can submit applications for funding; applications from independent parties or non-affiliated organizations will not be accepted
Lead agencies must provide matching funds of at least 25% of requested funding
Applicants must be enrolled in the Homeless Management Information System (HMIS) or comparable database (for victim services providers)
Applicants must be in compliance with all HUD HMIS requirements at time of application (new subgrantees must be in full compliance at time grant agreement is signed)
Applicants must participate in Maryland State Homelessness Data Warehouse (MSHDW)
Lead agencies must certify that subgrantees meet HSP requirements
Lead agencies must perform at least one risk assessment of all grantees over the term of the grant period
Lead agencies must conduct monitoring and compliance visits to all grantees deemed high-risk
Lead agencies must conduct monitoring and compliance visits to medium- and low-risk subgrantees based on risk assessment criteria
Grantees and subgrantees must comply with Housing First approach principles
Grantees and subgrantees must comply with fair housing and equal access requirements
Grantees and subgrantees must implement non-discrimination policies including protections for actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, and marital status
Family shelters must serve all family compositions regardless of sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or age of family members; 'women and children only shelters' are not eligible
Grantees and subgrantees must have formalized grievance procedures for termination and denial of benefits
Grantees and subgrantees must maintain sound financial program management in accordance with federal OMB Uniform Guidance and Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP)
All books, client records, and financial documents must be maintained in secure locations and kept for at least 5 years after grant close
Grantees must have and maintain written standards to guide subgrantees to meet HSP requirements
Grantees and subgrantees must participate regularly in Continuum of Care meetings and activities
Both new and renewal projects will be considered for funding
Applicants must read Application Guidance carefully before completing forms
Applicants must submit applications online via the Project Portal
For SFY2026, applicants must submit 2 budget spreadsheets (level funding and 30% increase scenarios)
Organizational Profile updates and supporting materials due March 21, 2025
Applicants must demonstrate transparent and competitive project selection process using performance-based scoring method
Applicants are encouraged to allocate 50% of funding to RRH and PSH projects or increase RRH/PSH funding by 10% above FY24 levels to improve application scores
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process for SFY2026 HSP involves multiple steps and key dates: (1) February 24, 2025 - Application package emailed to CoC/LHC lead agencies; (2) March 3, 2025 - Training session 10-11am via Google Meet (recorded); (3) March 21, 2025 - Organization Profile Review and supporting materials due via email and Project Portal (includes W-9, organizational chart, financial audits, articles of incorporation, tax exemption letters, certificates of good standing, charity registration, board list); (4) April 25, 2025 - SFY2026 Application, Budget and Project Reviews due by 5pm via DHCD Project Portal; (5) June 2, 2025 - Award notifications and grant agreements issued; (6) July 1, 2025 - Grant period begins. Lead agencies must: (1) Create a FY2025 Community Development and Services Application for HSP in the Project Portal; (2) Complete DHCD Project Portal Application and Budget Screens by April 25; (3) Upload supporting attachments including CoC/LHC Application (Word), Detailed Budget and Project Listing (Excel), Project Performance Tool (Excel), Stella P Report, 2024 System Performance Measures Report, HUD Annual Performance Reports from HMIS for each renewal project (covering 1/1/2024-12/31/2024), and 2024 Housing Inventory Count and Point in Time Count data; (4) Submit one application per CoC/LHC that compiles funding requests from selected subgrantees. Applications are subject to three reviews: Threshold Review (Organization Profile Review to verify eligibility and required attachments), CoC/LHC Performance Evaluation (scoring of application narrative responses), and Project-Level Performance Evaluation (project performance data review). All applications pass through threshold review before scoring.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) WholeHome Critical Home Repairs Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps Maryland homeowners facing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic by providing funds for critical repairs in their primary residences that could lead to displacement if not addressed. Without addressing these repairs, it will cause the homeowner to be involuntarily displaced from the property. The program provides one-time grants up to $10,000 per household with no liens recorded on the property.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $10,000 per household for critical repairs. The financial assistance is a one-time grant with no liens recorded on the property. Funds can be used for critical repairs including heating and cooling systems, water heaters, electrical and plumbing or septic repairs, wells, roof repair or replacement, mold and mildew remediation, asbestos removal, lead paint hazard elimination, structural and maintenance issues, and trip/slip issues. Payment can be structured as either 33% deposit with 67% at completion or 0% deposit with 100% at completion. Homeowners are responsible for selecting a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor and providing estimates. The program does not provide reimbursement for deposits or materials purchased by homeowners prior to approval.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 30, 2026, or until funding is fully reserved, whichever comes first
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners who have experienced financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic after January 21, 2020, own and reside in their primary residence, and have critical repairs that would cause involuntary displacement if not addressed.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical repairs to primary residences including but not limited to: mold and mildew remediation, asbestos removal, non-functional heating and cooling systems, electrical repairs, plumbing and septic repairs, wells, roof repair or replacement, lead paint hazard reduction or elimination, structural and maintenance issues, and trip/slip safety issues that address health, safety, and livability issues to prevent displacement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Income limits are based on household size and County Area Median Income (AMI), with applicants required to be at or below 150% of their County AMI. Specific income limits vary by county and household size as detailed in the income limits chart.
requirements_list: Experienced financial hardship due to COVID-19 after January 21, 2020
Household income at or below 150% of County AMI based on household size
Must be a Maryland homeowner
Must reside in the primary residence as principal residence
Must be named on the deed or proof of ownership documented
If other names appear on the deed, must provide proof they live elsewhere (driver's license, utility bill, notarized statement, or death certificate if deceased)
No minimum credit score requirement
Provide at least one detailed estimate dated within the last 60 days from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractor with photographs documenting the critical repairs
Estimate must not exceed $10,000

Contractor must provide: current MHIC License or appropriate trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance with per occurrence limits equal to or greater than $1,000,000, Letter of Good Standing from Maryland, and completed W-9 form

Income documentation: recent paystubs, tax returns if self-employed, award letters for Social Security/disability/pension, unemployment documentation, or notarized Zero Income Statement if reporting no income
Photo ID for applicant and any co-applicant
Must attest to COVID-19 financial hardship after January 21, 2020
One-time financial assistance per household
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. Applicants must complete the WholeHome Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) application and submit it with required documentation including: (1) income verification documents, (2) attestation of COVID-19 financial hardship after January 21, 2020, and (3) at least one detailed estimate dated within the past 60 days from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor with photo documentation. The contractor must also submit the Bid Cover Page and required business documents including current license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and signed W-9. Applications can be submitted by email to Rehab.HAFApplications@Maryland.gov or mailed to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA Special Loan Programs- Rehab Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF), 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. For inquiries, contact the Special Loan Programs office at 301-429-7409 or DHCD.SpecialLoans@maryland.gov. Upon approval, applicants must sign a Commitment Letter, Grant Agreement, Rehabilitation Contract, W-9 form, and final invoice from contractor. The program does not monitor work quality or manage the project; this is the responsibility of the homeowner and contractor.

structured_extraction.program_description: The federal Housing Choice Voucher Program provides rental subsidies in the form of vouchers to eligible families or individuals to use toward housing payments. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development through regional offices and local housing agencies. Local public housing agencies (PHAs) administer the program, including creating eligibility criteria, processing applications, developing and maintaining waitlists, verifying requirements, conducting housing inspections, approving landlords, and processing rent payments. The program includes special purpose vouchers for targeted populations such as Veterans (VASH), families involved with child welfare (FUP), and non-elderly disabled persons (NED2). Families can use vouchers to move to housing of their choice in the private market, subject to housing quality standards and rent reasonableness requirements. Applicants can check the status of their name on a waitlist through MRI Waitlist Check at http://waitlistcheck.com/.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides rental subsidies through Housing Choice Vouchers that eligible families and individuals can use toward housing payments at properties of their choice. The PHA determines the subsidy amount based on family income, family size, and local payment standards. Families typically pay 30% of their adjusted gross income toward rent, and the voucher covers the difference between the family's payment and the approved rent, up to the payment standard. Local public housing agencies (PHAs) administer the program including eligibility screening, waitlist management, housing inspections, landlord approval, and rent payment processing. Special purpose vouchers are available for Veterans (VASH), families involved with child welfare (FUP), and non-elderly disabled persons (NED2).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM (for current waitlist reopening)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible families or individuals seeking rental housing assistance, including families at or below 30%, 50%, and 80% of area median income (AMI), elderly persons, families with disabilities, veterans, families involved with child welfare, and non-elderly disabled individuals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing payments. Vouchers can be used to rent any type of housing that meets Housing Quality Standards, including single-family homes, townhouses, and apartments in the private rental market.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local public housing agencies in each Maryland county and municipality. Current waitlist reopening applies to Eastern Shore counties (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Talbot, Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties) and the Town of Elkton. The program is administered through the following offices: Allegany County Human Resources Development Commission, Frederick County Department of Housing and Community Development, Garrett County Community Action Committee Inc., and the Eastern Shore Regional Office for seven Eastern Shore counties. Applicants should contact their local Public Housing Authority for information on how to apply.
requirements_list: Must be a U.S. citizen or have eligible immigration status
Must meet income limits (generally at or below 80% of area median income, with preference for families at or below 30% AMI)
Families must provide mandatory Social Security numbers for all household members
Must pass eligibility screening and tenant screening criteria
Subject to lottery selection process for waitlist placement during open application periods
Must meet Housing Quality Standards for approved units
Must not have a history of drug-related criminal activity or other specified disqualifying factors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a preliminary application through the Waitlist Status Portal or submit a written pre-application as directed in the PHA public notice during open application periods. Applicants are placed on a waitlist and selected through a lottery process. Once selected, applicants complete a full application and undergo eligibility verification. Eligible families receive vouchers and are required to attend an eligibility briefing to learn about program rights and responsibilities. Families then have a specified period (typically 120 days) to locate an eligible unit and request tenancy approval. The PHA must approve the unit and landlord, conduct a Housing Quality Standards inspection, and approve the rent as reasonable before executing the Housing Assistance Payment contract. In-person assistance is available at specific locations for individuals needing support. Current application period for Eastern Shore and Town of Elkton locations runs from April 1, 2026, at 9:00 AM to April 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM. Contact your local Public Housing Authority for application information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides low- or no-interest loans to local housing authorities or county governments partnering with housing developers to increase housing production. The program also allows counties to purchase existing privately owned housing in partnership with housing authorities or developers to create public housing opportunities and reward counties pursuing innovative housing solutions.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low- or no-interest loans provided through the Housing Innovation Fund to support rental housing development projects. Loans are available for new construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing. Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing with at least 20% of units for households earning 50% or less of area median income, or at least 40% of units for households earning 60% or less of area median income. Loan terms fall into two categories: Short-term loans (3-5 years) at approximately 3% interest rate, or longer-term loans (7-10 years) at approximately 5.5% interest rate. HIPP loans are typically structured as subordinate loans. Maximum award per project is $2,500,000. Total FY 2026 funding available is $5,000,000 with a maximum of one award per jurisdiction. Application fee is $2,500.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Noon on May 18, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public housing authorities and county governments partnering with housing developers to create affordable rental housing. Only local housing authorities, county governments, and counties in conjunction with housing authorities or developers are eligible to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used for new construction of rental housing, acquisition of existing rental housing, or rehabilitation of rental housing. Eligible housing types include apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities. All projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized rental housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to eligible Maryland counties and local housing authorities. Projects must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public housing authority or county government partnering with a housing developer, or a county in conjunction with a PHA or developer to acquire existing housing
Sponsor must have an ownership interest in the project's ownership entity as demonstrated by organizational chart and/or partnership agreement
Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing

At least 20% of units must be set aside for households with gross annual income of 50% or less of area median income, OR at least 40% of units must be set aside for households with gross annual income of 60% or less of area median income

Eligible housing types include new construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing such as apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities
Projects must be ready for occupancy within two (2) years of award selection date
Project must meet all threshold requirements from the Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide

Applicants must comply with fair housing and equal opportunity laws including Title VI and VII of the Civil Rights Act, Fair Housing Act, Americans with Disabilities Act, and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act
Projects must meet DHCD Multifamily Policies regarding construction standards and individual unit health and safety requirements
Projects must agree to ongoing compliance, asset management, and inspections
All affordable unit set-asides must remain restricted at elected levels for at least 99 years for projects receiving Preference Points
Projects must include commitment to prevailing wage requirements for Preference Points
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should request an electronic application folder using the Electronic Submission Package Request Form in the Multifamily Library. One complete electronic application including attachments and exhibits must be submitted via Procorem WorkCenter by the deadline. All sections, attachments, and exhibits must be clearly tabbed. Application forms should not be retyped or modified. All required exhibits must be included with electronic signatures accepted. A $2,500 application fee must be sent separately to Community Development Administration, Post Office Box 2524, Landover Hills, MD 20784, with a copy of the check included with the application submission. The application must include CDA Form 202 (Multifamily Rental Financing Application dated February 2025), certifications, threshold checklist, applicant self-scoring, organizational chart, and letters of intent for all other financing sources. An information session is held on March 11, 2026 at 12pm. Waiver requests must be submitted in writing via the Waiver Request Form at least 15 days prior to the application deadline (by May 4, 2026). DHCD staff will review for completeness; incomplete submissions will be returned. Complete applications will be scored by a committee using scoring criteria including Project Readiness (up to 6 points), Location (up to 6 points), Preferences (16 points), Innovation (up to 10 points), Affordability (up to 12 points), and Developer/Owner/Partner Capacity (up to 12 points). The highest-scored proposal per jurisdiction will be recommended to the CDA Director for approval, then to the Secretary for final approval. DHCD reserves the right to reject or cease processing any proposal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for Maryland residents who make their homes more accessible by completing renovations with accessibility features. Eligible applicants can receive up to 50% of renovation costs back, with a maximum credit of $5,000.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a tax credit equal to up to 50% of qualified home renovation costs for accessibility features, with a maximum credit of $5,000 per year. Applicants must be Maryland residents, file taxes in Maryland for the year the renovations were completed, and provide proof of payment including receipts, invoices, and before-and-after photos.
