DHCD can approve up to $1,000,000 in total tax credits per year; if demand exceeds this amount, individual credits may be reduced. Eligible accessibility features include: no-step entrances, doorways with 32-inch or wider clear openings, grab bars and reinforced walls, handrails, rocker panel light switches, accessible routes, accessible handles, chairlifts and elevators, visual smoke/fire/carbon monoxide alarms, roll-in showers/tubs, alarms for sensory disabilities, railings for steps and hallways, hallways/circulation paths 36 inches or more, slip-resistant floors, switches/doorbells/thermostats/breaker boxes at no more than 48 inches above floor, electrical receptacles at least 15 inches above floor, lever water controls, full extension pull-out drawers/shelves/racks in base cabinets, accessible door hardware, bathroom mirrors/medicine cabinets within reach ranges, creation of accessible parking spaces, kitchen appliances/work spaces within reach ranges, and maneuvering space of at least 30 inches by 48 inches in bathrooms/kitchens.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1st of the current calendar year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who have completed home renovations to make their homes more accessible, including owners of their own home, family members' homes, or rental properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home renovations that include accessibility features such as no-step entrances, grab bars, handrails, chairlifts, elevators, roll-in showers, accessible kitchens and bathrooms, and other modifications to improve accessibility for people with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents only; applicants must file taxes in Maryland for the same calendar year they made the renovations.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident
File taxes in Maryland for the same calendar year the renovations were completed
Have proof of payment for home renovations that include accessibility features
Submit a completed application to DHCD and provide any additional information requested
Renovations must have been completed during the previous tax year
Submit required detailed invoices
Submit required proof of payment(s)
Submit required pre-accessibility renovation pictures
Submit required post-accessibility renovation pictures
Submit other supporting documentation and/or permits if applicable
Must not have received funds or tax credits from other sources for the same renovation work
Must keep documentation (invoices and receipts) and provide upon request
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: After completing your renovation, file your taxes for the year you completed the renovation. Complete the Independent Living Tax Credit Application form and submit it along with supporting documentation (detailed invoices, proof of payment, before-and-after photos, and other supporting documentation/permits) by June 1st of the current calendar year. Applications can be submitted either online or by email to DHCD.SLP_Documentation@Maryland.gov or by mail to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA Special Loan Programs- Independent Living Tax Credit Application, Attention: SLP Intake Team, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. A representative from DHCD may contact you to gather additional information. DHCD will review your application by August 31st of the current calendar year. If approved, you will be notified and issued a tax credit certificate. File an amended tax return (Form 502X) with the DHCD tax credit certification attached.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides loans to homeowners and landlords with limited income to install or repair indoor plumbing systems in residential properties, including wells, septic systems, water and sewer connections, and related fixtures. It is a specialized sub-program of the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program focused on plumbing-related health and safety improvements, addressing critical issues and bringing properties into compliance with applicable building codes and standards.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on the applicant's ability to pay and income level. For households at 80% of median income, interest rates range from 4.5% to 6.0%. For households at 60% of median income, interest rates range from 0% to 4.5%. Households at 50% of median income or below may be eligible for deferred principal and interest. The maximum loan term is 30 years. The maximum loan amount is generally $50,000. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage. Deferred amounts may be forgiven annually for families with incomes below 30 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes with incomes at or below 80 percent of statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income, and owners of rental residential properties if units will be occupied by income-eligible households. Household income limits as of July 1, 2025 vary by household size and geographic area (Washington, DC PMSA or Rest of State).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wells, septic tanks and drain fields, piping from septic system into residential building, connection expenses to public water or sewer systems, plumbing fixtures and equipment including handicapped fixtures, additions and modifications for private toilet and bath facilities, sand mound systems, purification systems, percolation test costs, and alternative or innovative septic and water systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Loan requests are generally processed directly by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction. For the Washington, DC PMSA (includes Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery and Prince George's counties), different income limits apply than for the rest of state.
requirements_list: Property must be structurally sound
Must be a single-family, owner-occupied house with inoperative or unsafe plumbing
Owner-occupants must have income at or below 80 percent of statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
Residents of assisted rental housing must have income at or below 80 percent of statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
Applicant must provide proof of home ownership including deed and current mortgage statement
Applicant must provide photo ID (driver's license, passport, military ID, etc.)
Applicant must provide most recent property tax bill
Applicant must provide declaration page of homeowners insurance policy
Applicant must provide copy of flood insurance policy if applicable
Applicant must provide income verification documents (paystubs, tax returns, bank statements, benefit award letters, etc.)
Applicant must provide lowest qualifying bid from a licensed Maryland tradesperson or company
Bid should not be more than 60 days old
Grand total of all bids should not exceed $50,000
Contractor must provide current MHIC License or applicable trade license (Electrical, Plumbing, HVAC, etc.)
Contractor must provide Certificate of Liability Insurance with per occurrence limits equal to or greater than $1,000,000
Contractor must provide Letter of Good Standing
Contractor must provide completed and signed W-9 form
Bid must include photographs documenting the critical repairs, contractor's phone number and email address
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact their local housing office or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Special Loan Programs at (301) 429-7409, 877-218-8101, or 1-844-369-4150. Applicants must complete the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program Application form and submit it along with all required documentation including income verification, proof of home ownership, property tax bill, homeowners insurance declaration page, flood insurance policy if applicable, and contractor bids with supporting documentation. The completed application and supporting documentation should be submitted via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mailed to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Loans are originated, packaged, and closed by the Special Loan Program's network of local administering agencies, which includes county housing and community development offices, nonprofit organizations, and local banks. Incomplete applications will not be processed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Grant Program (HUD-Funded, Statewide Except Baltimore City)
structured_extraction.program_description: This federally funded program helps Maryland homeowners and landlords remove lead hazards from their properties using funds from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development's Office of Lead Hazard Control and Healthy Homes. Available statewide except in the City of Baltimore, the program provides up to $25,000 per eligible property for lead abatement services performed by a licensed and accredited contractor.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $25,000 per eligible property to pay for lead abatement services performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor. Funds must be used specifically for lead hazard reduction activities. Available until April 1, 2029.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Available until April 1, 2029
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners and landlords who own properties with lead hazards, statewide except Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead abatement services performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide except in the City of Baltimore
requirements_list: Property owner must be eligible for the program
Work must be performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor
Properties must meet minimum program requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the Special Loan Program. Contact Special Loan Programs at the provided phone, email, or toll-free number for application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Loan and Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded program that helps make Maryland homes safer by removing or reducing lead hazards in owner-occupied single family homes, rental properties, and licensed daycare centers. Assistance is provided through grants or loans based on the applicant's ability to repay and location, with grants available in designated target areas and loans available statewide.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance in the form of grants or loans to reduce or eliminate lead-based paint hazards. Grants are available only in designated target areas with no income limits for applicants and require a 20% match for for-profit sponsors and 10% match for nonprofit sponsors. Amortizing loans available statewide with interest rates from 0% to 7% over 20 years, with maximum of $25,000 per unit and $100,000 annual sponsor maximum. Deferred loans available for applicants with no affordability to repay, at 0% interest over 20 years with potential forgiveness if no equity is available upon resale or after 20 years. In non-targeted areas, assistance is limited to applicants with household income at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI). Licensed day care centers are eligible. Clearance testing is required.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners and landlords of owner-occupied single family homes, rental properties, licensed residential childcare facilities, and non-profit organizations owning residential properties or daycare centers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead hazard reduction activities including door and window treatments and replacement, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, specialized cleaning, innovative approved lead hazard reduction methods, and other lead-related costs to meet lead dust clearance standards
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in target areas and non-target areas. Grants are available only in certain target areas. Applicants in non-targeted areas must meet income requirements. The Washington, DC PMSA includes Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties with different income limits than the rest of state.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland resident if an owner-occupant and own and occupy the dwelling as principal residence
Property must be owner-occupied single family home or residential rental property or licensed residential childcare facility
Units must be in need of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be structurally sound upon completion of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be registered with the Maryland Department of the Environment Lead Poisoning Prevention Program
In non-targeted areas, income must be at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI)
No income limits in targeted areas for grants
Work plan must fully address all lead hazards present in the project
Clearance testing is required upon completion
Grants require 20% match for for-profit sponsors, 10% match for nonprofit sponsors, and 10% match for owner-occupants with income above 80% of median
For grants, must be in target area or plan to utilize an innovative lead hazard reduction treatment
For deferred loans, underwriting must show no affordability to repay loan
Lead testing results must be provided
Property must be properly registered with MDE Lead Poisoning Prevention Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application form with all required supporting documentation to Special Loan Programs. Required documentation includes: income verification (two months of paystubs or two years of tax returns), proof of home ownership (deed and current mortgage statement), photo identification, property tax bill, homeowners insurance policy declaration page, flood insurance policy if applicable, photographs documenting lead hazards, contractor bids (lowest qualifying bid from licensed Maryland tradesperson/company not more than 60 days old, with grand total not exceeding project maximum), contractor's MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9 form. Applications may be submitted via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mailed to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Local county contacts through Special Loan Program Partners provide additional program and application information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Community Development Administration issues tax-exempt bonds on behalf of counties, municipalities, and their agencies to finance infrastructure projects that serve the community. The program manages the bond issuance process and loans the bond proceeds to local governments at market rates, reducing costs through economies of scale and pooled bond issues. The parity bond resolution for Local Government Infrastructure Bonds was created in 2002 and the newest indenture for local government financing was created in 2010. The program helps local governments that do not routinely issue bonds or have limited resources to initiate financing independently access long-term capital financing at favorable terms. Bonds are primarily credit enhanced with bond insurance, and security for the bonds is a pledge of and lien on proceeds of the sale of bonds, all local obligations, the CDA's right, title and interest in all infrastructure loans, all revenues and prepayments, and pledged funds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Community Development Administration issues tax-exempt bonds and loans the bond proceeds to local governments. The interest rate on loans is determined by market conditions at the time of bond sale based on the pooled bond issue rate. Local governments repay the debt and pay their proportional share of bond issuance costs. Loan terms are set by the local government but cannot exceed the useful life of the project or thirty years, whichever is less. Projects can range from $150,000 to $10 million or more.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies that need long-term capital financing for infrastructure projects and do not routinely issue bonds or have limited resources to initiate financing independently. Applicants must have legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain projects and pledge security for repayment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Street lighting, landscaping, sidewalks and public space improvements; public safety vehicles and equipment; water production, treatment, storage and distribution systems; storm water control and sewer collection and treatment facilities; government office and meeting facilities; police, fire, transportation, education, health, recreation, maintenance and other service-related facilities; financing of physical elements that constitute the public service system; and refinancing of existing debt for eligible projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties and municipalities are eligible statewide.
requirements_list: Local government must have legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain the proposed project
Local government must have legal authority to pledge security for and repay the proposed loan
Local government must have legal authority to pledge income tax payments and various other shared revenue from the State
Project must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system
Project must meet federal tax law requirements
Project must be undertaken by or on behalf of a local government, including its agencies
Loan term cannot exceed the useful life of the project or thirty years, whichever is less
Applicant must be a local government
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The local government completes an application that requires information similar to what a bond rating agency would need to evaluate creditworthiness. Applicants can submit an Expression of Interest form outlining the proposed project or specific questions to request technical assistance from the Community Development Administration. Bond issuance timing is influenced by the volume and frequency of participation by local governments. Contact the Community Development Administration for full application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Housing Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program that encourages private sector investment in the construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. Tax credits are awarded competitively to nonprofit and for-profit sponsors based on criteria in the state's Qualified Allocation Plan. The tax credit equals the applicable percentage of the qualified basis of each qualified low-income rental housing building, as determined by the IRS.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis to sponsors of eligible housing projects. The tax credit equals the applicable percentage of the qualified basis of each qualified low-income rental housing building. Project sponsors or their investor partners claim the tax credit on their federal income tax return. Credits represent equity for a building's initial construction or rehabilitation. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible for tax credits outside of the competitive process. The building must remain in compliance and is subject to a covenant to enforce compliance for a minimum of 15 years (Compliance Period) followed by an Extended Use Period of at least 15 additional years. During the Extended Use Period, compliance requirements are less stringent, with inspections occurring at least once every five years instead of annually. Owners must submit annual Owner Certifications of Continuing Compliance (OCPC), maintain tenant income and rent records, and conduct household income recertifications (full recertifications at least every five years for exempt buildings, or annually for non-exempt buildings).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Competitive allocation on annual basis; portal for end-of-year data uploads typically May 16 through June 20
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit sponsors seeking to develop or rehabilitate affordable rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. During Extended Use Period, contact Division of Credit Assurance for compliance matters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and rehabilitation of residential rental buildings that provide housing for low-income occupancy. Tax credits support the development or rehabilitation of qualified low-income rental housing buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Projects must be placed in service in or within two years after the year in which the allocation is made. Community Development Administration has final authority on compliance and monitoring.
requirements_list: Building must be a residential rental building placed in service within two years of allocation

Owner must rent either 20 percent of units to households with incomes at 50 percent or less of area median income, or 40 percent of units to households with incomes at 60 percent or less of area median income (or use Income Averaging option)
Building must comply with tenant income requirements, maximum rent levels, and low-income occupancy percentage requirements
Building must remain in compliance for a minimum of 40 years (15-year Compliance Period plus 15-year Extended Use Period plus additional restrictions)
Ten percent of the state's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors
Owner's CPA must certify total costs and compliance with program requirements before IRS Form 8609 issuance
Owners must submit annual Owner Certification of Continuing Compliance (OCPC)
Resident files must be maintained for each unit including income certifications and rent records
Property must be maintained in decent, safe, and sanitary condition suitable for occupancy
Projects with 100% LIHTC units exempt from annual tenant recertification; other buildings may apply for exemption after satisfactory initial inspection and no outstanding noncompliance
Utility allowances must be updated at least once per calendar year; tenants must be notified 90 days prior to changes
Owners must immediately report to DHCD any changes in ownership composition, management agents, or events affecting project credit

For projects entering Extended Use Period: inspections occur at least once every five years; file reviews conducted for lesser of 10% of low-income units or IRS Minimum Unit Sample Size; owners must obtain annual tenant income self-declarations in years without full recertification; next available unit rule comparable/smaller requirement no longer applies; applicable fraction determined by percentage of units only, not floor space
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis according to criteria outlined in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). Project sponsors submit applications during the annual allocation cycle. Applications are evaluated and awards are made based on evaluation of applications against QAP criteria. Once credits are allocated, owners must provide evidence of economic feasibility and obtain a cost certification from their CPA. The IRS Form 8609 (Low-Income Housing Certification) is issued in two parts: Part I is completed by DHCD and Part II is completed by the owner and filed with the owner's tax return. The owner's completed Form 8609 must be submitted to DHCD. A Low-Income Housing Tax Credit Covenant must be recorded before the end of the calendar year in which credits are first claimed. For properties transitioning to Extended Use Period after Year 15, a transition meeting with Division of Credit Assurance may be required. Annual OCPC submissions are required by deadlines published in DHCD notices. DHCD conducts on-site monitoring inspections at minimum frequency requirements. Owners must maintain comprehensive project files on-site containing all pertinent compliance documentation organized for easy access.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides relief grants to help schools, libraries, and anchor institutions close the digital divide by funding devices and internet access for K-12 students and school staff who lack necessary technology to connect to classrooms.

Total MEER funding made available was approximately $5,000,000 across eligible recipients statewide. Funding covers qualifying expenses for projects to expand broadband access and digital connectivity for underserved K-12 students, school staff, and community members.

structured_extraction.program_name: Main Street Maryland Program (Technical Assistance & Community Designation)
structured_extraction.program_description: Main Street Maryland supports community development and revitalization in Maryland's historic downtowns. The program has been transforming communities across the state since 1998 as the official coordinating program for the National Main Street Center. The program helps local communities with revitalization efforts using a comprehensive approach focused on economic vitality, design, promotion, organization, and creating clean, safe, and green neighborhoods. It offers a tiered approach based on community readiness, including Designated Main Streets (accredited programs with 34 communities), Affiliate Main Streets (9 communities), Aspiring Main Streets (two-year training program), and Connected Main Streets (commercial neighborhood districts).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Main Street Maryland provides technical assistance and support for community revitalization efforts. Communities receive guidance on the Main Street Approach™, which focuses on four core principles: Economic Vitality (using funding, incentives, and tools to support businesses and property redevelopment), Design (enhancing physical and visual features), Promotion (strengthening district identity), and Organization (building partnerships and community engagement). The program also emphasizes Clean, Safe, and Green practices focused on sustainability and resource conservation. Training opportunities vary by tier and include classroom-style instruction, virtual meetings, and recorded presentations, along with topical resource documents and manuals. In 2024, designated communities demonstrated significant impact including 200 new businesses opened, 3,030 existing businesses expanded, 505 properties improved, 45,848 full-time and 428 part-time jobs created, 327 volunteer hours contributed, and $75.2 million in total public and private investment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application process will reopen in May 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland municipalities, cities, and towns interested in revitalizing historic downtowns and commercial neighborhood districts. Applicants must be local governments or community organizations committed to economic development, historic preservation, and building community partnerships. Eligible communities must have a minimum population of 1,000 based on the most recent U.S. Census survey and must demonstrate commitment to employing a local Main Street Manager, supporting a local Main Street program budget, and organizing volunteer committees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance supports community revitalization efforts including supporting new and existing businesses, property redevelopment, enhancing physical and visual features of commercial districts, and creating vibrant, sustainable spaces that serve as economic centers for their communities. Funds support historic preservation and design initiatives to maintain communities' rich historical and cultural character through rehabilitation and adaptive reuse projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program currently supports over 50 communities statewide across Maryland's historic downtowns and commercial districts. Participating communities span all Maryland counties. Proposed Main Street area boundaries must be within a Priority Funding Area as determined by the Maryland Department of Planning.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested communities should begin by assessing community readiness and immersing themselves in the Main Street Approach™. Communities should gather stakeholders including local government leaders, visit established Main Street communities, and determine program goals. Once preparation is complete, applicants should contact Main Street Maryland staff. The application process to MD DHCD can take 6 months to a year. Newly designated communities can take 1 to 2 years to meet the National Main Street Center's standards for accreditation. Applications should be completed and submitted by a local government (municipality or county) or nonprofit organization with local government support. The application process will reopen in May 2026. Communities can also consult the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) for quick answers or contact staff at dhcd.mainstreetmaryland@maryland.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A credit enhancement program that supports small business growth and success in Priority Funding Areas across Maryland. The program enables private lenders to establish a loan loss reserve fund from fees paid by lenders, borrowers, and the State of Maryland, helping small businesses access financing they might not otherwise obtain.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program is a credit enhancement mechanism where lenders, borrowers, and the State of Maryland each contribute to a loan loss reserve fund. Enrolled loan amounts range from $10,000 to $1,000,000. Typically, the borrower and lender each contribute 1.5 percent, and Maryland matches 3 percent, totaling 6 percent of the original loan amount for the reserve account. The contribution percentages are determined by the lender within ranges established by the program. If an enrolled loan defaults, the reserve fund covers the loss. The program leverages $1 million of State funds to develop approximately $33 million in small business loans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, including nonprofit organizations, located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loan proceeds can be used for business operations and expansion. Projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area. Proceeds cannot be used for passive real estate ownership, residential or transient living facilities, institutional facilities like hospitals or universities, adult entertainment facilities, check cashing, gambling facilities, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn or gun shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, or the furtherance of sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects financed by enrolled loans must be located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas approved by the Maryland Department of Planning. The program is available for businesses located in Priority Funding Areas anywhere in Maryland.
requirements_list: Businesses must be located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas
Enrolled loan amounts range from $10,000 to $1,000,000

Lenders must be federally insured financial institutions, institutions regulated by the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, or have a participation agreement with Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A small business applies to a participating lender. The lender underwrites and enrolls an appropriate loan. The lender, borrower, and program each make contributions to a reserve account based on a formula determined by the lender within program guidelines. The lender submits a one-page enrollment form with summary information to the Maryland Capital Access Program. If a loan defaults, the lender files a claim using a one-page form for all or part of the enrolled loan amount.

structured_extraction.program_description: MEAP helps eligible Maryland households repair or replace heating, cooling, and water heating systems at no cost. The program operates year-round and is federally funded to make homes more comfortable. It is part of the DHCD Energy & Repair Programs suite.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems for eligible low-income households. Work eligibility is determined based on a home assessment and funding availability. The program is federally funded and operates year-round. Due to limited funding and high demand, applicants are currently placed on a waitlist, with most clients not expected to be serviced before summer 2026. The application process begins with submission of a complete application package to DHCD Weatherization office at 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Once eligible, a local agency will contact you to schedule a home assessment. The local agency will evaluate your service needs and discuss results with you. A contractor will then be scheduled to complete the recommended work.

Applicants may also be enrolled if they have a documented medical condition requiring functioning heating, cooling, or water heating systems (physician's letter required).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems to increase home comfort. Systems must be non-functioning to qualify.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Special flood assistance is available for homes in Allegany or Garrett County affected by flooding.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to local governments and community development organizations to capitalize grant funds that businesses can use to improve the exteriors of commercial properties located within Maryland Sustainable Communities. The program supports communities seeking to create consistent, attractive designs for their commercial corridors in order to bolster economic vitality and stimulate new private investments.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to counties, municipalities, and community development organizations to capitalize their own local facade improvement programs. Final recipients must be businesses located within designated Sustainable Communities. Individual business improvements must be between $1,000 and $50,000 of MFIP funding per award cycle. Funds support capital improvements only, prioritizing aesthetic improvements over routine maintenance. Eligible uses include: signage, exterior painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, exterior lighting, window and door upgrades, masonry or cornices, murals, removal of unattractive exterior finishes, and roofs. Ineligible uses include interior work, electric charging stations, solar panels, predevelopment and operating expenses, and improvements banned by local building codes or zoning.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Counties, municipalities, and community development organizations serving Sustainable Communities areas. Final recipients are businesses located within designated Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital costs for improving the exteriors and facades of business buildings and facilities. Eligible improvements include signage, exterior painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, exterior lighting, window and door upgrades, public-facing masonry or cornices, murals, removal of unattractive exterior finishes, and roofs. Improvements must be on or attached to primary elevations of commercial properties and prioritize aesthetic improvements over routine maintenance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Funding can only be used in areas designated as Sustainable Communities, which are geographic areas targeted for revitalization by local governments. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility. All MFIP projects are subject to the Maryland Historical Trust Act and Federal Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete a formal application including required attachments: evidence of site control, photographs of existing conditions, written consent from property owners/lessees, project description with two cost estimates and sketches, and evidence of business standing with the State. Local program guidelines must include criteria for rating qualified businesses and awarding grants. Awardees develop their own program guidelines compliant with MFIP requirements and are encouraged to include matching fund requirements, additional ineligible uses, broad distribution requirements, and geographic targeting. All improvements are subject to historic preservation review by DHCD's Preservation Officer and the Maryland Historical Trust. Work must comply with applicable building codes, zoning ordinances, Historic Preservation Commission requirements, and other regulations. DHCD provides model program documents following best practices that awardees can modify to suit their needs. For more information, refer to the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides affordable loans to homeowners to address critical health and safety issues in owner-occupied single-family homes and bring properties into compliance with applicable building codes and standards. The goal is to preserve and improve single-family homes while helping households earning up to 80% of the Adjusted Median Income set by DHCD each year. Administered by DHCD's Special Loan Programs unit, the program is available statewide through local housing offices and nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on the applicant's ability to pay and household income level. The maximum loan amount is generally $50,000, or up to 110% of home equity, whichever is less. Minimum loan amount is $5,000. The maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage (deed of trust recorded on property). Loans serving families with incomes at or below 50% of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may have deferred payments if needed for project feasibility. Interest rates range from 0% to 4.5% for households at 60% of median income, and 4.5% to 6.0% for households at 80% of median income. The maximum initial deposit for contractors is 33% of total project cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes with household income not exceeding 80% of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Primary residence only.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical health and safety repairs including mold remediation, gas leaks, roof repair and replacement, gutters, asbestos abatement, vermiculite removal, lead abatement, combustion appliance repair and replacement, chimney repair, foundation and sub-space waterproofing, radon mitigation, electrical hazards and upgrades, plumbing issues, water and well repairs, septic and sewer work, windows and doors for health and safety or water intrusion, structural repair, accessibility modifications for disabled persons and seniors, fall prevention measures, ductwork upgrades and installations (primarily for solid fuel-burning households in Allegany and Garrett counties), building shell stabilization, and pest treatments. All work must bring the property up to current building codes and standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Loans are processed directly by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction. Statewide availability through local housing offices and nonprofit organizations. Special consideration for Allegany and Garrett counties for ductwork upgrades related to solid fuel-burning households.
requirements_list: Owner-occupant of single-family home (duplex, townhome, condo, or manufactured homes excluded)
Household income cannot exceed 80% of statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
Property must be primary residence only
No active bankruptcy or foreclosure (both must be dismissed for minimum of 2 years)
Licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement contractor or trade professional must provide work proposal
Contractor work proposal must be dated within the past 60 days
Bid must include photographs documenting the critical repairs
Contractor must provide current MHIC License or relevant trade license
Contractor must provide Certificate of Liability Insurance with per occurrence limits equal to or greater than $1,000,000
Contractor must provide Letter of Good Standing
Contractor must provide completed and signed W-9 form
Must provide proof of home ownership including deed and current mortgage statement
Homeowners insurance required

If other names appear on deed but persons do not occupy property, must provide proof of their different residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact your local housing office or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Special Loan Programs at (301) 429-7409 or 877-218-8101 to obtain the application. 2. Complete the Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program application form. 3. Obtain at least one detailed estimate from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement contractor dated within the past 60 days that documents critical health and safety repairs with photographs. 4. Submit required contractor documentation including MHIC License or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9 form. 5. Gather and submit income verification documents including recent paystubs or employment letter, 2 years of Federal Income Tax Returns, 2 months of bank statements, and any benefit award letters. 6. Submit proof of home ownership including deed, current mortgage statement, and recent property tax bill. 7. Submit Declaration Page of Homeowners Insurance Policy and Flood Insurance Policy if applicable. 8. Submit completed application checklist and all required documentation to email DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 9. DHCD staff will review the application and contractor qualifications to verify compliance with program requirements. 10. If approved, sign commitment letter, rehabilitation contract, construction agreement, and W-9 form before funding is released.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative that reduces interest rates on loans for certified Minority Business Enterprises and Small Businesses by up to 2 percent when they obtain loans from participating banks.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Borrowers receive up to a 2 percent discount on loan interest rates for term loans or fixed-rate loans with one disbursement. Loan terms cannot exceed 10 years. Loans must be for projects or activities located in Maryland. Points charged by the lender cannot exceed 1 percent of the loan amount. The State Treasurer deposits funds equal to the loan amount with the issuing bank at a commensurately reduced interest rate. Participating lenders include Bank Annapolis, Industrial Bank, and Columbia Bank.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects or activities located in Maryland. Loans may not be used for the furtherance of sectarian or religious purposes or instruction.

Borrower must notify the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development prior to obtaining the qualifying loan
Borrower must obtain the loan from a participating financial institution designated by the Maryland State Treasurer's Office
Borrower must remain in good standing as a certified Minority Business Enterprise or small business with the State of Maryland to maintain the interest rate reduction benefit
Loan term cannot exceed 10 years

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An eligible applicant or participating lender submits a brief application to the Linked Deposit Program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, either online or on paper. The department verifies the applicant's eligibility and forwards the application to all enrolled banks. The department provides the borrower with a list of participating banks. The borrower then contacts participating banks to complete their full loan application. Participating banks underwrite the loan according to their standard requirements with an interest rate up to 2 percent lower than the rate for a similar loan. Upon loan approval and acceptance, the bank enrolls the loan in the Linked Deposit Program. The Maryland State Treasurer's Office then deposits funds equal to the loan amount with the issuing bank. Participating lenders include Bank Annapolis (www.bankannapolis.com), Industrial Bank (www.industrial-bank.com), and Columbia Bank (www.thecolumbiabank.com).

structured_extraction.program_description: Increases the construction and rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing for families with limited incomes using tax-exempt bonds and notes to provide construction and permanent financing, and leverages federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits. The program finances new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of existing rental housing, and can also refinance existing high interest rate private loans when done in conjunction with rehabilitation. It aims to create more housing for families with limited incomes through direct loans and insured or guaranteed loans.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds and notes provide construction and permanent financing for multifamily rental housing. Interest rates are based on the Community Development Administration's bond rate. Loan terms are generally 30 to 40 years permanent amortization, with permanent amortization periods typically 35-40 years depending on financing structure, and construction periods typically 20-24 months. A first lien position is generally required. Multiple financing options are available including FHA-CDA Risk Sharing (FHA Section 542(c)), GNMA MBS (FHA Sections 221(d)(4)), Freddie Mac Tax Exempt Loans, Cash Collateral/GNMA MBS, and FNMA MBS Collateral for Tax Exempt Bonds (both Immediate Start and Forward Start). Estimated all-in permanent mortgage rates range from approximately 5.77% to 6.82% depending on financing structure and credit enhancement. Upfront costs range from approximately $1,027,000 to $2,068,000 depending on financing option. Sponsors may make 20 units available to households earning 50 percent or less of area median income, or 40 percent of units available to households earning 60 percent or less of area median income. All loans must be insured or have other credit enhancement acceptable to the program. Bond proceeds must satisfy the 50% test for Low-Income Housing Tax Credits and must be 100% cash collateralized. Fees include CDA Financing Fee (1.625% of bond/loan amount), CDA Bond Loan Closing Attorney's Fee ($45,000 for first loan plus $9,000 for each additional), ongoing CDA Issuer Fee (0.40% of outstanding principal), Trustee Fees, Rebate Analyst Fees, and Servicing Fees (0.25% of outstanding principal for long-term loans). The program also accommodates pairing taxable GNMA loans with tax-exempt bonds for qualified projects to achieve lower interest rates and reduce borrowing costs.

structured_extraction.contact_name: Housing Development Programs; Benedict DuRant; Kristen Musallam

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of existing rental housing. Refinancing of existing high interest rate private loans if in conjunction with rehabilitation. Projects must contain a minimum of five units and complete independent dwelling units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Projects must be located in designated Priority Funding Areas. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds must comply with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan.
requirements_list: Housing must be for families with limited incomes.
Projects must contain a minimum of five complete independent dwelling units
Projects using tax-exempt bond financing must comply with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan to receive unallocated 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits
A first lien position is generally required for all bond loans
All loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program
All loans funded with tax-exempt bonds must comply with federal requirements for tax-exempt revenue bonds

Sponsor must make either 20 of the units available to households earning 50 percent or less of area median income, or 40 percent of units available to households earning 60 percent or less of area median income
Bond proceeds must be sufficient to satisfy the 50% test for Tax Credits and the full amount of Bonds must be secured 100% by cash collateral (Letter of Credit is not sufficient)

For Tax/TE Financing using taxable GNMA loans, the GNMA Loan must have HUD/GNMA credit enhancement via Section 221(d), 220, or other similar HUD programs; FHA Risk Sharing with CDA is not eligible for this structure
For Tax/TE Financing with rated bonds, a bankruptcy opinion meeting rating agency requirements (such as Moody's) must be obtained at borrower's cost

For Tax/TE Financing with rated bonds, borrower is not entitled to residual amounts on deposit in Bond indenture accounts, not entitled to collect excess investment earnings, and cannot direct investment of funds held in Bond indenture accounts
For Tax/TE Financing with unrated private placements, the entity purchasing Bonds must be approved by CDA and must retain the Bonds for the entire term without sale, pledge, transfer or disposal
MAP Lender must be engaged by the borrower for GNMA loan structures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For-profit and nonprofit developers may apply for Multifamily Bond loans. Prospective borrowers should contact CDA Multifamily Housing staff to discuss financing options and structure projects. A MAP Lender must be engaged by the borrower for GNMA loan structures. For projects utilizing Tax/TE Financing with rated bonds, a bankruptcy opinion meeting rating agency requirements must be provided at borrower's expense. Borrowers must submit completed TEFRA Public Hearing Notice Information Sheet. Applications are reviewed and underwritten by CDA loan underwriters. Fees are assessed at closing. Refer to the QAP Fee Schedule for complete fee details. The program accepts applications on a rolling basis. Contact Housing Development Programs at dhcd.rentalhousing@maryland.gov or 301-429-7854 for application procedures; for TEFRA public hearing notice requirements, contact Benedict DuRant at benedict.durant@maryland.gov or 301-429-7823.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability (MEEHA) Program - Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions in affordable multifamily rental housing developments by replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment, and supporting building energy conservation and alternative energy generating systems. The GHGRP specifically targets larger multifamily buildings (35,000+ gross sq ft) with deeper affordability requirements (minimum 51% of units at or below 80% AMI for at least 15 years). The GHGRP has $8.75 million allocated for fiscal year 2024 and $5 million each for fiscal years 2025 and 2026.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants only (no loans). The GHGRP has $8.75 million allocated for fiscal year 2024 and $5 million each for fiscal years 2025 and 2026. Funding is limited to $15,000 per unit. Measure-specific maximum funding amounts range from $4 per faucet aerator to $7,600 per mini-split heat pump (Tier 2), with different rates for different building types and system capacities. Funds are released after equipment has been installed and inspected.
