structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of affordable multifamily rental housing developments with buildings of 35,000+ gross square feet
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions by replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment. Support building energy conservation and alternative energy generating systems. Eligible measures include: air sealing, appliance replacements, domestic hot water systems, window/door replacements, HVAC systems, insulation, lighting upgrades, and electrification measures. Funding also available for energy audits, health and safety work, incidental repairs, and electrification add-on costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide (all Maryland counties)
requirements_list: Single building must have gross floor area of 35,000 sq ft or more (excluding parking garages), OR two or more buildings with combined gross floor area of 35,000 sq ft or more served by the same meter or heating/cooling system
Minimum 51% of households at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 15 years
If affordability designation does not exist, DHCD will create a regulatory agreement to be recorded with land records
Projects must be affordable multifamily rental housing developments
All affordability requirements must be maintained for the entire compliance period with ongoing annual monitoring
Qualified Energy Professional from DHCD's approved list must conduct energy audit for rehabilitation projects or review design for new construction
Comprehensive energy audit required per BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards with sampling of units (rehabilitation projects)
New construction projects must receive energy certification from an approved energy professional
Post-retrofit condition must meet current ASHRAE 62.2 ventilation standards
All exhaust fans must vent to exterior of building envelope, outside attic space
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Owner completes MEEHA Application Form and submits to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov or submits 202 application if also applying for DHCD Rental Lending programs. Application package must include: completed application, commercial utility bills, customer consent form for energy use information, grantee signature block, property deed with legal description, SDAT property ownership and status checks, Minority Business Enterprise Plan, ACH Direct Deposit Form, proof of affordability, and W-9 form. 2. A Qualified Energy Professional (QEP) from DHCD's approved list conducts a comprehensive energy audit (for rehabilitation) or reviews design for energy efficiency certification (for new construction). 3. QEP enters recommended energy conservation measures (ECMs) into DHCD's Hancock Mobile Intake Tool (MINT) or uses the Rehab Funding Request Form to create a funding request with actual contractor bids. Costs must include materials, equipment, and installation. 4. QEP submits Funding Request to DHCD on behalf of the project owner with supporting documents including utility bills, photos of existing conditions with model/serial numbers, and other required exhibits. 5. DHCD reviews and approves the Funding Request, sending a scope confirmation spreadsheet. 6. Project owner and DHCD execute a funding agreement. 7. Project owner installs the funded greenhouse gas reduction measures per approved scope. 8. Project team submits requisitions with documentation of installed measures. 9. DHCD performs inspections to verify installations meet program standards. 10. DHCD processes payment (typically 4–5 weeks after inspection). 11. After construction completion, project enters affordability compliance period and is monitored annually for continued compliance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to reduce electric or gas consumption in affordable multifamily rental housing developments through energy efficiency improvements and limited health and safety or incidental repairs. Gas reducing measures are available only in Baltimore Gas and Electric Company or Washington Gas Light Company utility territories. The program funds energy conservation measures (ECMs) for affordable multifamily projects. Funding may be provided as either a grant or a 0% interest deferred-payment loan. The EmPOWER program has $134.9 million allocated for calendar years 2024–2026. The program aims to reduce greenhouse gases and keep housing affordable.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding is provided as either a grant or a 0% interest loan with deferred payments; an additional fee may apply for loans. The EmPOWER program has $134.9 million allocated for calendar years 2024–2026. Tier 1 funding applies to projects with a minimum of 5 years of affordability; Tier 2 funding applies to projects with a minimum of 15 years of affordability. Maximum funding amounts vary by measure type and tier level (e.g., $4 per faucet aerator up to $7,600 per mini-split heat pump at Tier 2). Funds are released after equipment has been installed and inspected.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and developers of affordable multifamily rental housing developments. Eligible applicants include government bodies, for-profit companies, non-profit organizations, and individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduce electric or gas consumption through energy efficiency measures including building shell improvements, HVAC and water heating systems, lighting, appliances, fenestration, air sealing, insulation, and electrification measures. Limited health and safety or incidental repairs in projects completing these measures. Energy audit fees may be requested on the first construction draw.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Gas reducing measures are limited to Baltimore Gas and Electric Company or Washington Gas Light Company utility territories.
requirements_list: Minimum 20% of households must be at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less
Affordability requirement must be maintained for a minimum of 5 years for Tier 1 funding or 15 years for Tier 2 funding
Projects must be affordable multifamily rental housing developments
All building sizes and configurations eligible including single family units as group projects, individually metered, or master metered buildings
Qualified Energy Professional from DHCD's approved list must conduct energy audit for rehabilitation projects or review design for new construction
Energy audit must comply with BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards
Sampling protocol requires inspection of at least 10% of dwelling units (minimum 5 units) including one representative unit from each unique type
Post-retrofit condition must meet current ASHRAE 62.2 ventilation standards
Owner must provide utility account information and authorize utility to release energy use information for up to 3 years post-completion
All insulation materials must not contain formaldehyde intentionally added or present at greater than 0.1% by weight
If affordability designation does not exist, DHCD will create a regulatory agreement to be recorded with land records
All exhaust fans must vent to exterior of building envelope, outside attic space
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Owner submits completed MEEHA Application Form to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov or submits Form 202 if also applying for DHCD Rental Lending programs. Required documents include commercial utility bills, customer consent forms, proof of affordability, deed with legal description, property ownership checks, W-9 forms, Minority Business Enterprise Plan, and ACH Direct Deposit Form. 2. A Qualified Energy Professional (QEP) from DHCD's approved list conducts a comprehensive energy audit for rehabilitation projects (following BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards) or reviews design for energy efficiency certification for new construction. 3. QEP submits Funding Request to DHCD using either MINT (Hancock Mobile Intake Tool, operational January 1, 2026) or the Rehab Funding Request Form, with owner approval and supporting documents including photos and contractor bids. 4. DHCD reviews and approves the Funding Request, sending a scope confirmation spreadsheet. 5. Project owner and DHCD execute a funding agreement; if no affordability designation exists, DHCD creates and records a regulatory agreement. 6. Project installs the funded energy efficiency measures. 7. Project team submits requisitions with documentation of installed measures. 8. DHCD performs inspections and processes payment (usually 4–5 weeks). 9. After construction, project enters affordability period and is monitored for compliance for the duration of the affordability requirement.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive funding program that supports commercial and residential development projects in targeted revitalization areas in the National Capital region of Maryland. The program aims to make a meaningful neighborhood revitalization impact through modest investments coordinated with local strategies and Sustainable Communities Action Plans, furthering revitalization and economic growth goals. Applications are submitted through a competitive process with a defined timeline including training, application opening, registration cutoff, review, and award announcement.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive capital project grant/loan funding distributed to support commercial and residential development activities aligned with Sustainable Communities Action Plans in designated revitalization areas. Funds can be used for down payment assistance for homebuyers, acquiring or rehabilitating vacant properties, improving residential and business properties, energy efficiency improvements, affordable housing development, mixed-use projects combining housing and retail, community open space or public infrastructure development, and strategic demolition. Applications are submitted through the Project Portal after organization registration. The FY26 application round is closed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY26 Application Round is closed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and community development organizations working on commercial and residential revitalization projects in designated areas of the National Capital region of Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for homebuyers, acquiring or rehabilitating vacant properties, improving residential and business properties, energy efficiency improvements, affordable housing development, mixed-use projects combining housing and retail, community open space or public infrastructure development, strategic demolition, and capital projects supporting economic development, business attraction, and community revitalization.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities in Prince George's County (at least in part within the boundary created by Interstate 495 and the District of Columbia) OR in Montgomery County (within an Enterprise Zone or the boundary created by Prince George's County, Maryland Route 200, Interstate 270, Interstate 495 to the Maryland state line, and the District of Columbia).
requirements_list: Projects must support goals and objectives in a targeted area's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Projects must be located in eligible Sustainable Communities areas as defined by county and geographic boundaries
Applicants must be local governments or community development organizations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Project Portal after organization registration. The typical timeline includes training, application opening, organization registration cutoff, application closing, review period, and award announcement. Contact your Regional Project Manager for questions about specific address eligibility. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to view your jurisdiction's NED boundary. Regional Project Manager for Montgomery and Prince George's County: Jessica Argueta, Office Phone: 410-209-5848, Cellphone: 443-651-0658, Email: jessica.argueta@maryland.gov (Region 8: Central Maryland).

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financing support for the development and preservation of affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financing program for affordable rental housing development and preservation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and for-profit sponsors of affordable rental housing developments
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and preservation of affordable rental housing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Priority funding areas in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: An affordable housing production program that increases and preserves the supply of safe, sanitary affordable housing for extremely low-income and very low-income households through acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury housing with suitable amenities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HTF funds may be used as broadly and flexibly as permitted by federal regulations to address the unique underwriting needs of each project. Forms of assistance include equity investments, interest-bearing loans or advances, non-interest-bearing loans or advances, deferred payment loans, and grants. Ninety percent (90%) of the HTF annual allocation is used for production, preservation and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing through acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation. The Department retains ten percent (10%) for allowable administrative and planning expenses. Operating/rental assistance may be provided but no more than one-third of the state's annual HTF allocation and must be fully utilized within 5 years of award, though it can be subsequently renewed within the 30-year affordability period. HTF funds must be committed within 24 months of HUD's execution of the HTF grant Agreement.
structured_extraction.contact_email: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Community Development Administration, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, Maryland 20706
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and for-profit organizations developing affordable rental housing for extremely low-income (ELI) households, defined as households with incomes at the greater of 30% of Area Median Income (AMI) or at or below the poverty line. Projects must serve Maryland residents including families, seniors, and persons with disabilities or special needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development hard costs, acquisition costs, related soft costs, relocation costs, and operating/rental assistance. Eligible activities include production, preservation and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing through acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury housing. Operating costs include insurance, utilities, real property taxes, maintenance, and scheduled payments to reserves for replacement of major systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. All projects involving new construction must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) under Maryland's Smart Green and Growing Initiative, which includes all incorporated municipalities, areas between Baltimore and Washington beltways, Sustainable Communities, enterprise zones, areas designated by counties as PFAs, and certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas.
requirements_list: Market assessment demonstrating housing needs of ELI individuals and current demand for proposed units
Site control extending at least 180 calendar days after application date
Capital Needs Assessment for projects acquiring existing property
Phase I Environmental Site Assessment not more than one year old, including lead-based paint and asbestos testing for acquisition/rehabilitation projects
Evidence of public utilities availability (water, sewer, electric, gas, telephone, internet, cable)
Proper zoning for intended use; documentation of zoning change status if required
New construction projects must be in Priority Funding Areas with letter from local government certifying PFA location
Anticipated Development Schedule consistent with Department underwriting and construction review process

Underwriting Standards: minimum 5% vacancy rate, annual operating expenses $4,000-$7,000 per unit per year, minimum $300 per unit per year in reserves for replacement, operating reserves of 3-6 months of underwritten expenses, rent increases no more than 2% annually, operating expense increases at least 3% annually, minimum debt service coverage ratio of 1.15
Market Study prepared by independent professional with NCHMA peer review, not more than six months old, meeting HOME Rule requirements
Developer Experience: demonstrated accomplishment during past five years with similar projects, strong Primary Development Team (Developer/Owner, general contractor, architect, property manager)

Developer Financial Capacity: financial statements for three fiscal years prior to application plus interim statements, demonstrating sufficient working capital and net worth for project guarantees, access to sufficient working capital for pre-development and unexpected challenges
Demonstrated experience and capacity to own, construct, rehabilitate, manage and operate affordable multifamily rental housing
For projects with construction over $200,000 in federal funds: compliance with Section 3 requirements ensuring employment opportunities for low and very low income persons
30-year minimum affordability period
Compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental, zoning, and building code requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: HTF projects are selected by the Department for funding consideration subject to availability of funds. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and evaluated using Threshold Criteria. HTF funds are awarded through a non-competitive, first-ready first-served basis. Applications may be requested by a Sponsor as part of a project application, or Department staff may propose HTF funds during project review and underwriting in conjunction with other Department housing programs (RHFP, LIHTC, MBP, STHGP) or non-Department funding sources. HTF may not be used with funding sources that cannot be combined with HTF (e.g., Public Housing). All applications must contain a description of eligible activities to be conducted with HTF funds. Successful recipients receive a Notice of Award stating the Department's intent to award HTF funds. DHCD staff review all applicants to ensure compliance with minimum threshold requirements; applications not meeting all minimum threshold requirements will not be considered for financing.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Administration issues bonds to fund loans for business projects located in priority funding areas and traditionally underserved areas. Qualified business projects include acquisition and permanent financing of commercial and mixed-use real estate, refinancing of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects, and non-profit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation, and new construction. This program is distinct from the SSBCI-funded NBW programs and is funded through bond issuances by the CDA.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CDA-issued bonds fund loans for business projects including acquisition and permanent financing of commercial and mixed-use real estate, refinancing of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects, and non-profit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation, and new construction of facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and non-profit organizations with projects in priority funding areas and traditionally underserved areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, permanent financing, and refinancing of commercial and mixed-use real estate; non-profit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation, and new construction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in priority funding areas as defined in section 5-7B-02 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, and some projects in Sustainable Communities.
requirements_list: Project must be located in a priority funding area
Project must be acquired, owned, developed, constructed, reconstructed, rehabilitated or improved for the purposes of carrying on a business
For non-profits, the project must be a facility for occupancy and/or use by qualified nonprofit organizations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Community Development Administration for application procedures and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Assists small businesses with working capital and owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation through below-market-rate loans up to $5 million. Designed for businesses seeking new space or expansion opportunities, including mixed-use projects combining residential and commercial uses. Part of the SSBCI-funded NBW program suite.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $350,000 to $5,000,000 with flexible terms up to 30 years. SSBCI portion with up to 30% program match. Interest rate based on underwriting analysis. Requires private capital match of 4:1 (80-20) for non-SEDI/VSB or 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI/VSB, with minimum 1:1 match. Senior or junior debt available. Personal guarantees and collateral required. Application fee $250, closing fee $250. Applications are currently being accepted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses operating in Maryland with fewer than 500 employees. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI) who own or operate for-profit or nonprofit Maryland-based small businesses. Local governments are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation, mixed-use projects combining residential and commercial uses, machinery and equipment, working capital, and other costs associated with sustaining or expanding a small business in manufacturing, service, retail, office, or mixed-use sectors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located or to be located in a CDFI Investment area in Maryland.
requirements_list: Less than 500 employees
Proof of private capital match of at least 1:1
Target private capital to SSBCI funds match of 4:1 (80-20) for non-SEDI/VSB or 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI/VSB
Business located in CDFI Investment area
Business viability and positive neighborhood impact
Readiness to proceed
Adequate cash flow and collateral
Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees
Priority given to SEDI individuals who own or operate the business
For-profit or nonprofit Maryland-based small businesses as defined by U.S. Small Business Administration
Local governments are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete an SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks loan application package via the online portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication. Upon approval, applicants receive a commitment letter from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Loan approval requires meeting underwriting guidelines. Applicants must execute necessary legal documents prior to loan disbursement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) Loan to Lender Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides loans to Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) for relending to small businesses, with required private capital match. Focuses on businesses owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI), very small businesses (VSBs), and those in CDFI Investment Areas. The program is designed to catalyze loan capital availability for establishing and sustaining small businesses throughout Maryland. CDFIs serve as intermediaries, relending SSBCI funds combined with private capital to eligible small businesses.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CDFIs receive SSBCI Loans of $500,000 to $15,000,000 based on CDFI capacity. SSBCI Loans bear interest at 0%-2% with terms up to 7 years and annual renewal options thereafter. Initial proposal: 20% SSBCI funds and 80% private match capital for non-SEDI/non-VSB businesses; 30% SSBCI funds and 70% private match capital for SEDI and VSB businesses. Target private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI businesses or those with fewer than 10 employees, and 4:1 for non-SEDI businesses or those with 10 or more employees. Minimum required private capital match is 1:1. CDFIs must have 20% at risk. SSBCI funds can be in subordinate position to private capital. Risk of loss on each SBL is shared between DHCD and Lender on loan-by-loan basis with SSBCI portion in top loss position. CDFIs relend to small businesses (under $250,000 per loan unless prior written approval) for working capital, real estate acquisition down payments, minor renovations, machinery and equipment acquisition, and other business expansion costs. SBL terms: fixed rate, fixed payment loans up to 5 years (longer for asset acquisition); interest rates cannot exceed 18%; combined origination fee and points maximum 1%; application fee maximum $100; no prepayment penalties. CDFIs must begin making SBLs within 90 days of closing the SSBCI Loan. Applications processed on first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - SSBCI fund availability dependent
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) with CDFI certification that will relend to small businesses owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals and very small businesses in CDFI Investment Areas throughout Maryland. End borrowers include startups, newly established businesses, and growing businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: For CDFIs: Capital for relending to small businesses with required private capital match. For Small Business Loan Borrowers: Working capital, marketing/planning/feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payments, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment acquisition, and other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business. Ineligible uses include residential/transient living businesses, multifamily/single-family housing, nursing homes, assisted living facilities, community halls, fire stations, hospitals, colleges, universities, adult entertainment facilities, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, and tattoo parlors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: CDFIs operating in Maryland CDFI Investment Areas. Priority given to SBLs in CDFI Investment Areas. CDFIs must serve Maryland counties/cities as specified in their application. 34.46% of SSBCI funds must be expended on very small businesses and SEDI businesses combined.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) certified with demonstrated financial stability and good standing with the State and IRS

Must demonstrate experience administering small business loan programs including origination, credit and compliance underwriting, loan servicing, post-closing asset management, and compliance reporting
Must be able to leverage eligible required private capital as match to SSBCI funding (minimum 1:1 private to SSBCI match required; initial target 70-80% private match to 20-30% SSBCI funds)
Must demonstrate capacity to comply with SSBCI Statutes, Regulations, Policies, and DHCD requirements
Must be ready to provide adequate resources and staff to start making SBLs within 90 days of closing SSBCI Loan
Must be able to provide technical assistance to SBL Borrowers
Must demonstrate outreach capabilities to very small businesses (VSBs) and socially and economically disadvantaged individual (SEDI) led businesses or businesses in CDFI investment areas
End borrower businesses must be small businesses (fewer than 500 employees per SBA definition), retail, manufacturing, goods/services, home-based, or non-profit organizations
Individual SBLs cannot exceed $250,000 unless prior written DHCD approval obtained
SBL Borrower interest rates cannot exceed 18%
SBL terms cannot exceed 5 years unless for asset acquisition with longer useful life
No SBL prepayment penalties permitted
Combined SBL origination fee and points maximum: 1%
SBL application fee maximum: $100
Lender must not discriminate on basis of race, color, religion, sex, handicap, familial status, or national origin
Lender may not act as participant, have security interest, or be stakeholder in any SBL Borrowers
Lender must provide monthly, quarterly, and annual reports and annual audited financial statements
Lender must provide post-closing access to records for DHCD asset management and federal auditors
Lender must notify DHCD of changes in address or personnel affecting SBL service delivery
Lender must maintain compliance with all outstanding state liabilities

Ineligible SBL uses include residential/transient living businesses, multifamily/single-family housing, nursing homes, assisted living, crisis care, group homes, transitional housing, homeless shelters, community halls, fire stations, hospitals, colleges, universities, adult entertainment, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors
No outstanding liabilities with the State of Maryland (income taxes, sales taxes, payroll withholding taxes, unemployment taxes, or other penalties and fines)
Commitment to comply with non-discrimination requirements
Willingness to attend training sessions, peer networking meetings, and DHCD events
Capacity to submit monthly, quarterly and annual reports and annual audited financial statements
Ability to provide post-closing access to records for DHCD asset management and federal auditors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: CDFIs submit the SSBCI NBW Loan to Lender application (Appendix A) with required documentation to dhcd.ssbci@maryland.gov or by mail to 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Application must include: organization information, CDFI certification number, explanation of capacity and experience with small business lending, projected annual loan production for 6-year period, leverage and private capital terms explanation, evidence of financial stability and committed resources, description of lending program with demographic/geographic/industry targets, description of loan products and terms, reporting and audit capabilities, technical assistance plans, and documentation of any state liabilities. Applicants must provide most recent Annual Report, Annual Financial Statement, 501(c)(3) organizational documents, and last 3 years organization tax returns. Applications are processed on first-come, first-served basis pending SSBCI fund availability. Once approved, Lenders receive a commitment letter from DHCD reflecting total SSBCI Loan amount, required private capital match, and proposed SBL funding timetable. SSBCI Loans must be closed in accordance with terms and conditions provided by Maryland Attorney General. Draw down of SSBCI Loan can be in full at closing or via periodic draw requests; all draws must be properly matched with private capital at time of draw.

structured_extraction.program_description: A flexible loan program used by small businesses and lending partners to provide financing options during all phases of business growth. The program helps new and expanding small businesses and nonprofit organizations improve and revitalize existing commercial districts and town centers in targeted community revitalization areas throughout Maryland. Loans are available for construction, rehabilitation, expansion, machinery and equipment, working capital, and real estate acquisition.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct business loans and loan participations with lending partners. Loans up to $5 million with flexible terms up to 30 years. Interest rate determined by underwriting analysis. Applicant must contribute 10% cash. Personal guarantees required. Fees include $250 application fee, $250 closing fee, and 1% commitment fee.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based small businesses with 500 or fewer employees and nonprofit organizations seeking financing for commercial projects in targeted revitalization areas. New and expanding businesses are eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, rehabilitation, expansion or other construction, machinery and equipment, working capital, real estate acquisition, and other costs associated with opening, operating, or expanding a Maryland small business. Also supports revitalization of commercial districts and town centers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities, Priority Funding Areas, Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico counties, Transit-Oriented Development areas designated by the Maryland Department of Transportation, or BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zones.
requirements_list: Maryland-based small business with 500 or fewer employees or nonprofit organization

Project located in targeted geography (Sustainable Community, Priority Funding Area, Opportunity Zone in specific counties, Transit-Oriented Development area, or BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zone)
Demonstrate project viability and positive impact on neighborhood
Appropriate debt service levels
Sufficient collateral
Personal guarantee
Positive net operating income (NOI)
Strong business plan
10% applicant cash contribution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create an account or log in to the online Application Portal. Complete the application and pay a $250 application fee. For initial consultation, complete the Pre-Application Consultation Form and a team member will contact you.

structured_extraction.program_description: Dedicated to funding and growing the next generation of outstanding early-stage businesses in Maryland with high potential for job growth. Provides bridge financing for companies that have already raised equity from early-stage investors and are seeking additional capital to reach the next funding milestone. Supports businesses positioned to scale by providing venture debt or convertible notes on a pari passu basis with private capital match.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SSBCI funds provided on a pari passu basis with private capital match. Target SSBCI portion of venture debt is $500,000 to $2,500,000. Funding structure includes venture debt with repayment in principal and interest or convertible notes. SSBCI funds must be caused by and result in private capital match. Aggregate funding round less than $20,000,000. Typical bridge rounds are greater than $2,000,000. Minimum required private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 1:1; target matching private capital to SSBCI funds greater than 2:1. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and businesses owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage Maryland businesses with high potential for job growth, fewer than 500 employees, with existing paid-in capital over $2,000,000 or revenues over $1,000,000, that have already raised equity from early-stage investors and are positioned to scale. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and businesses owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge financing to support reaching the next equity raise milestone and business scaling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses operating in Maryland.
requirements_list: Less than 500 employees
Minimum required private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 1:1
Target matching private capital to SSBCI funds greater than 2:1
Existing paid-in capital greater than $2,000,000 or revenues greater than $1,000,000
Already raised equity from early-stage investors
High potential for job growth
Positioned to scale
In need of bridge financing to achieve milestones
Typical bridge rounds greater than $2,000,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should email dhcd.ssbci@maryland.gov to express interest and receive application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provided funding to local jurisdictions and their internet service provider partners to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas. The program was funded through the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 and aimed to deliver high-speed internet connectivity to residents and businesses in unserved Maryland communities. Program is now closed.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $50,000 to $500,000 covering 70% to 90% of eligible capital construction costs for broadband extension to unserved areas, depending on household density. Match requirement of 10% to 30% of capital construction costs based on density metrics (for wired: fewer than 8 households per mile = 10%, 8-15 households per mile = 20%, 15+ households per mile = 30%; for wireless: fewer than 40 households per tower = 10%, 40-70 households per tower = 20%, 70+ households per tower = 30%). Match may be comprised of cash contributions or, for ISP partners, in-kind capital construction costs. Local jurisdiction or ISP may own funded assets. Eligible uses include construction of facilities to deploy service at broadband speeds, middle mile infrastructure directly necessary for service delivery, and electronics necessary for service delivery including optical equipment, routers, switches, wireless radio equipment, and modems. Ineligible expenses include duplication of existing service, engineering design services, land or tower purchases, and operating expenses. Funding source is the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications were due on or before December 23, 2021. Program is closed; no longer accepting applications.

All equipment must be new and non-depreciated. Funds cannot be used for engineering design services (except limited tower structural exceptions), land or tower purchases, buildings, renovations, telephone or video service expenses not necessary for broadband delivery, or operating expenses.

Areas with past state grant funding ineligible

Match requirement: 10% to 30% of eligible capital construction costs based on household density metrics

Technology neutral: fiber optics, coax, fixed wireless (licensed or unlicensed), or other technologies meeting speed requirements acceptable
Local jurisdiction must have established partnership with ISP Partner prior to funding agreement
All equipment must be new and non-depreciated
Match must be available for each reimbursement request
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023
Project ownership by local jurisdiction or ISP Partner required
Applicant responsible for overall funding and implementation of project

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were submitted electronically as PDF to osb.md@maryland.gov by December 23, 2021. Required submission components included: (1) completed Grant Application Form; (2) executive summary; (3) application partnership statement naming ISP Partner; (4) experience statement; (5) network design and construction description; (6) subscriber profile with demographic data and projected take rate; (7) subscriber costs and service limitations; (8) detailed line-item capital construction budget; (9) implementation schedule with key milestones; (10) GIS shapefiles (.shp), KMZ, or KML files showing proposed funded service area and infrastructure; (11) certification from local jurisdiction applicant and ISP Partner. Awardees are strongly encouraged to enroll in the State of Maryland's Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) payment system for faster and more secure payment processing.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the DHCD Project Portal at https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/IGXLogin. To access the application, applicants must first register in the Portal system by selecting 'New User?' and completing the registration request form; approval may take up to 72 hours. First-time applicants to the Operating Assistance Grant Program should contact a project manager for eligibility verification and system access. New organizations should request access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. Applicants must ensure their organization profile includes all required documents before submitting their application. Applications missing required documents may be disqualified. TAG applications are evaluated using a single 5-point scoring scale that reflects the overall strength and readiness of the application. Scoring definitions are: 0 (Not Evident), 1 (Minimally Meets Expectations), 3 (Somewhat Meets Expectations), and 5 (Strongly Meets/Exemplary). Projects located in ENOUGH areas may receive up to 10 bonus points, and projects located in Just Communities areas will receive 10 bonus points. Review teams may conduct site visits and/or meetings with applicants prior to award decisions. Upon award notification, the project manager will draft the Award Agreement using a standard template and send a DocuSign envelope for signature. The authorized signatory must sign and return the agreement within five business days of receipt. Virtual training and step-by-step application guides are available in the DHCD Project Portal to assist applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project C.O.R.E. was a four-year partnership between Maryland State government and Baltimore City to demolish vacant buildings and catalyze redevelopment, reinvestment, and stabilization in Baltimore neighborhoods. The initiative provided funding for demolition, deconstruction, stabilization, and redevelopment activities in targeted Baltimore City neighborhoods, creating safer, healthier, and more attractive spaces for families to live. It aimed to improve economic opportunity and quality of life by creating safer neighborhoods, jobs, green space, and affordable housing. Targeted demolition sites were determined by Baltimore City in partnership with affected communities through the Vacants to Value program. The initiative also supported workforce development training programs and job creation through coordination with local trade organizations and non-profit organizations. Project C.O.R.E. has since evolved into the Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative (BVRI).

structured_extraction.program_description: Rental Housing Works provides gap financing (subordinate loans) to create jobs and strengthen the Maryland economy by supporting the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing. The program funds projects that use the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental Housing Works provides subordinate gap financing loans funded through State general obligation bonds. Loans are available up to $2.5 million per project (subject to waiver in certain circumstances). Standard loan terms include a 40-year amortization period with a 2% simple interest rate. Loan payments are limited to 75% of annual cash flow. Loans are due on sale, refinancing, any voluntary or involuntary property transfer, or upon an event of default. The program uses a Deed of Trust Note with Surplus Cash and Contingent Interest structure. During the construction loan period, no principal or interest payments are required. During the permanent loan period, borrowers make annual surplus cash payments equal to a specified percentage (typically 50% until developer fee is paid, then a lower percentage) applied to principal reduction. After principal repayment, contingent interest may be payable from surplus cash up to a maximum amount equal to annual simple interest at 4% on the outstanding balance. Upon a capital event (sale, refinancing, or transfer), payment is due equal to the lesser of the contingent interest percentage of borrower net proceeds or the outstanding debt plus contingent interest. Payments address accrued fees first, then principal, then contingent interest.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis in conjunction with a Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credit application. Applicants must submit a completed RHW Application Submission Package with required threshold documentation. Required documentation includes: completed CDA Form 202 clearly identifying RHW funds; written documentation of required zoning for use and density; certification that awards of any competitive public and private funding necessary for feasibility have been made; completed FTE Job Calculator showing full-time equivalent jobs to be created; and certification to the RHW Application Submission Package. The department tracks applications by date of receipt and reviews them in conjunction with Multifamily Bond Program applications. Applications are evaluated against threshold criteria; those that pass are scored using evaluation criteria. Projects passing scoring proceed to kick-off meetings where timelines and critical path schedules are distributed. Projects are funded on a first-ready, first-served basis. All funding awards must be approved by the Board of Public Works.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: DHCD awards Section 811 PRA funds to eligible multifamily rental properties (with at least 5 units) through a Cooperative Agreement with HUD. Eligible properties must have financing commitments from Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC), State Rental Housing Funds, HOME Investment Partnerships Act (HOME), or other federal, state, or local government programs. The program provides long-term project-based rental assistance payments to property owners to subsidize the contract rent of eligible units. Rental assistance payments equal the difference between the contract rent and the tenant rent paid by eligible residents. The Grantee or Contract Administrator makes rental assistance payments to the property owner on behalf of eligible tenants. Administrative costs are allowable at a rate of no more than 8% of the rental assistance grant amount. Assistance is permanent and ongoing for eligible tenants who maintain eligibility.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Housing projects that serve low-income adults with disabilities. Eligible residents are non-elderly adults with disabilities between ages 18 and 61 (below age 62 at selection) who have a qualifying disability, receive Medicaid, have a household income at or below 30% of the Area Median Income (AMI), and are referred by the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD). Priority populations include: (1) Institutionalized Medicaid recipients; (2) Households at risk of institutionalization due to current housing situation; (3) DDA Community Pathways Waiver participants, BHA Residential Rehabilitation Program participants, and Brain Injury waiver participants transitioning to independent renting; and (4) Homeless persons who are Medicaid recipients (prioritized by HEARTH Act definition). Also helps for-profit and non-profit sponsors of affordable rental housing developments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Project-based rental assistance to subsidize the contract rent of eligible units in approved rental housing for extremely low-income persons with disabilities. Funds support permanent supportive housing with access to community-based, long-term care services. Administrative costs for planning, infrastructure, technology, and program operation are also allowable.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Projects must be located in priority funding areas. Funding is anticipated to be distributed with approximately 75% of units in the Baltimore and Washington D.C. metropolitan areas and the remaining 25% on the Eastern Shore and Western Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must be multifamily rental properties with at least 5 housing units
Projects must receive financing commitments from LIHTC, State Rental Housing Funds, HOME, or other federal, state, or local government programs
Properties with existing use restrictions for persons with disabilities are not eligible unless PRA funds support other unrestricted units in the building
Existing units receiving project-based operating housing subsidy (Section 8 or similar) within 6 months prior are ineligible
Units with use agreements requiring housing for persons 62 or older are ineligible
Eligible residents must be between ages 18 and 61 (below 62 at selection)
Eligible residents must have a qualifying disability as defined in 42 U.S.C. § 8013(k)(2)
Eligible residents must receive Medicaid or be eligible for community-based, long-term care services through Medicaid waivers or state plan options
Eligible residents must have household income at or below 30% of the Area Median Income (AMI)
Eligible residents must be referred through the Inter-Agency Partnership Agreement process, typically by MDOD
Eligible residents must reside in the unit as their sole place of residence
Property owners must enter into a Rental Assistance Contract (RAC) with the Grantee
Annual income recertification is required for eligible tenants
Units must meet Decent, Safe, and Sanitary standards and Uniform Physical Condition Standards (UPCS)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: DHCD reviews applications from eligible multifamily housing properties seeking Section 811 PRA funding. DHCD meets with an Interagency Committee that includes representatives from the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD) and Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to evaluate projects that align with program goals and target populations. Once a project is selected through the competitive process, DHCD issues a Reservation Award Letter to the developer confirming that the property is eligible for funding. The Owner and Grantee then execute a Rental Assistance Contract (RAC) using HUD forms HUD-92235-PRA (Part I) and HUD-92237-PRA (Part II). Property managers are trained on program requirements, enrollment procedures, unit application processes, and transition planning. MDOD and MDH conduct outreach and referral to identify eligible residents and provide supportive services. Referred eligible residents must complete rental applications and pass screening in accordance with fair housing, criminal background, and credit requirements. Once approved, eligible tenants execute a lease (form HUD-92236-PRA) with the property owner. The Grantee makes ongoing rental assistance payments to the property owner based on the difference between contract rent and tenant rent. Annual recertification of tenant income and eligibility is required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides competitive grants and loans to anchor institutions (such as universities, hospitals, and cultural organizations) for community development and capital improvement projects in Sustainable Communities or areas of the state that have not received recent investment. The program aims to generate jobs, strengthen partnerships between anchor institutions and Maryland, and create safer, healthier, and more attractive communities. Projects must connect to community revitalization strategies and help achieve outcomes identified in community action plans.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides competitive grants and loans to anchor institutions for capital improvement projects, including community facilities, educational amenities, healthcare facilities, and other community development initiatives. Applicants must provide matching funds equal to the amount of financial assistance received (1:1 match requirement). Applications are submitted through the Project Portal after organization registration. The FY26 Application Round is closed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY26 Application Round is closed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anchor institutions, defined as institutions of higher education or hospital institutions in Maryland, as well as cultural organizations, seeking to support community revitalization. Hospital institutions must have at least five physicians organized as a medical staff, maintain facilities to provide diagnostic and treatment services, and admit or retain individuals for overnight care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvement and community development projects by anchor institutions, including community facilities, educational amenities, healthcare facilities, and other initiatives that further revitalization goals. Projects must be located within Sustainable Communities boundaries or areas of the state that have not received recent investment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Funds can only be used in Sustainable Communities or areas of the state that have not been invested in. Projects must be located within Sustainable Communities boundaries and help achieve outcomes identified in community action plans. Applicants should use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an anchor institution (institution of higher education, hospital institution, or cultural organization in Maryland)
Hospital institutions must have at least five physicians organized as a medical staff
Hospital institutions must maintain facilities to provide diagnostic and treatment services for two or more unrelated individuals under medical staff supervision
Hospital institutions must admit or retain individuals for overnight care
Applicants must provide matching funds equal to the amount of financial assistance received (1:1 match)
Projects must build an ongoing relationship between the anchor institution and the community
Projects must be located within Sustainable Communities boundaries and connect to community revitalization strategies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Project Portal after organization registration. The typical timeline includes training, application opening, organization registration cutoff, application closing, review period, and award announcement. For more information and application instructions, visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shelter and Transitional Housing Facilities Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides grants to improve or create transitional housing and emergency shelters by providing capital financing for emergency shelters and transitional housing facilities that provide housing and support services to households to prevent homelessness and assist households to be able to live independently. The purpose is to reduce homelessness in the State.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters with supportive services. Grant funds may cover up to one-half of total project costs, or under certain conditions up to 75 percent of total project costs. Eligible uses include: acquiring land and buildings; site preparation; cost of labor and materials for construction and rehabilitation; acquisition of machinery, equipment, and furnishings with at least 15-year life expectancy; architectural and engineering services; and real estate development fees. Grant funds may be used for the cost of acquiring land and buildings; necessary studies, surveys, plans, specifications, appraisals, compaction tests, test borings, construction cost estimates and environmental impact reports; site preparation; cost of labor and materials for construction, rehabilitation, and installation of improvements; acquisition of necessary machinery, equipment, and furnishings installed at the project; and fees and premiums normally incurred in real estate development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and local governments that serve homeless or at-risk individuals and households
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters with supportive services. Eligible project activities include acquiring land and buildings, site preparation, architectural/engineering services, construction, relocation, renovation, restoration, site development and improvements, utilities, and equipment and furnishings with at least 15-year life expectancy. Funds may not be used for operating assistance, refinancing existing debt, maintenance, or replacing furnishings in existing facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Local government letters of support are required for all projects. All projects involving new construction must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA), which includes all incorporated municipalities (including Baltimore City), areas between the Baltimore and Washington DC beltways, Sustainable Communities, Federal and State enterprise zones, and areas designated by county governments as PFAs.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or local government
Residents must be homeless or in danger of becoming homeless individuals and households
Sponsors must maintain the project as transitional housing or emergency shelter for a term of 15 years
If use is discontinued prior to 15 years, the grant becomes repayable
Local government letters of support are required for all projects
All projects involving new construction must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA)
Applicants must identify the homeless target population they expect to serve and continue to serve designated population(s) throughout the 15-year funding term
Supportive services must be specifically oriented to meeting the needs of the homeless target population
Applicants must submit copies of commitment letters, agreements or other documents identifying the sources of funding for the services to be provided
A plan outlining funding sources for services and operating expenses during the term of the project is required at time of application
Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs) should be solicited and hired for all contracts (State goal of at least 29% MBE participation)
Maryland resident businesses should be solicited and hired to design and construct grant projects
LEED building technologies are encouraged for construction and renovation
Maryland Historical Trust must complete review before State will disburse funds; applicants must contact the Trust early enough to allow adequate time to resolve any historic-preservation concerns
Any roof purchased with State funds must have at least a 20-year, no-dollar-limit warranty
Roofing projects must comply with State roofing policy
No project funds may be used to further sectarian religious instruction or in connection with sectarian religious buildings or programs
Forest Conservation Program applies to construction activities on land greater than 40,000 square feet
Must comply with State debarment requirements and not use debarred businesses

Equipment and furnishings must have a life expectancy of at least 15 years with normal maintenance, be unlikely to become technically obsolete for 15 years, be of durable construction, and not be elaborate or extravagant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Housing Development Programs office at (301) 429-7854 or 1-800-543-4505 or consult the Shelter and Transitional Housing Grant Program Guidebook for detailed application procedures. Applications must meet threshold requirements and will undergo processing including underwriting and construction review. The Department will evaluate applications for viability and review commitment letters. The Maryland Department of Human Resources' Office of Transitional Services or Department of Health Office of Health Care Quality will review the adequacy of proposed supportive services. Processing time and specific deadlines are available upon contact with the program office.

structured_extraction.program_name: Single Family Housing Revenue Bonds (2009 Parity Indenture)
structured_extraction.program_description: Single Family Housing Revenue Bonds issued under a parity indenture created in December 2009 to finance primarily single-family housing. This indenture was created as a result of the U.S. Treasury's New Issue Bond Program. Single-family loans are credit enhanced by FHA, VA, and USDA/RD (RHS). Bonds are issued as taxable, variable rate until proceeds are drawn and converted to tax-exempt fixed rate when new single-family homes are financed.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bonds finance single-family housing with credit enhancement by FHA, VA, and USDA/RD (RHS). Bonds are issued as taxable, variable rate until proceeds are drawn and converted to tax-exempt fixed rate when new single-family homes are financed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family homebuyers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financing of single-family homes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide
requirements_list: Single-family housing projects
Loans must be credit enhanced by FHA, VA, or USDA/RD
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Community Development Administration for application procedures

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to preserve and improve single-family properties by bringing them up to applicable building codes and standards or meeting minimum housing quality standards. The program helps address critical health and safety issues in owner-occupied homes and is targeted to jurisdictions not served by other Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development rehabilitation financing programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent to 6% interest loans with terms up to 30 years. Maximum loan amount is generally $50,000. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage. Interest rates are based on applicant income and ability to repay. Loans serving families with incomes at or below 50 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may have deferred payments if necessary for project feasibility. Household income of owner-occupants generally cannot exceed 80 percent of the statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income limits, though some loans may be made to families with incomes up to 80 percent if they have circumstances making them ineligible for other Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development financing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes with low to moderate household incomes seeking to address critical health and safety repairs. Program is generally not available in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Prince George's County, or Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical health and safety repairs to owner-occupied single-family homes including mold remediation, gas leaks, roof repair and replacement, asbestos abatement, lead abatement, combustion appliance repair and replacement, chimney repair, foundation and sub-space waterproofing, radon mitigation, electrical hazards and upgrades, plumbing issues, water and well repairs, septic and sewer issues, windows and doors (for health/safety, water intrusion, and security), structural repair, accessibility modifications for disabled and seniors, fall and injury prevention measures, ductwork upgrades, building shell stabilization, and pest treatments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is generally not available in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Prince George's County, or Montgomery County. Available in most other Maryland jurisdictions where participating local governments administer the program.
requirements_list: Owner-occupied single-family home as primary residence
Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
Property must be within jurisdiction of participating local government
Licensed Maryland contractor with current MHIC or trade license required
Contractor must provide Certificate of Liability Insurance with per occurrence limits of $1 million or greater
Contractor must provide Letter of Good Standing
Bid must include photographs documenting critical repairs
Bid should not be more than 60 days old
Total cost of all bids should not exceed $50,000
Critical repairs must address health and safety issues or building code violations
For loans exceeding $5,000 or with deferred payments, property will be secured by mortgage
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain bids from at least one licensed Maryland Home Improvement contractor or trade professional for critical repairs needed. 2. Compile required documentation including proof of home ownership (deed and current mortgage statement), photo ID, property tax bill, homeowners insurance declaration page, income verification documents (recent paystubs, 2 years tax returns, bank statements), contractor bids with photographs, and contractor credentials (MHIC license, insurance certificate, Letter of Good Standing, W-9). 3. Complete the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program application form with applicant information, income details, housing expenses, assets, liabilities, and demographic data. 4. Submit completed application and all supporting documentation to Special Loan Programs via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 5. Application will be processed by Special Loan Programs; all loan requests for properties within participating local government jurisdictions are processed directly by those local governments.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Strategic Demolition Fund catalyzes activities that accelerate economic development and job production in existing Maryland communities. The fund aims to improve the economic viability of greyfield development—redeveloping existing developed land—which often faces more barriers than sprawling greenfield development. It supports demolition of vacant and blighted properties as part of Maryland's state revitalization efforts, with projects required to be located within Sustainable Communities boundaries or qualifying Opportunity Zones. Funding is limited and focuses on high-impact projects.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital project funding provided through competitive grant applications for strategic demolition and site development projects. Funds support eligible demolition and site development projects, with awards focusing on projects that can have high economic and revitalization impact in their existing communities. Projects must be located within Sustainable Communities boundaries or Opportunity Zones in qualifying counties and contribute to revitalization goals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY26 Application Round is closed; typically annual
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and nonprofit community development organizations working outside of Baltimore City seeking to support greyfield redevelopment, as well as communities seeking to address vacant, blighted, or underutilized properties through strategic demolition.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for: demolition of derelict non-contributing structures; site acquisition and assembly to create redevelopment-sized parcels; site development; and construction-level architectural and engineering designs that support community revitalization goals and contribute to neighborhood improvement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the boundaries of a Sustainable Community and help achieve outcomes identified in that community's Sustainable Communities Action Plan, or within Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties (outside Baltimore City). Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility.
requirements_list: Lead applicants must be local governments working outside of Baltimore City or nonprofit community development organizations working outside of Baltimore City
Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities outside Baltimore City or Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties
Projects must focus on demolition of derelict structures or site development for redevelopment potential
Projects must contribute to revitalization goals and outcomes identified in the relevant Sustainable Communities Action Plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Project Portal after organization registration. The typical timeline includes training, application opening, organization registration cutoff, application closing, review period, and award announcement. For more information and application instructions, refer to the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Sustainable Communities Program provides a geographic designation for local areas to support community development, revitalization, and sustainability through coordinated strategies. It gives local governments resources to improve older communities and promote growth that is environmentally, economically, and socially responsible. The program combines resources for historic preservation, housing, and economic development under a single designation, focusing on infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, and development that strengthens existing communities. Once designated, communities gain access to an interagency revitalization toolbox of financing programs and tax credit incentives administered by multiple state agencies including the Departments of Housing and Community Development, Commerce, Planning, Environment, and Transportation.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides a geographic designation valid for five years that makes communities eligible to apply for certain state programs and incentives including: Community Legacy Program (capital funding for business retention/attraction, homeownership encouragement, commercial revitalization); Neighborhood BusinessWorks (gap financing for small businesses and nonprofits); Strategic Demolition Fund (grants for predevelopment, demolition, and land assembly); Operating Assistance Grants (grants for operating and technical assistance costs); National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund (for grey field development in the National Capital region); Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Program (grants and loans to anchor institutions for community development); Main Street Maryland Program (technical assistance, training, planning, architectural design, historic preservation assistance, and specialized training on commercial revitalization); Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (additional place-based revitalization investments for inner beltway communities); Maryland Façade Improvement Program (funds for commercial property exterior improvements); Job Creation Tax Credit (enhanced credits up to $5,000 per job with lower job creation thresholds of 25 jobs instead of 60); Enhanced Local Tax Increment Financing Authority (expanded permitted uses for historic preservation, environmental remediation, demolition, parking, schools, and affordable housing); Low Income Housing Tax Credit (additional points in Community Context category); Sustainable Maryland Certified (20 points toward certification); Water Quality Financing Administration Programs (below-market interest rate loans and grants); State Highway Administration Programs (transportation alternatives and safe routes to school); Sidewalk Retrofit Program; and Kim Lamphier Bikeways Network Program (additional points for projects in Sustainable Communities).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing (Five-year designation period)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (municipal or county) and community development organizations seeking to revitalize and strengthen their communities through coordinated state investment and sustainable development practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The designation unlocks access to state funding and incentives for community development, revitalization, historic preservation, housing and economic development, infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation projects, business retention and attraction, commercial revitalization, streetscape improvements, mixed-use development, water quality improvements, environmental remediation, and strengthening of existing commercial districts and residential communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All proposed Sustainable Communities Area applications must be located entirely within a Priority Funding Area and near or within a town center or transportation center. Eligible areas are distributed across all Maryland counties. For State Designated TOD Areas approved after 2023, the area must contain planning elements satisfying State Revitalization Programs requirements. For TOD Areas approved before 2023, they must have an approved Sustainable Community Action Plan or update TOD applications.
requirements_list: Entire area must be within a Priority Funding Area
Proposed community should be within or near a town center or transportation center
Must show financial need for local revitalization including support for nonprofit organizations, strengthening older commercial districts and residential communities, and improving public amenities
Must have a defined geographic area with an existing built environment that needs revitalization or additional state investment
Must submit a Sustainable Community Action Plan summarizing key initiatives and projects
Must have a local government resolution supporting both the boundary designation and Action Plan
Designation is valid for five years
For State Designated TOD Areas approved after 2023: must contain planning elements satisfying State Revitalization Programs requirements
For TOD Areas approved before 2023: must have approved Sustainable Community Action Plan or update TOD applications
For Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI) eligibility, must submit a separate revitalization plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, request an application template by sending an email to Tynan Stevenson with the subject line including 'Sustainable Communities [New Designation or Renewal] Application,' community name, and sponsoring jurisdiction. Note that for new designations, you must have a meeting with program staff before applying. Then submit an application that includes a defined geographic area, a Sustainable Community Action Plan consistent with existing community or comprehensive plans, and a local government resolution. An interagency panel led by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development reviews the application. The panel presents the application to the Governor's Smart Growth Subcabinet for final approval. Once approved, the designation is valid for five years.
