structured_extraction.program_name: UPLIFT (Utilizing Progressive Lending Investments to Finance Transformation)
structured_extraction.program_description: A public-private partnership program that increases homeownership opportunities in underserved areas affected by redlining by covering the appraisal gap—the difference between the cost to develop a property and its market sale price. The program accelerates the pace of development, construction, and sale of quality affordable housing in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities to help close the appraisal gap that occurs in historically redlined communities. It aims to increase property values, create homeownership opportunities, and build wealth for families.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State covers the difference between the cost to build and the sale price (the appraisal gap) through UPLIFT funding. Selected qualified development teams acquire, develop, build, and sell quality affordable housing in targeted neighborhoods using a combination of public and private financing. Homebuyers acquire fee simple title using a combination of down payment, down payment assistance, first mortgage loan (Maryland Mortgage Program or other source), other acceptable subsidy support, and a soft promissory note with the Department. A $1,000 non-refundable application fee is required per project. Additional fees may include an origination fee and a closing fee as the project progresses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit developers and builders engaged in developing affordable housing in historically redlined communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds cover the appraisal gap to enable development, construction, and sale of quality affordable housing in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities. The appraisal gap is the difference between total eligible development costs and the price the property can be sold for in the market. Funds help with costs to acquire, develop, build, and sell affordable homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Qualified areas include low-income census tracts (where 50 percent of households have incomes below 60 percent of the Area Median Income or have a poverty rate of 25 percent or more) and designated Sustainable Communities. Refer to the UPLIFT Qualified Areas Map for specific eligible locations. New Construction projects are not to be located in FEMA Flood Zone Areas, though waivers may be requested with appropriate documentation.
requirements_list: Project must be located in a Low-Income Census Tract and a designated Maryland Sustainable Community
Development teams must be qualified and selected with determinative or controlling position held by Lead Developer
Projects must meet Design and Construction Standards established by UPLIFT
Applicants must submit a pre-application meeting request and complete the meeting before submitting a formal application
Applicant must complete the UPLIFT Electronic Application Submission Request Form after pre-application meeting
Must comply with program application requirements and submission procedures
Must pay $1,000 non-refundable application fee per project
Development team must demonstrate comparable experience in significantly scaled projects
All corporations, LLCs, or limited partnerships must submit audited, reviewed, or compiled financial statements
Primary Development Team includes developer, general contractor/builder, architect, Neighborhood Engagement Facilitator, and marketing and sales entity
Projects must include newly constructed or formerly vacant structures that will be substantially rehabilitated
Developer must have acceptable credit history and current financial capacity to execute the project
Projects must comply with all applicable State and local building codes
Environmental assessments and site control documentation required
New Construction projects in FEMA Flood Zones require waiver requests with engineer documentation or flood mitigation plans
Applicants must submit both an electronic and a physical hard copy of the application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 0: Review the UPLIFT Program Guide and compile project details, timelines, and plans. Schedule and complete a Pre-Application Meeting and submit required pre-application materials at least two business days before the meeting. Step 1: Complete the UPLIFT Electronic Application Submission Request Form. Upon DHCD's internal review, applicants receive access to a Dropbox folder for application submission. Step 2: Download the Application Documents Package from the UPLIFT website. Step 3: Complete each section of the application including narratives, certifications, development information, and financials. Step 4: Pay the $1,000 non-refundable fee per project and upload proof of payment to Dropbox. Step 5: Create a free Dropbox account and upload all application documents to their respective folders by clicking the blue 'Join folder' button. Step 6: Sign and upload the Final Submission Checklist and deliver hard copy to DHCD's office at 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Step 7: DHCD conducts threshold review and evaluation scoring of eligible projects. Step 8: If approved, project enters underwriting pipeline for feasibility assessment. Step 9: Upon underwriting approval, Secretary issues commitment letter authorizing resource deployment. Step 10: Initial financing closing and Notice to Proceed issued to builder. Step 11: Construction Kick-off Meeting held to coordinate construction phase processes, marketing, and occupancy requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's largest residential energy conservation program that helps income-eligible homeowners and renters reduce heating and cooling costs through energy-conservation measures while addressing health and safety issues in their homes. The program installs energy conservation materials and improvements including home energy audits, blower door air infiltration reduction, insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofit, furnace cleaning, tuning, repairs, and replacement. Priority is given to the elderly, persons with disabilities, and families with children.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free energy conservation services delivered through local weatherization agencies at no cost to eligible participants. Services include home energy audits, blower door air infiltration reduction, insulation installation in attics, floors and walls, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofit, furnace cleaning, tuning, repairs and replacement, and health and safety improvements. Funds may also be used for Weatherization Readiness to address deferral conditions such as structural repairs, sewage problems, electrical red-tagged equipment, moisture or drainage issues, mold, and pest infestation before weatherization services can proceed. Program funding includes DOE Weatherization Assistance Program Formula funds, DOE Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (BIL) funds, EmPOWER Maryland Weatherization funds, and Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) funds. In the 2024-2025 program year, Maryland expects to serve 278 units under the DOE formula with an average cost per unit of $7,496.27.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible homeowners and renters in Maryland who meet household income requirements or participate in qualifying assistance programs. Priority given to applicants over age 60, those with disabilities, those with children in the home, and households with high energy usage or energy burden.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy conservation improvements to reduce heating and cooling costs, including blower door air infiltration reduction, insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofit, furnace repairs and replacement, and health and safety items. Funds may also be used for Weatherization Readiness to address deferral conditions such as structural repairs, sewage problems, electrical red-tagged equipment, moisture or drainage issues, mold, and pest infestation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland coverage through local weatherization agencies serving all 24 counties plus Baltimore City. Local Weatherization Agencies include: Allegany County HRDC; Baltimore City DHCD; Community Action Council of Howard County; Frederick Community Action Agency; Garrett County Community Action Committee; Housing Authority of St. Mary's County; Maryland Rural Development Corporation; and Shore Up! Inc.
requirements_list: Household income must be at or below 60% of State Median Income (SMI) or 200% Federal Poverty Level (FPL), whichever is higher
Automatically income-eligible if currently receiving Utility Bill Pay Assistance through Office of Home Energy Programs, SNAP, TANF, SSI, or HUD housing assistance programs
Priority given to applicants over age 60, those with disabilities, those with children in the home, and households with high energy usage or energy burden
All weatherization workers must have EPA Lead Renovation, Repair and Painting (LRRP) certification
All weatherization workers must have OSHA 10-hour Construction Safety certification
All weatherization workers must have Asbestos Awareness training
Weatherization installers must have Building Performance Institute (BPI) HEP Retrofit Installer Technician training or equivalent skills
Crew leaders must have BPI HEP Crew Leader training or equivalent skills
Energy auditors must have BPI HEP Energy Auditor certification
Quality Control Inspectors must have BPI HEP Quality Control Inspector certification
Other trades must hold valid Maryland licenses or certifications as required for the work being performed
HVAC equipment installers and removers must hold valid EPA-approved section 608 type I or universal refrigerant certification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Local Weatherization Agency (LWA) for your county to submit an application. The LWA will conduct outreach and accept applications from eligible households. Once an application is submitted, the LWA reviews it and verifies income eligibility. If eligible, the applicant is certified and scheduled for an energy audit within 30 days of certification. During the audit, the LWA identifies energy conservation opportunities and models a package of feasible improvements. A work order is prepared detailing weatherization services to be provided. Permits are obtained as required. Work is completed according to program requirements and the SWS-aligned Maryland Field Guide. Upon completion, a certified quality control inspector performs 100% inspection of completed work. DHCD inspects a minimum of 10% of completed units for quality assurance. Occupant education is provided to maximize energy savings. Alternatively, complete an interest form or application through DHCD; upon confirmation of eligibility, receive a letter with an assigned contractor and contact the contractor to schedule an in-home energy assessment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to provide financial stability to child care providers in Maryland during the pandemic recovery period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Round 1 of the Child Care Stabilization Grant program providing financial assistance to child care facilities for stabilization purposes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers and child care facilities in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To support the stabilization and operations of child care programs during pandemic recovery
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all licensed child care programs in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funded by the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 that provides financial assistance to existing child care providers in Maryland to help them stabilize their operations and remain open. The program distributes approximately $128 million in funding to eligible child care providers throughout Maryland, including licensed family child care homes, large family child care homes, child care centers, and education programs under a Letter of Compliance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded as a $10,000 base award to each eligible child care provider, plus additional per-licensed slot funding up to $126 for specific criteria including infants served, toddlers served, enrollment in the Child Care Scholarship program, participation in Maryland EXCELS program (rating 1-5), or location in a census tract with Social Vulnerability Index greater than 0.6. Funds do not have to be repaid as long as providers meet required certifications. The grants are taxable income. Allowable uses include: personnel costs and benefits, rent or mortgage payments, utilities, facilities maintenance and improvements, insurance, personal protective equipment, cleaning and sanitation supplies and services, health and safety training, equipment and supplies to respond to COVID-19, goods and services necessary to maintain or resume child care services, and behavioral health supports for children and employees.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 23, 2022 by 6:00pm (EST) CLOSED
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed family child care homes, large family child care homes, child care centers, and education programs under a Letter of Compliance that are currently operating throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel costs and benefits (including owner pay, employee wages, benefits, premium pay, bonuses, and vaccine-related costs), rent or mortgage payments, utilities, facilities maintenance and improvements, insurance, personal protective equipment, cleaning and sanitation supplies and services, health and safety training, equipment and supplies to respond to COVID-19 (including computers, software, thermometers), goods and services necessary to maintain or resume child care services (including food, diapers, toys, learning materials, licensing fees), and behavioral health supports for children and employees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all licensed child care providers throughout Maryland who meet eligibility requirements.
requirements_list: Must be an existing child care program currently operating (not a start-up)
Must be a family child care home, large family child care home, child care center, or education program under a Letter of Compliance
Must meet one criteria from each eligibility column as specified in the program guidelines
Head Start and Early Head Start programs are not eligible
Applicants with multiple child care locations must submit separate applications for each site
Must submit application online through the provided survey link
Must comply with all required certifications throughout the grant term
Must certify implementation of health and safety policies in line with Maryland guidance and CDC guidance to the greatest extent possible
Must maintain at least the same weekly wages and benefits for all employees throughout the grant period and not furlough employees from application submission through the grant period
Must provide relief from copayments and tuition payments for enrolled families to the extent possible, prioritizing families struggling to make payments

Must keep all documents and records related to the child care business stabilization grant, including communications of health and safety protocols, employee payroll records, benefits documentation, and family payment records
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers submitted online applications through a SurveyMonkey link. The application window opened January 3, 2022 and closed January 23, 2022 at 6:00pm EST. Applicants were required to gather documentation including verification of licensed child care slots, enrollment data, and other required information. MSDE offered virtual support sessions to help providers complete applications. Scanned copies, faxes, or printed applications were not accepted. Applications received by the deadline were reviewed to determine eligibility and completeness. MSDE representatives contacted applicants if applications were incomplete or additional information was required.

structured_extraction.program_name: 2022 Equipment Assistance Grants for National School Lunch Program (NSLP) Operator
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant provides funds for National School Lunch Program operators to purchase equipment to serve healthier school meals, improve food safety, and expand access to school meals. Equipment requests may include new equipment, renovation of equipment, or replacement of equipment. Individual items must have a value greater than $1,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants totaling $954,126 for the 2022 funding year to purchase equipment with a value greater than $1,000 per item to serve healthier school meals, improve food safety, and expand meal access. Equipment can be new, renovated, or replacement items. Costs incurred before grant approval cannot be funded. The grant operates in two phases: Phase 1 from October 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024, and Phase 2 (reallocation) from July 1, 2024 through September 30, 2024. Awards are made within 30 days of the application deadline.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, February 1, 2023. No later than 5:00 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: National School Lunch Program operators in Maryland schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of food service equipment to serve healthier school meals, improve food safety, and expand access to school meals. Equipment requests may include new equipment, renovation of equipment, or replacement of equipment. All individual items must have a value greater than $1,000.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland schools
requirements_list: Equipment items must have a value greater than $1,000 each
Costs incurred prior to grant approval cannot be funded
High-needs schools with 50 percent or more of enrolled students eligible for free or reduced-price meals receive priority
Schools that have not previously received an NSLP Equipment Grant receive priority
Applicants must consider meaningful impacts on nutrition and quality of meals
Applicants must demonstrate strategies for adopting lunchroom changes that provide convenience and appeal to students
Age of food service equipment or lack of appropriate items is considered
Availability of existing State and local funding for equipment purchases is considered

Programs and projects must operate in compliance with STATE and federal statutes and regulations, including the 1964 Civil Rights Act, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 34, Elementary and Secondary Education Act, EDGAR, GEPA, and Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)
Facilities must be accessible to individuals with disabilities as required by the ADA
Grantee must comply with Federal Executive Order 12549 regarding Debarment and Suspension
Grantee must establish and maintain fiscal control and fund accounting procedures per 2 CFR 200
Grantee must retain all financial records for five years or longer if required by federal regulation
Entities expending federal funds of $750,000 or more in a single fiscal year must have an annual financial and compliance audit per 2 CFR 200.500 et seq.
Grantee must adhere to MSDE reporting requirements and submit all required reports
Grantee must receive prior written approval from MSDE Program Monitor before implementing programmatic changes
Budget realignments of $1,000 or 15% of total object must be submitted at least 45 days prior to end of grant period
Requests for grant extension must be submitted at least 45 days prior to end of grant period
Web-based or technology instructional products must comply with Section 508 of the Federal Rehabilitation Act and Section 7-910 of the Education Article, Annotated Code of Maryland
Grantee must repay any misspent or misapplied funds identified through audit
Phase 1 awardees must complete all spending and submit final reports no later than June 30, 2024
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application was released on December 26, 2022 on the MSDE Grants webpage. Interested applicants can attend virtual customer service support sessions held on January 9, 2023 and January 18, 2023 to review application requirements and ask questions. The Grant Information Guide (GIG) provides an overview of all details associated with the grant and serves as a guide for completing the application. Key application requirements include Goals, Measurable Outcomes, Evidence of Impact, Plan of Operation, Key Personnel, and Project Timeline. Submit completed applications no later than 5:00 p.m. EST on Wednesday, February 1, 2023. Awards are made within 30 days of the application deadline, with NOGAs (Notices of Grant Awards) to follow the notification. Questions can be directed to Sara Brandt at sara.brandt@maryland.gov or 410-767-0201.

structured_extraction.program_name: Accreditation Support Fund - Maryland Program Accreditation
structured_extraction.program_description: Assists licensed child care centers and school-age only programs with the cost of instructional materials and resources needed to pursue Maryland Accreditation, which demonstrates a high level of quality through a rigorous self-assessment and program improvement process. Programs are reimbursed for classroom learning materials purchased while actively pursuing Maryland Accreditation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides reimbursement for instructional materials and classroom learning resources associated with pursuing Maryland Accreditation. Maximum reimbursement amounts: $2,500 for programs serving 100 or fewer children; $3,000 for programs serving more than 100 children. Reimbursable items include books, puppets, blocks, puzzles, rhythm instruments, dramatic play props, technology equipment, language and literacy materials, discovery and science materials, physical development items, music materials, and other non-consumable classroom learning materials. Consumable items such as paint, crayons, markers, glue, and paper are not reimbursable. Reimbursement covers only items purchased within 12 months prior to the application date. Funds cannot be used for facility improvements, association membership fees, staff training, accreditation fees, or costs already paid through another funding source. Each child care center with an individual license number can apply separately.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and school-age only programs pursuing Maryland program accreditation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Instructional materials and classroom learning materials associated with pursuing Maryland Accreditation, including books, puppets, blocks, puzzles, rhythm instruments, dramatic play props, technology equipment, science materials, and other non-consumable learning resources. Does not cover consumable items, accreditation fees, facility improvement, association membership fees, staff training, or costs covered by another funding source.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center or school-age only program
Must be pursuing Maryland program accreditation
Each facility must have an individual license number to apply (each site with an individual license can apply separately)
Must submit receipts and invoices for purchased materials
Purchases must be within 12 months prior to application date
Consumable items (paint, crayons, markers, glue, paper, etc.) are not reimbursable
Cannot use funds for facility improvements, association membership fees, staff training, accreditation fees, or costs already covered by another funding source
Maximum reimbursement: $2,500 for programs serving 100 or fewer children; $3,000 for programs serving more than 100 children
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the Application for Maryland Accreditation Support form online through the Maryland OneStop portal at onestop.md.gov. 2. Use the Infants and Toddlers Classroom Materials Checklist or Preschool and School-Age Classroom Learning Materials Checklist to identify eligible reimbursable items. 3. Complete a separate form for each vendor and attach receipts/invoices for all purchases. 4. Submit the completed application through the online portal. 5. The MSDE Accreditation Specialist will review the application, notify the applicant of any missing documentation, and process the application for payment. Approval time is typically 10–30 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Assists licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers, and school-age only programs with the cost of pursuing national accreditation by covering required application fees for initial applications, renewal applications, and annual updates through MSDE-recognized accrediting organizations. Awards are paid directly to the accrediting organization on behalf of the applicant.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program covers required application fees for national accreditation through MSDE-recognized accrediting organizations, including: American Montessori Society (AMS), Association Montessori International/USA (AMI/USA), Association of Independent Maryland Schools (AIMS), Association of Waldorf Schools of North America (AWSNA), Cognia Early Learning Accreditation, Council on Accreditation – After-School Accreditation (COA/ASA), Lumen Accreditation, Maryland Accreditation (MSDE), Middle States Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Elementary and Secondary Schools (MSA-CESS), National Accreditation Commission (NAC), National Association for the Education of Young Children (NAEYC), National Association for Family Child Care (NAFCC), and National Early Childhood Program Accreditation (NECPA). Eligible costs include initial application fees, renewal application fees, and annual update fees. The assistance cannot exceed the fee charged by the accreditation organization. Awards are paid directly to the accrediting organization on behalf of the applicant. Funds cannot be used for facility improvements, association membership fees, staff training, or costs already paid through another funding source.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers, and school-age only programs in Maryland seeking national accreditation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Required application fees for national accreditation including initial application, renewal application, and annual update fees from MSDE-recognized accrediting organizations. Cannot be used for facility improvement, association membership fees, staff training, or costs paid through another funding source.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center, registered family child care provider, or school-age only program

Must be pursuing accreditation through a MSDE-recognized accrediting organization (AMS, AMI/USA, AIMS, AWSNA, Cognia Early Learning Accreditation, COA/ASA, Lumen Accreditation, Maryland Accreditation, MSA-CESS, NAC, NAEYC, NAFCC, or NECPA)
Must submit a completed application submitted to the accrediting organization
Must submit a completed Accreditation Work Plan based on steps to achieve accreditation
Must submit a copy of the accrediting organization's fee page
Must submit a copy of current accreditation certificate if currently accredited
Award amount cannot exceed the fee charged by the accreditation organization
Cannot use funds for facility improvements, association membership fees, staff training, or costs already covered by another funding source
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the Application for National Accreditation Support online through the Maryland OneStop portal at onestop.md.gov. 2. Upload required documentation including: completed application submitted to the accrediting organization, completed Accreditation Work Plan, copy of the accrediting organization's fee page, and copy of current accreditation certificate if applicable. 3. Submit the application. Within 30 days of submission, MSDE will review the application and notify the applicant of approval status via email. If approved, payment will be processed directly to the accrediting organization.

structured_extraction.program_name: Administrative Review Training for School Meals Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: An online course designed to prepare local education agencies for the Administrative Review of their School Meals Programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Online training course that prepares local education agencies for administrative review of their School Meals Programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies administering School Meals Programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and preparation for administrative review compliance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland school districts.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Online course enrollment through Maryland State Department of Education.

structured_extraction.program_name: Afterschool Meals Program (NSLP Snacks + CACFP Snacks/Suppers)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial reimbursement to help eligible organizations serve snacks and/or suppers to children in afterschool care programs through two federal programs: (1) the National School Lunch Program, which reimburses school districts for serving snacks to children in supervised afterschool programs providing educational or enrichment activities; and (2) the Child and Adult Care Food Program, which reimburses school-based, non-profit, and non-school-based organizations for serving healthy snacks and/or suppers to children in area-eligible afterschool care programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial reimbursement through USDA programs for serving snacks and/or suppers to children in afterschool programs. Under the NSLP component, school districts participating in the National School Lunch Program are reimbursed for snacks. Under the CACFP component, eligible organizations (school-based, non-profit, or other) are reimbursed for healthy snacks and/or suppers in area-eligible programs. All participating programs must provide supervised educational or enrichment activities. Call 410-767-0199 to speak with OSCNP staff to determine eligibility and participation requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School districts, school-based programs, non-profits, and other organizations operating afterschool care programs serving children
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Serving snacks and/or suppers to children in supervised afterschool programs providing educational or enrichment activities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to school districts participating in the National School Lunch Program and area-eligible organizations throughout Maryland
requirements_list: For NSLP component: school district must be participating in the National School Lunch Program
For CACFP component: program must be area eligible
Afterschool program must provide educational or enrichment activities
Afterschool program must be supervised
Organization must be school-based, non-profit, or non-school-based
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations must meet eligibility requirements for either the NSLP or CACFP component. Contact USDA or the Maryland State Department of Education Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs at 410-767-0199 for application details and to determine eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual continuing education training (updated for 2025) that all child care staff and family child care providers must complete. This 90-minute online update covers health, safety, and nutrition topics. Successful completion earns 1.5 hours of Core of Knowledge credit in the Health, Safety, and Nutrition category and produces a certificate of participation that must be provided to the licensing specialist.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free annual online training covering health, safety, and nutrition for child care professionals. The 90-minute course qualifies for 1.5 hours of Core of Knowledge/Hours in the Health, Safety, and Nutrition category. Training is delivered through the Canvas learning management system (msde.instructure.com) and consists of multiple sequential modules: an Introduction module (must be completed first to unlock other topics), followed by topic-specific modules that can be completed in any order. All modules must be completed and a final review score of 80% or higher achieved to unlock the Certificate of Completion. The certificate can be downloaded, printed, or emailed and must be provided to the licensing specialist. Training must be completed by December 31, 2025 for current staff, or by March 31, 2026 for newly approved family child care providers and staff hired between October and December 2025.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Training must be completed by December 31, 2025 for current staff. All newly approved family child care providers and staff hired between October and December 2025 must complete the training by March 31, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All child care staff and family child care providers in Maryland. Also recommended for child care substitutes and volunteers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Annual update training covering health, safety, and nutrition competencies required for child care settings. Qualifies for 1.5 hours of Core of Knowledge continuing education credit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must complete the full 90-minute training
Must be employed in or operating a licensed child care program
Training must be completed by December 31, 2025 for current staff (or by March 31, 2026 if hired October–December 2025)
Must achieve 80% or higher score on the Final Review module to unlock Certificate of Completion
Must download, print, or email the certificate of participation after successful completion and provide a copy to the licensing specialist
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Go to https://msde.instructure.com/login/canvas and log in with your email address and password. 2) Click on the Educator Resources button on the MSDE Canvas Welcome Page. 3) Click on the Early Childhood Modules button. 4) Click on the Basic Health and Safety Annual Update 2025 button. 5) Select and complete the Introduction to Basic Health and Safety module first (other modules are locked until completion). 6) Complete all remaining topic modules in any order; use the EXIT COURSE button in the upper right corner between sessions. 7) Once all topics are complete, the Final Review module becomes available. 8) Complete the Final Review with a score of 80% or higher to unlock the Certificate of Completion module. 9) Download, print, or email your certificate of completion and provide a copy to your licensing specialist.

structured_extraction.program_name: Annual Program Training for School Meals Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: Annual administrative training to provide updates on USDA regulations and guidance, and professional development for school nutrition professionals administering School Meals programs including the National School Lunch Program, School Breakfast Program, Child and Adult Care Food Program, Summer Food Service Program, and Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual administrative training covering updates on USDA regulations and guidance, professional development, and training on School Meals programs including the National School Lunch Program, School Breakfast Program, Child and Adult Care Food Program, Summer Food Service Program, and Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School nutrition professionals and staff at local education agencies and child care providers administering school meals programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development and training on USDA regulations, school meals program administration, and nutrition services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to school districts and child care providers in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Training is offered through Maryland State Department of Education - Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: A registered apprenticeship program that combines paid on-the-job training with related technical instruction to provide students with high-quality career-connected learning. Students work toward industry-recognized credentials while earning income and gaining real-world work experience.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students receive 450 hours of paid on-the-job training and 144 hours of related technical instruction. Placements are flexible and can occur during the school day, after school, over the summer, or on weekends. Adult apprentice programs may help with college tuition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students and adults seeking career-connected learning opportunities; employers seeking to develop talent pipelines
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-the-job training and related technical instruction in approved apprenticeship positions across various industries
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland through local school districts
requirements_list: Approved by the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council
Employer registration and sponsorship required
Industry-aligned position
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students and families should contact their school's apprenticeship or career-connected learning coordinator to explore opportunities, eligibility, and scheduling. Employers should partner with a Maryland Department of Labor Navigator to learn how to register positions and host student apprentices.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free online training course that all child care providers, staff, and substitutes must complete to meet state and federal requirements of the Child Care and Development Block Grant (CCDBG) and Maryland regulations. The course covers four modules across health and safety topics relevant to child care providers and staff working in licensed child care programs, takes approximately 3 hours to complete, and is delivered via the MSDE Canvas learning management system. Upon successful completion with a score of 80% or higher, participants receive a certificate of completion. An annual update version (Annual Health and Safety Update) is also available for continuing education credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training consisting of four modules covering health and safety topics required by the Child Care and Development Block Grant (CCDBG) and Maryland regulations (COMAR). The course takes approximately 3 hours to complete and is accessed through the MSDE Canvas learning management system at https://msde.instructure.com. The Introduction module must be completed first; subsequent modules may be completed in any order. The system remembers progress between sessions; participants should use the EXIT COURSE button when leaving to save their place. Upon completing all modules, participants take a final review and survey in one sitting. Scores are calculated immediately upon submission. Participants must score a minimum of 80% on all topic reviews and the final review and survey to receive a certificate of completion. Up to four attempts are allowed to achieve the passing score (some cohort rules limit to two attempts — confirm current rules at registration). Certificates appear in the participant's account and must be printed and saved before the course end date; MSDE does not retain or re-issue copies after expiration. Registration opens for one week each month: April cohort registration opens March 13 and closes March 23, with training completion required by April 22; May cohort registration opens April 13 and closes April 23, with training completion by May 22; June cohort registration opens May 13 and closes May 23, with training completion by June 22. Late registrations are not accepted. New employees have 90 days after hire to complete the course. All staff must complete by December 31, 2025; newly approved family child care providers and staff hired October–December 2025 must complete by March 31, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration windows vary by cohort. April cohort registration opens March 13 and closes March 23 at 12:00 pm; training must be completed by April 22. May cohort registration opens April 13 and closes April 23 at 12:00 pm; training must be completed by May 22. June cohort registration opens May 13 and closes May 23 at 12:00 pm; training must be completed by June 22. Late registrations are not accepted. New employees have 90 days after hire to complete. All staff must complete by December 31, 2025; newly approved family child care providers and staff hired October–December 2025 must complete by March 31, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All child care providers, staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for the care and safety of children in licensed child care programs in Maryland. Also recommended for child care substitutes and volunteers. New employees in child care settings must complete within 90 days of hire.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The training covers required health and safety competencies for child care settings, including topics aligned with COMAR and best practices. Completion demonstrates compliance with Child Care and Development Block Grant requirements and is a prerequisite for child care provider licensing and credentialing compliance. Training may also include Breastfeeding Awareness content.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. For those without computer access, public libraries have computers available for course completion.
requirements_list: Must be working in or seeking to work in a licensed child care program
Must have a valid email address to register (one name per email address; separate email addresses required for multiple registrations)
Must have basic computer skills including using a mouse, typing, using email, viewing videos, navigating the internet, and printing from a browser
Must complete all four modules and final review and survey
Introduction module must be completed first to unlock subsequent modules
Must score a minimum of 80% on all topic reviews and the final review and survey to receive a certificate
Final review and survey must be completed in one sitting
Must complete training prior to the course end date (accounts expire after course concludes)
Certificate must be printed and saved before the course end date; MSDE does not retain copies
New employees must complete training within 90 days of hire for compliance
All staff must complete by December 31, 2025; newly approved family child care providers and staff hired October–December 2025 must complete by March 31, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Register during the designated one-week registration window each month by completing the online registration form at https://msde.instructure.com. 2) Receive login instructions and username/password via email before the course opens. 3) Access training at https://msde.instructure.com/login/canvas and log in using your email address and password. 4) Select the Introduction to Basic Health and Safety module first; other modules unlock after its completion. 5) Work through the remaining modules in any order. 6) Use the EXIT COURSE button before leaving to save your place; the system remembers your progress between sessions. 7) Complete the final review and survey in one sitting. 8) Scores are calculated immediately; if you score 80% or higher, your certificate of completion appears in your account. 9) Print and save your certificate before the course end date, as copies are not retained by MSDE. For questions or technical issues, email cdetraining@maryland.gov or healthandsafetyocc.msde@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The BOOST Scholarship Program provides scholarship awards to eligible students from low-income families to attend participating nonpublic schools. Priority is given to students who qualify for free or reduced-price meals and to students who received BOOST scholarships in the previous year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards are provided as checks sent to participating nonpublic schools. The scholarship must be deposited by the participating school and applied to the student's tuition account. Award amounts depend on household income, student academic level, and financial assistance provided by the school. The award may be reduced if it exceeds the tuition owed to the school. Funds must be used for tuition and required fees for enrollment only; they cannot be used for transportation or meals. For the 2026-2027 school year, approximately 2,500 awards are estimated to be available from a total funding allocation of approximately $9,000,000 plus carryover of unused funds from the previous year. Base award amounts and additional awards for students receiving special education services are determined by the BOOST Advisory Board.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 8, 2026, no later than 11:59 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.contact_name: Allison Sanborn (BOOST Program Manager) and James Clark (Administrative Support)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students from low-income families (those eligible for free or reduced-price school meals) who are enrolled or accepted at participating nonpublic schools for grades kindergarten through 12th grade.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition payments and required fees at participating nonpublic schools. Funds cannot be used for transportation or meals. The scholarship award must be applied to the student's tuition account at the school.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to nonpublic schools that hold a certificate of approval or are registered with the State Board of Education, are approved to participate in the Nonpublic Textbook Program, and provide more than only prekindergarten and kindergarten programs.
requirements_list: Student must be in grades kindergarten through 12th grade in the 2026-2027 school year (Pre-K students are not eligible)
Student must be enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school for the 2026-2027 school year
Household must qualify for Free and Reduced-Price Meals (FARMs) based on Federal 1040 tax returns
Parents/guardians must upload 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns to verify annual income and household size

Priority ranking: (1st) Students who received BOOST in 2025-2026 and their siblings; (2nd) New applicants from public school qualifying for free meals; (3rd) New applicants from public school qualifying for reduced-price meals; (4th) Continuing nonpublic school students qualifying for free meals; (5th) Continuing nonpublic school students qualifying for reduced-price meals
Student must not have a prior BOOST award that is still being carried over
Participating nonpublic schools must hold a certificate of approval from or be registered with the State Board of Education
Participating nonpublic schools must be approved to participate in the Nonpublic Textbook Program
Participating nonpublic schools must provide more than only prekindergarten and kindergarten programs
Participating nonpublic schools must comply with all BOOST reporting requirements by specified deadlines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Parents/guardians must complete an online BOOST Scholarship application through the Submittable portal, including: (1) Child's full name as it appears on birth certificate; (2) Whether child received BOOST previously; (3) Whether child is a sibling of a prior BOOST recipient; (4) Grade level for 2026-2027 school year; (5) Nonpublic school name and current school enrollment information; (6) Whether child has learning disability and receives special education services; and (7) Upload of 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns in PDF format for income and household size verification. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and completeness on a rolling basis but are not first-come, first-serve. After the May 8, 2026 deadline, all application data is collected and provided to the BOOST Advisory Board. The Advisory Board convenes in summer 2026 to determine base award amounts and additional awards for special education students. Parents/guardians are notified by email by August 2026 if their child is offered an award and must accept or decline by the specified deadline. Participating nonpublic schools must confirm student enrollment and upload IEP/IFSP/504 Plan documentation for students receiving special education services. Scholarship checks are printed and mailed via FedEx to schools in October through December 2026. Parents/guardians must sign the back of the check at the school. No awards are offered after December 11, 2026. Customer service support sessions are held on specified dates; weekly virtual office hours are offered Wednesdays 12-1 pm from March 18 through May 6, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF)
structured_extraction.program_description: A tuition assistance program that helps child care providers and staff earn college degrees in early childhood education and related fields at participating colleges and universities in Maryland. The program pays tuition, fees, and required textbooks directly to the participating college or university on behalf of participants rather than reimbursing them. Participants must be credentialed at Level Two or higher in the Maryland Child Care Credential program. First-time applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis, with priority given to applicants who have not yet completed any college courses for credit from an accredited college or university. Funding may continue annually if funds are available and the recipient continues to meet requirements. Recipients must fulfill a service commitment period of employment in Maryland child care after degree completion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tuition assistance is provided directly to the participating college or university on behalf of the applicant for tuition, college fees, and required textbooks for degrees in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education. Payments are made directly to the institution rather than reimbursing participants. Funds may only be used for actual expenses of college coursework incurred subsequent to an award and cannot be used to pay for costs previously incurred. Service commitment requirements after degree completion: 2 years for an associate's degree, 4 years for a bachelor's degree, 2.5 years for a master's degree, or 1 month for each college credit successfully completed. Recipients must work at least 20 hours per week in a licensed Maryland child care program during the service commitment period. Failure to complete the service requirement or withdrawal without good cause requires repayment of all tuition, fees, and textbooks paid on the recipient's behalf.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First-time applications due by March 1; Continuation applications due by June 30; Transfer applications due by June 30
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and staff who work at least 10 hours per week in a licensed child care center or as registered family child care providers in Maryland and participate in the Maryland Child Care Credential program at Level Two or higher, as well as accredited colleges and universities participating in the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, fees, and required textbooks for earning a degree in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education at a participating Maryland college or university. Funds can only be used toward the completion of a college degree in an approved field for college coursework incurred subsequent to an award and cannot be used to pay for previously incurred college enrollment costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must work in a licensed child care center or be a registered family child care provider in Maryland. Recipients must maintain employment in child care in Maryland while participating in the program and after completion. Upon completion of the degree, participants must work in an approved child care facility in Maryland for at least 20 hours per week during their service commitment period. Available statewide at participating Maryland institutions of higher learning.
requirements_list: Participate in the Maryland Child Care Credential program at Level Two or higher
Work in a licensed child care center or be a registered family child care provider in Maryland
Work at least 10 hours per week in child care
Fulfill entrance requirements at the participating college of choice
Have at least one year of documented experience working with groups of children in an approved setting
Maintain employment in child care in Maryland while participating in the program
Participate in professional development
Agree to complete a child care service requirement in Maryland for at least 20 hours per week after completion of the degree or withdrawal from the fund
Maintain at least a 2.50 cumulative grade point average from the point of first entering the program
Apply for all financial assistance for which eligible (including FAFSA if appropriate)
Submit all required documentation including employer letter or family child care license, credential certificate, college acceptance letter with declared major, and professional development plan
Degree must be in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education from an institution recognized by the U.S. Department of Education
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Be accepted into a CCCPDF participating college or university. Step 2: Schedule an appointment with the CCCPDF Coordinator at the participating college to which you have been accepted and meet with the Coordinator to review the application checklist for completion and obtain their signature. Applications not reviewed by the Coordinator will be returned. Step 3: Apply directly to the college/university through the CCCPDF Coordinator, ensuring all required documents are included. Step 4: Submit the completed CCCPDF application with all required documentation to the Office of Child Care. First-time applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis, with priority given to applicants who have not yet completed any college courses for credit. An approval or denial letter will be sent to the applicant by the college/university. Continuation and transfer applications require updated documentation including a signed letter from current employer on letterhead or current family child care license, copy of current Maryland Child Care Credential certificate at Level Two or higher, and revised professional development plan if applicable. Incomplete applications will not be processed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Quality Incentive Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that provides funding to child care facilities and family child care providers to purchase supplies, materials, and equipment that improve and enhance the quality of care for children. Grants are awarded quarterly and are based on the size of the facility, with providers eligible for an award once every three years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded quarterly in January, April, July, and October during each state fiscal year. Funding amounts are based on the number of children in care: up to $1,000 for facilities with fewer than 10 children, up to $1,500 for facilities with up to 29 children, and up to $2,500 for facilities with more than 30 children. Eligible expenses include supplies, materials, and equipment that improve child care quality; the program guide details eligible and non-eligible expenses. Child care providers are eligible for a grant award once every three years. One application per child care facility location is required, with FEIN or SSN identification provided per site for providers operating multiple locations.

The program guide details eligible and non-eligible expenses.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Scholarship Program helps eligible families in Maryland pay for high-quality child care and early education programs. Families can receive a temporary 60-day scholarship through the Fast Track application process (determined within 3 business days) or a full 52-week (or two-year) scholarship to cover part of their child care costs at licensed child care centers, registered family homes, or informal child care providers. The program serves approximately 37,000 children, 25,000 parents, and 3,500 early care and educational programs. Participating child care providers receive advance enrollment-based payments from MSDE twice per month. The program also supports families experiencing homelessness, families referred by DHS, Head Start participants, and parenting youth in out-of-home care. As of May 1, 2025, the program temporarily stopped issuing scholarships to new families due to a funding freeze; currently enrolled families continue to receive benefits without interruption if they maintain eligibility and complete recertification on time.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible families receive payment scholarships that cover a portion of child care costs at Maryland EXCELS-participating licensed child care centers, registered family homes, or informal child care providers (relatives or non-relatives in the child's home). The scholarship shows the state-paid rate and the family co-payment. Co-payments range from $0 to $3 per week depending on the unit of care authorized: $3.00/week for 3-unit scholarships, $2.00/week for 2-unit scholarships, and $1.00/week for 1-unit scholarships. Co-payments can be waived for families who are homeless, receiving SNAP, WIC, TCA, SSI, WAG, Housing Choice Voucher Program benefits, Head Start or State-Funded Pre-K enrollment, migrant workers, minor parents, or Montgomery County GBI program participants. Families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) have a zero co-payment. Family co-payments decrease for multiple children receiving scholarships. A temporary 60-day Fast Track scholarship is issued within 3 business days of approval while the full application is processed. Full 52-week or two-year scholarships are issued upon approval of the complete application. Initial income scale maximum ranges from approximately $61,222–$76,117 for a family of 2 to $135,049–$167,904 for a family of 12; continuation income scale maximums are higher. Providers receive advance payments twice per month (on the 15th and last day of the month), calculated by converting the weekly scholarship amount to a daily rate and multiplying by payable days. Payment covers up to 60 days of child absences per calendar year. True-up reconciliation adjustments are made monthly. Providers receive payment within 7 days of payment processing completion via direct deposit. Parents are responsible for any tuition above the scholarship rate plus their co-payment. Applications and documents can be submitted online, by email to CCSCentral2@maryland.gov, by fax at 202-478-2102, or mailed to CCS Central 2, PO BOX 346031, Bethesda, MD 20827.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: As of May 1, 2025, the program temporarily stopped issuing scholarships to new families due to a funding freeze. Applications are still accepted and processed; approved applicants are added to a waitlist until funding becomes available. Ongoing redetermination applications must be submitted 45 days before current scholarship end date and at least 15 days prior to avoid payment breaks.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible Maryland families with children younger than 13 years old, or individuals ages 13–19 with a qualifying disability, who are working, in an approved training program, or attending school. Includes families experiencing homelessness, families referred by DHS or other public agencies, Head Start participants, parenting youth in out-of-home care (HB1121), and migrant workers. Also includes licensed child care centers, letter of compliance facilities, military child care centers, registered family child care providers, large family child care homes, and informal child care providers who wish to accept families with Child Care Scholarship support (must be Maryland EXCELS participants).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for high-quality child care and early education services at Maryland EXCELS-participating licensed child care centers, registered family homes, and informal child care providers (relatives or non-relatives in home settings). Includes before and after school child care, center-based care, family child care homes, and informal care. Funds can cover full-time, part-time, before/after school care, and summer extended hours. Providers use advance payments to cover operational costs associated with scholarship-supported children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland in all 24 counties and Baltimore City to all eligible Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be working, employed, in an approved training program, or attending school; for families where both parents live in the same household, both parents must meet all eligibility requirements

Must be a recipient of Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or have household income within CCS income guidelines (Initial Income Scale for new applications; Continuation Income Scale for changes/redeterminations)

Child must be younger than 13 years old, or an individual ages 13–19 with a qualifying disability (physically or mentally incapable of self-care appropriate to age, verified by physician, licensed/certified psychologist, or licensed social worker)
Child must be a U.S. citizen or qualified alien (birth certificate or proof of citizenship/qualified alien status required); parents are NOT required to be U.S. citizens
Must provide proof of identity for all household members (government-issued document for adults; birth certificate or immigration documentation for children)
Head of household must provide photo ID
Must be willing to have child immunized to Maryland state standards or provide documentation of exemption; for non-school-age children in informal care, immunization proof is required
Must provide proof of Maryland residency (utility bill, lease, mortgage statement, or Maryland driver's license with matching address)

For employment: must provide most recent four consecutive weeks of pay stubs (4 weekly, 2 bi-weekly, 2 semi-monthly, or 1 monthly); for school/training: current schedule on school/employer letterhead showing days and hours

Must document all other income sources (alimony, Social Security, SSI, self-employment, TCA, tips/commission, unemployment benefits, veterans assistance, workers compensation, armed services pay, bonuses)
For self-employment: previous year's tax return (if after April 15) or profit and loss statements for past 3 months plus completed Self-Employment Attestation Statement
Must register in the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal at https://family.childcareportals.org

For informal providers: must pass criminal background check (CJIS fingerprinting), Child Protective Services background clearance, complete Basic Health & Safety training (3 hours) plus annual update (1.5 hours), CPR and First Aid certification, care location inspection, Emergency Preparedness Plan, Emergency Care & Medication Authorization forms, and proof of residency and identity; informal non-relative care must take place in child's home; relative care can be in child's home or provider's home
Providers must be Maryland EXCELS participants to enroll scholarship children
Providers must register and use the Child Care Provider Portal at https://provider.childcareportals.org/

Providers must submit timely and accurate attendance records within 14 days of audit request (25% of paid invoices randomly selected bi-weekly); records can be requested up to 5 years from date services were paid
Children in informal relative care require proof of relatedness (great-grandparents, grandparents, aunts, uncles)
For families experiencing homelessness: submit homelessness coversheet signed by DHS, shelter, or transitional staff
Migrant workers must provide employer documentation verifying status
Emancipated minors must provide documentation verifying financial responsibility and adult decision-making status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families apply through the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal at https://family.childcareportals.org (Spanish version at family.childcareportals.org/s/?language=es). Step 1: Register for a new account with email verification and two-factor authentication. Step 2: Submit a Fast-Track application (available only once per family) with three required documents: proof of employment or enrollment in training/school (on employer or school letterhead with activity schedule), proof of residency (utility bill, lease, mortgage statement, or Maryland driver's license with matching address), and proof of income (most recent 4 weeks of consecutive pay stubs). Step 3: Fast-Track application is processed within 3 business days by CCS Central 2. Step 4: If eligible, a temporary 60-day scholarship is issued while the full application is processed. Step 5: Within 15 days of Fast-Track approval, submit the Full Application with additional documentation: proof of all income including bonuses, commissions, alimony, Social Security, SSI, self-employment, TCA, tips, unemployment, veterans benefits, workers compensation; proof of citizenship or qualified alien status for all children; proof of identity for all household members; proof of address; documentation of other benefits (SNAP, WIC, TCA, WAG, GBI, Housing Assistance). Full Application is processed within 30 calendar days from submission or within 5 business days of receipt of all required documentation; if approved, a two-year scholarship is issued. Step 6: Select a child care provider participating in Maryland EXCELS; families can find providers at https://findaprogram.marylandexcels.org/ and check provider history at www.checkccmd.org. Step 7: For continued benefits, submit a Redetermination Application 45 days before current scholarship end date (at least 15 days prior to avoid payment breaks). Returning customers may submit New Scholarship Applications processed within 30 calendar days. Interim changes to household composition, income, or activity can be submitted at any time through the portal. For informal child care providers, the eligibility determination process can take up to 60 days pending receipt of all background clearances; MSDE will not authorize payment until all required documents are approved. For assistance finding child care, contact Maryland Family Network at 877-261-0060. Translators available by phone upon request. Documents may also be submitted by email to CCSCentral2@maryland.gov, fax at 202-478-2102, or mail to CCS Central 2, PO BOX 346031, Bethesda, MD 20827. Providers register at https://provider.childcareportals.org/, accept scholarship enrollment requests within 5 business days, track child attendance daily with parent signatures, submit invoices through the portal, and respond to Attendance Verification requests within 14 days. Dispute resolution available via informal inquiry (within 90 days of payment), informal appeal (within 90 days of notification), or formal appeal for Intentional Program Violations through the Office of Administrative Hearings.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides advance monthly payments to child care providers based on enrollment of children with child care scholarships. Providers receive two payments per month (on the 15th and last day of the month) rather than retroactive payments, based on the number of scholarship-enrolled children appearing on their invoice by the last Saturday of each month. The program uses enrollment-based calculations rather than attendance-based reimbursement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSDE provides advance payments to child care providers twice monthly (on the 15th and the last day of each month, with payment typically received by providers starting the 6th and 21st of each month). Payments are based on enrollment-based calculations: the number of children with enrolled scholarships appearing on a provider's invoice as of the last Saturday of the previous month. Monthly payments are divided equally into two payments and calculated based on a daily rate to account for varying numbers of days per month. Payments include coverage for days of absenteeism unless a child's absences exceed 60 days within a calendar year (informal providers are not paid for absences and holidays). A True-Up reconciliation process reconciles payments in the fourth month and onward to account for enrollment changes, early scholarship endings, voucher end dates, EXCELS tier adjustments, adverse actions, registration fees, union dues, and recoupments.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline for ongoing program participation; families apply for child care scholarships on a rolling basis through the Family Portal
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers, registered family child care home providers, large family child care home providers, and informal child care providers serving children with child care scholarships in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payments for child care services provided to scholarship-enrolled children; providers may use funds for operating costs and staff compensation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to all counties

Children must appear on provider's invoice by the last Saturday of the previous month to be included in that month's Advance Payment

Providers must submit invoices and attendance records for each monthly service period within 60 days of the end of the service period; failure to submit within 60 days may result in payment recoupment
Providers must pass MSDE Program Integrity Audits

Providers must be approved by the Maryland State Department of Education to operate as a child care provider
EXCELS participation is required for CCS program participation; if EXCELS participation ends mid-month, no payment is issued for dates after EXCELS expiration unless participation is renewed
For informal providers: not paid for child absences or holidays; overpayment established when absences are reported
For all providers: if a child is absent more than 60 days in a calendar year without a medical waiver, an overpayment is established for the excessive absences
Registered Family Home Providers who are SEIU members will have union dues deducted from Advanced Payments
Maryland EXCELS Tier Payments are added to the Advanced Payment based on provider's quality rating
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers submit documentation and invoices through the Child Care Provider Portal at https://provider.childcareportals.org. Families apply for child care scholarships through the Family Portal at https://family.childcareportals.org. Providers must register for a portal account and provide required documentation. Families can submit Fast-Track applications (3 business day determination), Full applications (30 calendar days or 5 business days after all documentation received), or New applications (30 calendar days or 5 business days after all documentation received). Once approved, scholarships are assigned to providers. Advance payments are calculated monthly based on enrollment data from the last Saturday of the previous month and issued automatically on the 15th and last day of each month. Providers receive two equal payments split across these dates. Providers must submit signed invoices and attendance records for each monthly service period within 60 days of the end of the service period. MSDE issues individualized notification emails at the start of each month detailing the advance payment calculation. For disputes, providers may submit inquiries through the Provider Inquiry Link within 90 days of payment receipt or submit informal appeals through the Provider Portal within 90 days; CCS will address inquiries within 3 business days and issue final decisions on informal appeals within 90 calendar days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's program to ensure the quality of professional development offered to child care professionals. Individuals and organizations can become approved trainers to deliver training that meets quality standards and is accepted for the Maryland Child Care Credential and continued education to meet licensing regulations. The Office leads statewide review, approval, renewal, and monitoring of trainers and training proposals (birth to 8 years old) for Core of Knowledge, Pre-Service, and Continued training, and provides technical assistance to applicants and approved trainers, and facilitates quarterly trainer meetings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved trainers receive a unique approval number valid for 4 years, allowing them to develop and deliver training accepted for the Maryland Child Care Credential and continued or elective training to meet licensing regulations. Training approval numbers must be designated on training certificates issued to child care professionals. The program provides technical assistance to applicants and approved trainers, and facilitates quarterly trainer meetings. Training proposals are reviewed on a bi-monthly basis by the Training Review Team composed of advanced trainers and DEC staff, using an established and approved rubric. Community colleges, universities, approved national organizations, and individuals recognized as authorities in their field are exempt from approval requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Renewal applications must be received 30 days prior to expiration date of approval number
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and organizations who want to provide training to child care professionals in Maryland, including those seeking to offer Core of Knowledge, Pre-Service, and Continued training for children birth to age 8.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training development and delivery to child care professionals in approved subject areas and Core of Knowledge domains. Oversight and approval of training programs in Core of Knowledge, Pre-Service, and Continued training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Community colleges, universities, approved national organizations, and individuals recognized as authorities in their field are exempt from approval requirements.
requirements_list: Attend required Training Orientation
Submit Training Approval Application with supporting documentation
Must comply with requirements identified in COMAR 13A.14.08
Maintain 24 hours of training in adult training methods or approved subject/domains for renewal
Submit quarterly training reports
Attend minimum of 2 quarterly trainer meetings for renewal
Abide by ethical standards and COMAR 13A.14.08 regulations
Renew approval every 4 years with application submitted 30 days prior to expiration
Designate trainer approval number on all training certificates issued to child care professionals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for the required Training Orientation at https://earlychildhood.marylandpublicschools.org/trainers to receive knowledge of the training approval process, requirements, and Core of Knowledge content areas. Submit a training proposal using the online form at https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScXOLUENPIRviMKYdRNqFCVLpQf6a4ONEh77IYF_pnVuhLDNw/viewform. Submit the application and supporting documentation electronically to trainingcredential.msde@maryland.gov. Training proposals are reviewed on a bi-monthly basis by the Training Review Team; letters are generated following review sessions. For renewal, submit the renewal application 30 days prior to the expiration of your approval number.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF) assists low-income families in obtaining child care so they can work or attend training and education. The program also fosters the quality of child care and promotes coordination among early childhood development and afterschool programs. CCDF made available $5.2 billion to states, territories, and tribes in Fiscal Year 2012 and continues to provide ongoing federal funding administered through Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CCDF provides subsidies and financial assistance to help low-income families pay for child care services, enabling parents to work or participate in training and education programs. The program also supports quality improvement initiatives and promotes coordination among early childhood development and afterschool programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families who need child care in order to work or attend training and education programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides child care food subsidies for low-income families. Child care centers that participate can receive reimbursement for food costs to help ensure young children are well-fed and ready for kindergarten.
