structured_extraction.program_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Child and Adult Care Food Program provides nutritionally balanced meals and snacks to young children, older adults, and people with chronic disabilities at participating childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, emergency shelters, and adult day care facilities. The program reimburses participating agencies with federal funds for meals and snacks that meet United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) nutrition standards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The CACFP reimburses child and adult care agencies with federal dollars for meals and snacks that comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns. CACFP sponsors receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their CACFP meal reimbursements. The annual maximum reimbursement for a child or adult care center serving 25 free-eligible participants breakfast, lunch, and a snack 5 days per week is available. Family child care homes can receive annual maximum reimbursement for serving 6 Tier I participants breakfast, lunch, and a snack 5 days per week.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland State Department of Education; The Planning Council - Lisa Lyons, CACFP Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child and adult care agencies, including childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, emergency shelters, and adult day care facilities serving children including infants, adults over 60, and adults living with a disability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Meals and snacks for children and adults that comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland at participating facilities. Over 300 agencies across the state participate in the CACFP. Meals and snacks must comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns
Children 18 years and younger in emergency shelters are automatically eligible for free meals
Family Child Care Providers must participate through specific sponsoring organizations
Interested centers must complete the CACFP Interest Survey and Budget Worksheet
Centers must complete CACFP Basics Training and three-part online application
Centers must pass a pre-approval visit by MSDE before approval to participate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. An interested child or adult care center calls MSDE at 410-767-0199 to begin the CACFP Interest Process. 2. The interested center completes the CACFP Interest Survey and Budget Worksheet. 3. MSDE determines the center's eligibility to participate in the CACFP. 4. The center must complete CACFP Basics Training and three-part online application. 5. MSDE completes a pre-approval visit. 6. MSDE approves the center to participate in the CACFP and the center can begin to claim reimbursement for meals served. Family Child Care Providers should contact their designated county sponsoring organization to begin enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A meal service option that allows schools and school districts in low-income areas to serve breakfast and lunch at no cost to all enrolled students, without collecting household income applications. Schools and school districts with an Identified Student Percentage (ISP) of 25% or higher are eligible to elect CEP. Identified students are those directly certified for free meals based on participation in programs such as SNAP and TANF. CEP promotes equity and access to nutritious meals during the school day by providing federal funding for free meals without income verification requirements.

Schools and school districts with an Identified Student Percentage (ISP) of 25% or higher are eligible to elect CEP. Identified students are those directly certified for free meals through programs like SNAP or TANF.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing free breakfast and lunch meals to all enrolled students during the school day

requirements_list: School or school district must have an Identified Student Percentage (ISP) of 25% or higher
Identified students are those directly certified for free meals through programs like SNAP or TANF

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that requires local education agencies identified as having significant disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or discipline to reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B funds to implement proactive and responsive actions addressing root causes of over-identification by race or ethnicity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local education agencies identified as having significant disproportionality must reserve 15 percent of their IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds to implement CCEIS activities. Funds support educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and support including evidence-based literacy instruction, professional development, systemic awareness building, stakeholder engagement, root cause analysis, implementation driver supports (staffing, training, coaching, consultation), professional learning experiences, and comprehensive program evaluation. Allowable costs include salaries for coaches, mentors, general education teachers, guidance counselors, school-based psychologists, RTI/MTSS coordinators, school social workers, substitute teachers, and tutors; extended contracts/extended hours for staff; professional development services; travel for staff; computing devices and instructional software/materials for intervention delivery; and special education teacher salaries when delivering Tier 2 and Tier 3 interventions. Non-allowable costs include universal/core curriculum, student transportation, office equipment, furniture, rent/occupancy costs, universal screening, special education referral/evaluation costs, and occupational/physical therapy services unless for students identified as needing Tier 2 or Tier 3 interventions.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Gary W. Richardson, MBA (Branch Chief); Demetria White (Interagency Specialist)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies in Maryland identified as having significant disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or disciplinary actions by race or ethnicity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and support including evidence-based literacy instruction; professional development; building systemic awareness and leadership; stakeholder engagement; root cause analysis; planning proactive and responsive actions; implementing systemic drivers including staffing, training, coaching, and data systems; professional learning for staff; and comprehensive program evaluation. CCEIS funds must address identified factors contributing to significant disproportionality, which may include lack of access to scientifically-based instruction, economic/cultural/linguistic barriers, inappropriate use of disciplinary removals, lack of access to appropriate diagnostic screenings, differences in academic achievement levels, and policies/practices/procedures contributing to disproportionality. Funds serve children ages 3-21 who are not currently identified as requiring special education and who need additional academic and behavioral support, as well as children currently identified as requiring special education (though funds may not be used exclusively for this group).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to local education agencies in Maryland identified by the state as having one or more subgroups of students evidencing a risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years in identification, placement, or disciplinary removals. Determination is based on Maryland's significant disproportionality methodology and threshold standards.
requirements_list: Local education agency must be identified by the state as having significant disproportionality over-identification based on race or ethnicity
Must have risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years (unless risk ratio declines by defined amount from one year to the next)
Must address factors contributing to significant disproportionality
Must address and review policies, practices, or procedures identified as contributing to over-identification

Must convene local implementation team and diverse stakeholder group including school/student support representatives, general and/or special education coordinators, school-based administrators and staff, parents/community members, and other internal/external partners
Must engage in self-assessment and data review process using a state-recommended self-assessment tool
Must conduct root cause analysis examining decision-making processes, procedures, and practices for students ages 3 through 21
Must plan and implement proactive and responsive actions based on root cause factors identified
Must align expenditures with specific actions to mitigate root causes and meet CCEIS plan outcomes
Must include review and/or adjustment of policies, procedures, and/or practices annually
Must implement academic and/or behavioral interventions as preventative or corrective actions
Must provide professional learning for personnel capacity-building focusing on observable changes in causes of disparate outcomes
Must set measurable outcomes including goals and interim benchmarks aligned to grant reporting periods with implementation and progress monitoring measures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local education agencies identified as having significant disproportionality submit a Comprehensive Coordinated Early Intervening Services Plan using the state template to the Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Intervention and Special Education Services. The application process includes: (1) completing the SFY 2025 CCEIS Plan Template which requires identification of the local implementation team, reserved fund amounts by funding source (611 and/or 619), categories of analysis (identification, placement, disciplinary removals) being addressed, at-risk areas, self-assessment and root cause analysis narrative, planned response actions (PRAs) with alignment to root causes and measurable outcomes, and detailed budget; (2) submitting required fiscal documents including MSDE Grant Budget C-1-25 forms and Budget Detail Forms; (3) obtaining required signatures from Local Director of Special Education, Chief Academic Officer, Finance Officer, Superintendent (or Deputy), and MSDE equity/program/fiscal liaisons and Resource Management and Monitoring Branch Chief. Interim progress reports are due January 31 (for periods ending September 30 and December 31) and final reports due November 30. Grant amendments may be submitted as needed with updated C-1-25, C-1-25 A, C-1-25 B forms and Budget Detail documentation.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To offset costs of opening child care programs

The program supports both student nutrition and domestic agricultural producers, with distribution coordinated through the Maryland State Department of Education's Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs (OSCNP).

structured_extraction.program_name: Food Safety Training for School Nutrition Professionals (ServSafe / FISH Initiative)
structured_extraction.program_description: An ongoing program providing food safety training options and resources for school food service personnel in Maryland participating in federally funded child nutrition programs. Certified instructors from local education agencies can teach classes and order materials at no cost through the Food Is Safe Here (FISH) Initiative. A minimum of 8 hours of food safety training is provided to meet USDA Professional Standards requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free ongoing food safety training program using National Restaurant Association's ServSafe curricula and certification exam. Includes a minimum of 8 hours of food safety training to meet USDA Professional Standards. Covers ServSafe Food Handler and Food Manager training and certification review sessions. Certified instructors from local education agencies can teach classes and order materials at no cost. Materials orders available through online form with four-week advance notice required. The Food Is Safe Here (FISH) Initiative is the overarching program umbrella. More information at msde-fish.org.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford Community College Child Care Apprenticeship
structured_extraction.program_description: An 18-month apprenticeship program through Harford Community College combining 257 hours of classroom instruction with 3,000 hours of on-the-job training in early childhood education. The program is designed for aides and newcomers to the field and includes certificates in Preschool, Infant & Toddler, School-Age care, and CDA Preparation. Participants can receive tuition assistance through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF) for this program. The apprenticeship is registered with the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council and articulates to 21 college credits towards an Early Childhood Education AAS degree.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An 18-month registered apprenticeship combining classroom and on-the-job training. Apprentices complete 257 hours of asynchronous online classroom instruction (except CPR/first aid and Medication Administration which can be in-person) covering topics including child growth and development, preschool and infant/toddler curriculum, school-age care, positive discipline, and CDA preparation. Apprentices complete 3,000 hours of on-the-job training mentored by a lead teacher, focusing on child safety, building relationships, promoting learning, and adhering to licensing requirements. Completed apprenticeship articulates to 21 college credits towards an Early Childhood Education AAS degree, with an additional 3 credits for the CDA. Tuition assistance is available through CCCPDF for eligible participants who meet the apprenticeship program requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking on-the-job training and education in early childhood care and education, including aides and newcomers to the child care field
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition for the Harford Community College Child Care Apprenticeship program, which combines 257 hours of classroom instruction with 3,000 hours of practical on-the-job training in early childhood education, leading to certificates and college credit towards an Early Childhood Education degree.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The apprenticeship program works with over 70 registered child care programs throughout Maryland. Completers work in six different counties and Baltimore City. Participants must meet CCCPDF eligibility requirements including working in a licensed child care center or as a registered family child care provider in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must meet CCCPDF eligibility requirements to receive tuition assistance
Participate in both on-the-job training and classroom learning
Apprenticeship is 18 months long with 257 classroom hours and 3,000 on-the-job training hours
Program designed for aides and newcomers to the child care field
Work with a participating registered employer child care program
Complete online asynchronous courses plus in-person CPR/first aid and Medication Administration training

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Support Services (IECMHSS) — Consultation & Technical Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: This program improves the ability of staff, programs, and families to prevent, identify, treat, and reduce the impact of social, emotional, and other mental health problems among children birth through 5 years old. It provides consultation, training, coaching, and mentoring to child care providers, teachers, and families through a hybrid model addressing both individual child/family needs and classroom/program environments. IECMH consultants work with teachers to improve classroom quality and help manage challenging child behaviors, while also connecting children and families to appropriate mental health services and community resources. The program operates across 12 statewide child care licensing regions in Maryland, with origins in Baltimore City and the Eastern Shore.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides consultation, training, coaching, and mentoring services to child care providers, teachers, and families. IECMH consultants work with both individual children and families as well as entire classroom programs to build staff confidence and competence in handling challenging behaviors and to improve overall classroom quality. The program also refers children and families needing more intensive mental health services to appropriate support programs and community resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers, teachers, families with children birth through 5 years old, child care programs, and Head Start centers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Consultation, training, coaching, and mentoring to prevent and address social, emotional, and mental health problems in young children; referrals to more intensive mental health services and community resources; classroom environment improvement; family support
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in 12 statewide child care licensing regions across Maryland, originally started in Baltimore City and the Eastern Shore
requirements_list: Child care programs must be part of or connected to the child care licensing system
Program focuses on children birth through 5 years old
Participants must engage with consultants for training, coaching, and mentoring
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Program services are provided through local child care licensing regions and partnerships with community resources. Interested programs should reach out to their local child care licensing region or the Division of Early Childhood.

structured_extraction.program_name: Judy Center Early Learning Hubs (Judith P. Hoyer Early Child Care and Education Enhancement Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive family support hubs located in elementary schools across Maryland, established by the Judith P. Hoyer Early Child Care and Education Enhancement Program enacted by the Maryland State Legislature in May 2000. Judy Centers serve families with children from prenatal stages through age 5 using a multigenerational approach, empowering families as their children's most important teachers. The program prepares children for school success by delivering high-quality, comprehensive, full-day (7–12 hours per day), full-year early care and education services in Title I and high-needs school catchment areas. In FY2024, 86 Judy Centers operated across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions, serving 17,681 children and 14,750 families. Per the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, Judy Centers are expanding by 9 sites annually until 2025, then at 18 sites annually from 2026–2030. Services include developmental screenings, family learning activities and engagement, parenting classes and workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based family and child playgroups (minimum 2 sessions weekly), referrals for services and supports (80,367 referrals in FY2024), early intervention identification, evidence-based home visiting, case management with families, service coordination with community partners, meals during school days/breaks/weekends/after-school hours, health-related services (dental, vision, hearing, mental health screenings), professional learning for staff and partners, and full inclusion of children with disabilities through IEP and IFSP services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant-funded programs providing comprehensive, integrated, full-day (not less than 7 hours or more than 12 hours per day), full-year early care and education services. Services include developmental screenings and assessments, family learning activities and engagement through on-site parent and child playgroups, parenting classes and training workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based family and child playgroups, referrals for services and supports, early intervention identification, evidence-based home visiting, case management with families, service coordination with community partners, meals during school days/breaks/weekends/after-school, health-related services (dental, vision, hearing, mental health, nutritional assessments), professional learning for staff and partners, and support for children with disabilities through IEP and IFSP services. Each Judy Center site is staffed with a coordinator who manages programs and services for enrolled families. As of FY2024, 86 Judy Center sites operate statewide across all 24 jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; families engage directly with Judy Centers throughout the year
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager; Nancy Garcia, Judy Center Specialist (Spanish assistance)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children from prenatal stages through age 5 who live within the school zone where a Judy Center is located, particularly those in Title I and high-needs schools serving historically underserved communities. Children served will attend Pre-K and Kindergarten at the school where the Judy Center is located. In FY2024, services were provided to 17,681 children and 14,750 families across 86 sites.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full-day/full-year early care and education services; developmental screenings and early identification; family learning activities and engagement; parenting classes and workshops; adult education and workforce development connections; evidence-based family and child playgroups; service referrals; early intervention identification; home visiting; case management; meals during school day and breaks; health screenings and referrals (dental, vision, hearing, mental health); transition support across programs; professional learning for partners; and full inclusion of children with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Judy Center Early Learning Hubs are located in elementary schools across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions (all counties plus Baltimore City). As of FY2024, there are 86 sites statewide. Families must live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located. Judy Centers prioritize Title I and high-needs school zones. Per Blueprint for Maryland's Future, expanding by 9 sites annually until 2025, then 18 sites annually from 2026–2030. Find your local hub at https://marylandfamiliesengage.org/judy-center-hubs-map/.
requirements_list: Children must live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located
Children will attend Pre-K and Kindergarten at the school where the Judy Center is located

Families must engage with the Judy Center at least 12 times during the fiscal year OR be enrolled in formal partner programs such as Kindergarten, Prekindergarten, Early Head Start, Head Start, Patty Centers, family child care providers, or child care centers to be counted as served
Children ages birth through five, regardless of abilities, have access to all programs and services
Children with disabilities and their families are fully included in all services as part of IEP and IFSP requirements
All early care and education programs partnering with the Judy Center must be accredited or actively pursuing accreditation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families interested in accessing Judy Center services should contact their closest Judy Center Early Learning Hub directly or visit the Judy Centers map at https://marylandfamiliesengage.org/judy-center-hubs-map/ to find location and contact information. No formal application deadline exists; families can engage with their local Judy Center at any time during the fiscal year on a rolling basis. Individual Judy Center coordinators can be reached through their respective school locations. A comprehensive coordinator contact list by county and school location is available at http://earlychildhood.marylandpublicschools.org/system/files/filedepot/2/judycentercoordinatorlistwebsitefeb2015_.pdf. For program-level inquiries, contact Kaymi Plank at kaymi.plank@maryland.gov or 410.767.0675; Spanish assistance available from Nancy Garcia at nancy.garcia1@maryland.gov or 410-767-0785.

structured_extraction.program_name: Licensing Compliance Grant for Family Child Care Providers (LCGFCCP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that helps registered family child care providers offset costs of opening, operating, and maintaining their child care programs by reimbursing up to $1,000 in eligible expenses related to achieving or maintaining compliance with family child care licensing regulations. Eligible expenses include safety supplies, provider medical examination fees, criminal background check fees, small household repairs in approved child care areas, approved child care training course fees, expenses related to local water, sewer, fire, and health requirements, program materials and equipment, and other costs necessary for completing the registration process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses registered family child care providers up to $1,000 in eligible expenses incurred to achieve or maintain compliance with family child care licensing regulations. Reimbursement is provided as a grant award. Eligible expenses include safety supplies, provider medical examination fees, criminal background check fees, small household repairs in approved child care areas, approved child care training course fees, expenses related to local water, sewer, fire, and health requirements, program materials and equipment, and other costs necessary for completing the registration process.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Safety supplies, provider medical examination fees, criminal background check fees, small household repairs in approved child care areas, approved child care training course fees, expenses related to local water, sewer, fire, and health requirements, program materials and equipment, and other costs necessary for completion of the registration process and achieving or maintaining compliance with family child care regulations.

Funding supports council establishment, maintenance, and execution of responsibilities including establishing school readiness benchmarks, conducting needs assessments, developing action plans to increase program participation, coordinating early childhood initiatives, and reporting progress to the State Advisory Council on Early Childhood Education and Care.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary professional development program that recognizes and rewards child care professionals — both staff and administrators — who exceed state licensing and registration requirements for training, education, and experience. The program improves the quality and stability of the child care workforce by supporting participants in advancing their careers through approved training, work experience, and professional activities. Child care staff can achieve up to seven credential levels (1–6 plus 4+), while administrators can achieve up to four levels. Participants receive achievement bonuses, training vouchers, and are eligible for tuition assistance for college degrees through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Staff achievement bonuses: $200–$1,000 paid one time at Levels 2, 3, and 4; $600–$1,000 paid annually at Levels 4+, 5, and 6. Administrator achievement bonuses: $600 paid one time at Level 1; $750–$1,500 paid annually at Levels 2, 3, and 4. Training Vouchers and Reimbursements of up to $400 per year for those credentialed at Level 2 or higher (if funds available). All participants are eligible to receive tuition assistance for Associate's, Bachelor's, or Master's Degrees through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF). Each credential level requires completion of Core of Knowledge (COK) training in six key topics (Child Development, Curriculum, Health/Safety/Nutrition, Special Needs, Professionalism, Community), Professional Activity Units (PAUs), and specified work experience. Credentials are issued for a 12-month period and may be renewed annually.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Coming soon
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers and operators, directors, teachers, assistant teachers, or aides working part-time or full-time in licensed child care centers or Letter of Compliance programs in Maryland. Must work directly with children on a daily basis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Achievement bonuses for reaching credential levels, training vouchers and reimbursements for credential Level 2 or higher providers, and tuition assistance for approved college or university programs (Associate's, Bachelor's, or Master's Degrees) through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund. Supports professional development through approved Core of Knowledge training, Professional Activity Units participation, and college or university enrollment for early childhood education programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Must be a registered family child care provider or work in a licensed child care center or Letter of Compliance program in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider, an operator, director, or staff member (teacher, assistant teacher, or aide) in a licensed child care center or Letter of Compliance program in Maryland
Must work directly with children on a daily basis (excludes regional/district managers, administrative, maintenance, food service, and transportation staff)
Cannot have been sanctioned by the Office of Child Care
Cannot be a substitute or volunteer in a child care program

Must complete approved Core of Knowledge (COK) training for the applicable credential level in six key areas: Child Development, Curriculum, Health/Safety/Nutrition, Special Needs, Professionalism, and Community
Must participate in Professional Activity Units (PAUs) related to the child care profession
Must continue working in a registered or licensed child care program for at least one year after acceptance
Credentials are issued for a 12-month period and must be renewed annually by submitting updated training, Professional Activity Units, and proof of continued employment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants select a credential level pathway based on their qualifications and goals and create a professional development plan aligned with their desired credential level. They complete approved Core of Knowledge (COK) training from MSDE-approved trainers or accredited colleges, accumulate required Professional Activity Units (PAUs) through professional activities such as association membership, conference attendance, mentoring, training presentations, or accreditation participation, and submit documentation to the credentialing branch. Renewal applications open annually and require submission of training completion, PAU documentation, and proof of continued employment. Requests for approval of activities not listed on the standard PAU matrix must be submitted using the Professional Activity Unit (PAU) Approval Form and are reviewed within 60 days. For additional information and assistance, contact workforceadvancementocc.msde@maryland.gov or (410) 767-7852.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Child Care Resource Network (MCCRN) and Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Child Care Resource Network (MCCRN) provides technical assistance to child care providers on starting, expanding, and operating child care centers or family child care homes, covering licensing and compliance, behavioral issues, special needs support, credential development, and program accreditation. MCCRN also administers the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF), which provides tuition assistance for credentialed child care providers to pursue college degrees in early childhood education and related fields.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides technical assistance services including guidance on licensing and compliance, behavioral issues, special needs support, credential development, and program accreditation for child care providers. Also provides tuition assistance through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF) for eligible child care providers to pursue college degrees. CCCPDF funding covers tuition, college fees, and textbooks for degree programs in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, and Special Education at participating Maryland colleges and universities. Payments are made directly to the college or university, not reimbursed to participants. CCCPDF also provides financial support and resources for child care providers to advance their professional qualifications and training.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First-time Applications due by March 1st; Continuation Applications due by June 30th
structured_extraction.program_audience: Existing and potential center-based and family child care providers, Head Start programs, nursery schools, cooperatives, drop-in centers, playgroups, community and non-profit organizations, community groups, employers, and public agencies seeking to expand child care resources. For the CCCPDF, credentialed child care providers seeking to obtain a college education and advance their professional qualifications.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance for licensing, compliance, behavioral support, special needs services, credential development, and accreditation. CCCPDF funding can be used for tuition, college fees, and textbooks toward completion of a college degree in approved fields (Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, Special Education), as well as general professional development and career advancement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. CCCPDF participants must work in a licensed Maryland child care center or be a registered family child care provider in Maryland.
requirements_list: For CCCPDF: Must participate in the Maryland Child Care Credential Program at Level Two or higher
For CCCPDF: Must work in a licensed child care center or be a registered family child care provider in Maryland and work at least 10 hours per week
For CCCPDF: Must fulfill entrance requirements at the participating college of choice
For CCCPDF: Must have at least one year of documented experience working with groups of children in an approved setting
For CCCPDF: Must maintain employment in an approved child care facility in Maryland while participating in the program
For CCCPDF: Must participate in professional development
For CCCPDF: Must agree to complete service requirement as a provider in an approved child care facility in Maryland for at least 20 hours per week after degree completion
For CCCPDF: Must maintain at least 2.50 cumulative GPA from point of first entering the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For technical assistance, access services through the Maryland Child Care Resource Network. For the CCCPDF: Step 1 - Schedule an appointment with the CCCPDF Coordinator at the participating college to which you have been accepted. Step 2 - Apply directly to the college/university through the CCCPDF Coordinator. First-time applications are due by March 1st; continuation applications are due by June 30th. Applications must be completed and submitted by the deadline to be processed. Applicants must first be accepted into a participating college before applying for the Fund.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Quality Rating and Improvement System (QRIS) that awards child care and early education programs ratings from 1 to 5 stars based on meeting standards in areas like developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement. The program helps early childhood and school-age care programs improve their services with the goal of increasing the number of high-quality care options in Maryland. Participating providers receive support from regional Quality Assurance Specialists, training resources, and a roadmap for quality improvement to help them improve their operations, educational quality, and overall ratings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a direct payment for specified use to participating programs. Additionally, participating providers receive guidance from a regional Quality Assurance Specialist assigned by county/region, training resources, work group access, and a roadmap for continuous quality improvement. Providers submit evidence of meeting Maryland EXCELS Standards through an online system and receive ratings for each standard area as well as an overall quality rating from 1 to 5. Regional Quality Assurance Specialists are assigned by county/region (including Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Cecil & Harford, Carroll & Howard, Montgomery, Allegany, Frederick, Garrett & Washington, The Eastern Shore, Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's, and Prince George's) and provide ongoing assistance with increasing quality ratings, training opportunities, work groups, and access to resources.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing
structured_extraction.contact_email: Regional specialist email varies by county
structured_extraction.contact_phone: Regional specialist phone varies by county; general: (410) 767-0100
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early childhood or school-age child care programs, including child care centers and family child care providers seeking to improve program quality and earn higher quality ratings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides technical support, training, and guidance to improve child care and early education practices in areas such as developmentally-appropriate practices, professional development, and family engagement. May also provide direct payments for specified use to participating programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Quality Assurance Specialists are assigned by county/region including: Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Cecil & Harford, Carroll & Howard, Montgomery, Allegany, Frederick, Garrett & Washington, The Eastern Shore, Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's, and Prince George's.
requirements_list: Must operate an early childhood or school-age child care program.
Must be committed to providing high-quality care and education that exceeds basic licensing requirements.
Participate in Maryland EXCELS as a child care or early education provider
Commitment to quality improvement
Willingness to meet Maryland EXCELS Standards in areas like developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement
Ability to document and upload evidence of meeting standards through the online system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To participate, providers can visit the program website at http://marylandexcels.org to create an account and get started. Once enrolled, contact a regional Quality Assurance Specialist assigned to your county or region for assistance. Work with the specialist to create and upload evidence of meeting the Maryland EXCELS Standards into the online system. Evidence is reviewed by Maryland EXCELS staff who provide ratings for each standard area and an overall rating. Regional specialists are available throughout Maryland to provide support with training, work groups, and resources.
