structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local Lead Agencies designate a program director or project manager as the Grants Submission Coordinator (GSC) who receives an Entity Code and log-on credentials to access the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website at https://msde.sftp.md.gov/. The GSC and authorized personnel log in (creating a new password on initial login) and access shared folders for their grant programs. To submit, grantees double-click the appropriate folder and either drag-and-drop or use the upload button to submit files. All grant applications, reports, and amendment requests must be labeled according to MSDE file naming conventions (e.g., INTG_EntityID_SFY_CLIG_APP.pdf for applications, or INTG_EntityID_SFY_CLIG_GrantNumber_TypeCode.pdf for reports and amendments). After uploading to the ToMSDE folder, grantees must send an email notification to their assigned fiscal grants liaison specifying the document name(s). Grantees should save a screenshot of the file upload timestamp as proof of submission. Documents sent by MSDE to grantees in the FromMSDE folder are subject to deletion 30 days from posting date, so grantees should immediately download and save documents locally. The GSC must notify the fiscal grants liaison immediately if authorized personnel change to deactivate access for departing employees.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state special education program that provides formula and project grants to local governments and non-profits to create and operate early intervention services, while also directly delivering free, family-centered early intervention services to infants and toddlers with disabilities and developmental delays from birth to age three. Teachers, therapists, and providers work with families to build on strengths, address family goals and concerns, help families learn about their child's needs, and connect families with community resources. Services are delivered in natural environments such as homes, child care settings, or community locations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides formula and project grants to local jurisdictions to support early intervention services. It also directly delivers free, family-centered early intervention services to infants and toddlers with disabilities and developmental delays from birth to age three. Services include developmental screenings, evaluations, individualized family service plans (IFSP), therapeutic services (speech, physical, and occupational therapy), and coaching provided in the home, child care settings, or community locations. All evaluations and services are provided at no cost to families.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and non-profit organizations that provide services to infants and toddlers with disabilities, as well as families of infants and toddlers from birth to age three with disabilities, developmental delays, or medical conditions that could impact development. Referrals can be made by parents, child care providers, doctors, grandparents, nurses, friends, or other relatives.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support the creation and operation of local early intervention services including developmental screenings and evaluations, individualized family service plans, therapeutic services (speech, occupational, and physical therapy), coaching and family support services, community resource coordination, and services provided in natural environments such as homes, child care settings, or community locations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to all children from birth to age three living in Maryland.
requirements_list: Child must be from birth to age three and live in Maryland
Child must have a disability, developmental delay, or medical condition that affects or could affect their development
Child does not require a diagnosis to be eligible; developmental delay alone qualifies for eligibility determination
Free developmental assessment is provided to determine eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For families: 1. Submit a referral online at referral.mditp.org or call 1-800-535-0182 to obtain local contact information and make a referral by phone. 2. After the referral, someone from the local Infants and Toddlers program will contact you to discuss the child's development and concerns. 3. A developmental screening or evaluation appointment is scheduled and conducted in the home or another location of the family's choice. 4. If the child is eligible, the family becomes part of the early intervention team and together develops an individualized family service plan. All evaluations and services are provided free of charge. Families provide permission for all assessments and services and can stop or change services at any time. For local jurisdictions: Applications are submitted annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides state funding to supplement federal meal reimbursements, allowing participating economically disadvantaged schools to offer free breakfast consumed in the classroom at the start of each school day. Currently, 581 schools participate in MMFA across Maryland. The program increases students' access to and participation in breakfast, ensuring all children in qualifying schools have access to nutritious meals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State funds supplement federal meal reimbursements to allow participating schools to offer free breakfast in the classroom. Currently 581 schools participate in MMFA. Breakfasts must meet USDA nutrition guidelines and Dietary Guidelines for Americans and must be consumed in the classroom.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children in economically disadvantaged schools throughout Maryland; schools must meet economically disadvantaged criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding for nutritious breakfast programs served in the classroom to students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Economically disadvantaged schools throughout Maryland. Currently 581 schools participate.
requirements_list: School must meet economically disadvantaged criteria
Meals must be consumed in the classroom
Breakfasts must meet USDA nutrition guidelines and Dietary Guidelines for Americans
Schools must be participating institutions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Qualifying economically disadvantaged schools apply through the Maryland State Department of Education's Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs. Contact scnp_mailbox.msde@maryland.gov or (410) 767-0199 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (Autism Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides community-based, long-term, person-centered therapeutic services and support to eligible children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder to enable home and community living as an alternative to institutional care. Services include adult life planning, environmental accessibility adaptations, family consultation, intensive individual support services, residential habilitation, respite care, and therapeutic integration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The waiver covers community-based therapeutic services and support including: Intensive Individual Support Services (IISS) - one-on-one assistance based on the child's need for interventions and support to help children acquire, retain, and improve self-help, socialization, communication, daily living, functional living, behavior management, and adaptive skills; Therapeutic Integration (TI) or Intensive Therapeutic Integration (ITI) - structured programs outside school hours providing therapeutic activities and expressive therapies for children with socialization, isolation, hyperactivity, impulse control, and behavior problems; Respite Care - short-term supervision and assistance with activities of daily living; Environmental Accessibility Adaptations (EAA) - funding for physical adaptations to the home necessary for health, welfare, and safety; Family Consultation (FC) - individualized consultation and training provided to the child's family; Adult Life Planning (ALP) - family-centered education and support in accessing adult community services; and Residential Habilitation (Regular or Intensive) - community-based residential placement for children who cannot live at home because they require highly supervised and supportive environments with the goal of returning the child to the home. Participants also receive service coordination through their local education agency and qualify for full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and mental health services. Children must maintain eligibility by using at least 5 hours of Autism Waiver services per month.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 45 days from the date of application letter from MDH to complete the financial eligibility application
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and youth ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old who have Autism Spectrum Disorder and meet institutional level of care requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used for environmental home modifications, therapeutic services, family consultation and training, one-on-one support services, residential habilitation services, respite care, therapeutic integration programs, and case management services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Children must reside in Maryland. Available statewide with over 60 approved provider agencies. There is a military exception: Dependents of US Military Service members invited to apply to the Autism Waiver while the family is out of the state for military services shall be offered an opportunity to apply upon request when they return to Maryland and meet all technical eligibility requirements.
requirements_list: Have a current educational classification of Autism or a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder
Be ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old
Reside in Maryland

Receive early intervention or special education services identified through an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) for ages 1-5, an Individual Education Program (IEP) in an early childhood or Kindergarten setting for ages 3-5, or an IEP with 15 hours or more of special education and related services and/or 1:1 adult supports per week for first grade through high school exit
Meet eligibility requirements for an Intermediate Care Facility for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICF-IID) institutional level of care
Be able to be safely served and maintained in the home and community with Autism Waiver services
Meet financial eligibility for Medical Assistance with monthly income not exceeding 300 percent of Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits and countable assets not exceeding $2,000
Choose the Autism Waiver as the waiver that best meets the child's needs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Call the Autism Waiver Registry Helpline at 1-866-417-3480 to express interest and register on the Autism Waiver Waitlist. Provide child's name, date of birth, address, county of residence, contact information, and confirm diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder and existence of IFSP or IEP with at least 15 hours of special education/related services per week. 2. Maryland Department of Health (MDH) vendor conducts initial screening during intake call based on parent self-report. If technical eligibility criteria are met, the child's name is added to the Registry and MSDE is notified with a letter sent to the family. If technical eligibility criteria are not met, family receives a 30-day deadline to provide updated/additional information. 3. MSDE verifies technical eligibility: resident of Maryland, under age 21, Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis, and IFSP or IEP with 15 hours of special education/health-related services. The child's name is added to the Autism Waiver Waitlist with a confirmation letter sent to family. 4. When a vacancy occurs and the child reaches the top of the waitlist based on chronological order, an invitation to apply is sent to the family giving a 45-day deadline to accept the invitation, establish contact with the AW Contact at the local education agency (LEA), complete the technical eligibility checklist, and submit the financial application. Enclosures include Medical Assistance (MA) Financial Application, Parental Rights and Responsibilities, AW Contact List, and Application Documentation Checklist. 5. Family works with the AW Contact at the LEA to confirm technical, financial, and medical eligibility. Work with the Service Coordinator to complete the financial eligibility application within 45 days from the date of application letter. Contribute to the Level of Care assessment process that determines medical eligibility. 6. Receive notification of eligibility from the State. If eligible, the letter includes a start date to begin Autism Waiver services. 7. Attend a multidisciplinary team meeting to develop a Plan of Care. 8. Maintain eligibility by using at least 5 hours of Autism Waiver services per month. Application is processed based on chronological order from the time the child's name is placed on the Waitlist. The number of available slots is determined by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). Approved provider agencies deliver services. Contact information for the AW Contact at your local education agency or early intervention program is available by county.

structured_extraction.program_description: A required pre-service training course for individuals seeking to acquire a Child Care Center License or a Family Child Care Registration in Maryland. The course is a 6-hour classroom training covering Health, Safety, and Nutrition topics in medication administration theory and practice, provided by licensed Maryland Registered Nurses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A six-hour classroom training course combining theory and practice in medication administration, covering Health, Safety, and Nutrition. The training is provided by licensed Maryland Registered Nurses. Participants must pass content and skill tests to receive a certificate of completion. Many trainers also offer Special Needs Support Services for individualized medical management and treatment plan/procedure skills competency support (Type 1 Diabetes, Seizure management, Tube Feeding, Urinary Catheter, Oxygen Mask/Cannula). Spanish-language training is available through select trainers.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Division of Early Childhood - Office of Child Care
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking to acquire a Child Care Center License or a Family Child Care Registration in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in medication administration for child care providers, including theory and practical skill development in medication administration, with optional special needs support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through an extensive network of licensed Registered Nurse trainers serving all counties. Multiple trainers are available in most regions to provide flexible training options.
requirements_list: Must be seeking a Child Care Center License or Family Child Care Registration
Must complete the six-hour classroom training course covering Health, Safety, and Nutrition
Must pass content and skill tests to receive certificate of completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Locate an approved Medication Administration Trainer from the official trainer list (available at the program website) based on your geographic location and any specific needs (such as special needs support or Spanish-language instruction). Contact the trainer directly using the provided phone number or email address to schedule the six-hour classroom training course. Complete the training and pass both the content and skill competency tests to receive a certificate of completion.

structured_extraction.program_name: NSLP and SBP Training for Residential Child Care Institutions and Nonprofit Private Schools
structured_extraction.program_description: Twice-annual administrative meetings providing updates on USDA regulations, guidance, and professional development for Residential Child Care Institutions and Nonprofit Private Schools participating in the National School Lunch and School Breakfast Programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free twice-annual administrative training meetings for Residential Child Care Institutions and Nonprofit Private Schools covering USDA regulations, guidance updates, and professional development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential Child Care Institutions and Nonprofit Private Schools participating in school meal programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and professional development on USDA nutrition program regulations and guidance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residential child care institutions and nonprofit private schools
requirements_list: Participation in National School Lunch Program and/or School Breakfast Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs for dates and locations of twice-annual administrative meetings.

structured_extraction.program_name: National School Lunch Program (NSLP) and School Breakfast Program (SBP) - Public School Systems Training
structured_extraction.program_description: Twice-annual administrative meetings providing updates on USDA regulations, guidance, and professional development for public school systems participating in the National School Lunch and School Breakfast Programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free twice-annual administrative training meetings covering USDA regulations, guidance updates, and professional development for school nutrition staff.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public school systems participating in the National School Lunch Program and School Breakfast Program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and professional development on USDA nutrition program regulations and guidance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland public school systems
requirements_list: Participation in National School Lunch Program and/or School Breakfast Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs for dates and locations of twice-annual administrative meetings.

structured_extraction.program_description: State aid program that helps pay for students with disabilities who are placed in nonpublic special education schools through the Individualized Education Program (IEP) process. The state covers a share of the tuition cost based on state law. The program covers both MSDE-approved day and residential programs as well as individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state special education programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state reimburses a portion of the tuition cost for students placed in nonpublic special education schools. The state's share is calculated according to Education Article §8-415 of the Maryland Annotated Code. Reimbursement includes standard educational and related services, extended school year services, residential services when applicable, and related services/supplemental aides/program modifications as outlined in the IEP. Children are counted in the September 30th enrollment with a code indicating nonpublic placement. Per diem rates are provided for approved programs, and cost sheets accompany applications to confirm annual charges for services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted within 30 calendar days of entry date, discharge date, or service revision date. For ESY or entry dates occurring during July/August, submit by September 30. For entry dates occurring between June 3 and June 30, submit by July 7.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local school systems and special education supervisors/directors seeking state reimbursement for students with disabilities placed in nonpublic special education schools through the IEP process
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition costs for nonpublic special education school placements for students with disabilities, including standard educational and related services, extended school year services, residential services when applicable, and supplemental aides and program modifications as outlined in the IEP
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Individual placements may include out-of-state special education programs when deemed appropriate by the IEP team.
requirements_list: Student must have an Individualized Education Program (IEP) indicating placement in a nonpublic special education school
Nonpublic school must be MSDE-approved (for day and residential programs) or meet individual placement approval requirements
Student must be enrolled and counted in the September 30th enrollment count
For MSDE-approved programs: cost sheet must be submitted with application

For individual placements: IEP team minutes supporting placement, letter from service-providing school confirming ability to implement FAPE in least restrictive environment, and copy of mediated or due process agreement (if applicable) must be submitted
Local school system Special Education Supervisor/Director or designee must verify and sign the application
All information must be typed or printed legibly on official NTAP application forms
Financially responsible local education agency must be identified
Medical Assistance Number should be provided when available
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: School districts submit applications for either MSDE-approved day and residential programs or request individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state special education programs. Applications are reviewed and processed by the Division of Early Intervention and Special Education Services. For MSDE-approved programs, submit the completed NTAP application (NSS/NTAP FORM FY 2023) with an accompanying approved cost sheet. For individual placements, submit the completed application with cost sheet, IEP team minutes, school letter, and any mediated/due process documentation. Applications must be submitted within 30 calendar days of entry date, discharge date, or service revision date. ESY or entry dates in July/August must be submitted by September 30. Entry dates between June 3-30 must be submitted by July 7. Written notice may be provided if unable to meet timelines. MSDE may conduct audit and investigation of submitted information. Discrepancies or noncompliance findings may result in required refund of State funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Outdoor Nature-Based Child Care License Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An innovative initiative by the Maryland State Department of Education that expands high-quality child care options in Maryland by allowing early education in outdoor, nature-based settings. The program creates opportunities for child care providers to offer nature-based care in outdoor environments through a pilot licensing framework, providing funding and technical support for the development and operation of these programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding and technical support for child care providers to establish, develop, and operate nature-based child care services in outdoor settings through a pilot licensing framework.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and early education organizations seeking to establish or operate outdoor nature-based child care programs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing, developing, and operating nature-based child care services in outdoor settings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed or approved child care provider
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are currently open for interested child care providers and organizations. Visit the program page for details on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Patty Centers / Family Support Center Network (formerly Family Support Centers)
structured_extraction.program_description: A network of 24 Patty Centers (formerly known as Family Support Centers) located in 14 Maryland counties that offer free educational and health-related services to parents and their children ages birth through three. The centers promote optimal child development, help parents build effective parenting skills, create supportive parent networks, and connect families to community resources. Services are provided either on-site or through referral and include infant and toddler care assessment, parent education, adult education, family literacy, job readiness training, health education and referrals, home visits, peer support, and service coordination between agencies. Early Head Start programs within the network specifically serve Southern Anne Arundel County, seven communities in Baltimore City, Caroline County, Cecil County, Dorchester County, and Talbot County. The network is funded by the Maryland State Department of Education, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, private foundations, corporations, and individuals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including quality infant and toddler care and assessment, parent education classes, adult education and family literacy programs, job readiness training, health education and referrals, home visits for some services, peer support groups, and coordination of services between agencies to connect families with community resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents and their children ages birth through three in participating Maryland counties. No income requirements specified.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services are designed to promote optimal child development, help adults develop effective parenting skills, support school and employment goals, provide community support networks, and connect families to agencies and resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in 24 Patty Centers located in 14 Maryland counties: Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Baltimore City, Carroll, Cecil, Dorchester, Frederick, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Washington, and Worcester. Early Head Start programs specifically serve Southern Anne Arundel County, seven communities in Baltimore City, Caroline County, Cecil County, Dorchester County, and Talbot County. For more information and to locate the nearest Patty Center, visit the Maryland Family Network website at marylandfamilynetwork.org.
requirements_list: Children must be ages birth through three
Parents and children must be residents of counties with Patty Centers
No income requirements specified
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families can visit their local Patty Center directly to access services. Contact your local Patty Center directly using the provided phone numbers and email addresses for enrollment and service information. For more information and to locate the nearest Patty Center, visit the Maryland Family Network website at marylandfamilynetwork.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: Under the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, all three- and four-year-old children from families earning incomes at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level are granted access to high-quality full-day Pre-K at no cost to families. This program represents the family-facing benefit — eligible children are enrolled with approved Pre-K grantee providers including public school systems, private child care centers, Head Start programs, and family child care networks throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free full-day pre-kindergarten services for eligible children from families earning at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level. Children are enrolled at no cost with approved Pre-K grantee providers across all 24 Maryland counties and Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Three- and four-year-old children from low-income families earning at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: High-quality full-day Pre-K educational services to prepare children for kindergarten and school success.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland in all 24 counties plus Baltimore City. Specific approved grantee providers vary by county.
requirements_list: Child must be three or four years old
Family income must be at or below 300% of Federal Poverty Level
Must be enrolled with an approved Pre-K grantee provider
Approved providers include public school systems, private child care centers, Head Start programs, and family child care networks
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families should contact the Maryland State Department of Education or visit the Division of Early Childhood website to identify approved Pre-K grantees in their area, then enroll directly with their chosen approved provider.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that provides funding to local education agencies (LEAs), Head Start programs, and qualified private providers to deliver high-quality full-day pre-kindergarten and school readiness services to three- and four-year-old children from families earning at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level. Authorized under the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, the grant supports both traditional Pre-K Grant programs and Pre-K Expansion Blueprint funding. Total funding available is $26,644,000 with an estimated average grant award of $400,000, supporting approximately 50 grants at a rate of $19,950 per full-day slot. Programs must provide a minimum of 180 instructional days annually with an instructional day of at least 6.5 hours.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding of up to $19,950 per full-day prekindergarten slot. Total funding available is $26,644,000 with an estimated average grant award of $400,000, supporting approximately 50 grants. Approved uses include: teacher and assistant teacher salaries and fringe benefits (commensurate with local LEA salaries based on credentials and experience), equipment, materials and instructional supplies, MSDE-approved curriculum resources aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards, reasonable rental/mortgage and utility costs (prorated by square footage), technology costs (not exceeding 10% of total), accreditation and Maryland EXCELS rating maintenance costs, professional learning activities, screening and intervention services, program evaluation and monitoring costs (not exceeding 5%), meals meeting CACFP requirements, academic field trips, and indirect costs (not exceeding 15% for nonprofits or 10% for other grantees). Funds may NOT be used for supplanting existing funds, capital improvements, costs incurred prior to grant approval, or transportation (except field trips).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, March 11, 2026. No later than 5:00 pm EDT. (Extended from original March 9 deadline; amended 3/6/2026)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dr. Nykia Washington, Prekindergarten and Mixed Delivery Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies (school systems), Head Start programs, and qualified private child care providers (including center-based programs and family child care networks) licensed or registered to serve young children, seeking to deliver high-quality full-day pre-kindergarten services to eligible three- and four-year-old children from low-income families in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports administration and delivery of high-quality full-day prekindergarten programs and school readiness services aligned with the Blueprint for Maryland's Future and Maryland Early Learning Standards. Approved uses include staff salaries and fringe benefits, equipment and classroom materials, evidence-based curriculum resources, technology, accreditation maintenance, professional learning, health screenings and intervention services, program evaluation, meals, and academic field trips.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland to all local education agencies, private providers, and Head Start programs meeting eligibility requirements in all 24 counties plus Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local School System (LSS), Head Start program, or qualified vendor as defined in COMAR 13a.06.02
Must hold a valid license or registration issued by MSDE (if applicable)
Must meet Maryland EXCELS rating requirement: Level 3 or higher for private providers; Level 4 or higher for public providers
Must serve children from families with household incomes at or below 300% of Federal Poverty Level
Must provide high-quality full-day pre-kindergarten services with instructional day of at least 6.5 hours for minimum 180 school days per year
Must align programming with the Blueprint for Maryland's Future and Maryland Early Learning Standards
Must participate in Maryland EXCELS program with plan to maintain or achieve Level 5

Lead teachers must meet Blueprint for Maryland's Future requirements and hold either: (1) P-3 state teaching certificate; (2) bachelor's degree in early childhood education or related field; (3) bachelor's degree in related field from accredited foreign institution verified as equivalent; (4) bachelor's degree in any field with minimum CLASS scores; or (5) documented 10+ years early childhood experience (20 hours/week, 180 days/year) plus CLASS assessment minimum scores
Lead teachers without P-3 certification must achieve minimum CLASS scores: Emotional Support Domain 5.00, Classroom Organization Domain 5.00, Instructional Support Domain 3.00

Lead teachers with P-3 certification must receive salary commensurate with local LEA teachers in respective county; those without P-3 certification must receive minimum salary per Lead Teacher Salary Schedule based on credentials and experience
For classrooms with more than 10 students, an Assistant Teacher must be staffed

Assistant teachers must have high school diploma and by July 1, 2027 (private) or 2027-2028 school year (public) earn CDA with preschool designation, associate degree in ECE, or documented 15+ years ECE experience (private) or 5+ years (public) as of July 1, 2024

For Montessori programs: staff must hold bachelor's degree plus Montessori credential from AMI, AMS, or MACTE-accredited program; student-to-staff ratio of 10:1 (max 20 students under 5) or 14:1 (max 28 students if some are 5+)

Must designate a qualified instructional oversight person with bachelor's degree or higher in early childhood education or related field, dedicating minimum 8-10 hours monthly (director teaching full-time cannot serve this role)
Lead teachers must be hired by July 1, 2026 to avoid disruption in grant funds

Programs seeking renewal or expansion must demonstrate track record of success: maintained lead teachers meeting all requirements, minimum EXCELS Level 3 or higher, compliance with reporting and fiscal guidelines, no corrective action plans, and 85% seat fill rate by December 31, 2025
Programs must implement valid and reliable child assessment tools and provide teacher training on implementation and data use
Programs must provide health screenings and referrals for vision, hearing, speech and language, general health, and physical development
Programs must offer or coordinate support services for families including parenting support, physical and mental health services, and early intervention
Must use High-Quality Instructional Materials (HQIM) with fidelity

Must provide at least 20 hours of professional learning for instructional staff annually aligned with Blueprint priorities including science of reading, early mathematics, social foundations, and CLASS improvement
Must develop SMART goals addressing standards alignment, instructional practice, quality improvement, and child outcomes
Must describe income verification procedures and maintain documentation on-site for family eligibility
Must demonstrate procedures for identifying and appropriately serving students with disabilities, students experiencing homelessness, and multilingual learners
Programs must submit Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) by September 30, 2026 if LEA receives Blueprint funding
For Head Start applicants: must submit letter of support from Head Start program-funded grantee if applicant is not the funded grantee
All grant requirements must be met prior to start of grant year and before invoices or advance requests can be paid
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted electronically through Qualtrics (https://msde.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0qxUC1IT7xwk08C) by 5:00 p.m. EDT on March 11, 2026. Paper applications are available for reference only. Applicants first answer eligibility questions confirming the program meets basic requirements. Based on eligibility responses, applicants are directed to either a Full Application (all new applicants and existing grantees without track record of success, requiring minimum 80 points) or a Modified Short Form Application (existing grantees seeking renewal/expansion with documented success, requiring minimum 45 points). The application is divided into four sections: Applicant Information, Slots Requested, Application Questions (Full or Modified), and Appendices. Applicants cannot move backward between sections once completed. Full applications cover 10 scored sections: Program Eligibility/Maryland EXCELS and Accreditation (10 pts), Evidence of Need/Market Analysis (10 pts), Measurable Goals (20 pts), Program Quality and Curriculum (10 pts), Plan of Operation (10 pts), Staffing/Key Personnel/Management Plan (10 pts), Project Timeline/Implementation Plan (10 pts), Collaboration and Sustainability (10 pts), Fiscal Systems and Controls (10 pts), and Budget and Budget Narrative (10 pts). Required appendices must be uploaded including works cited, income eligibility policy documentation, key personnel resumes, and budget forms. Applicants review all answers and may download a PDF copy before final submission; once submitted, changes cannot be made. MSDE provides customer service support sessions and office hours; email prekexpansiongrant.msde@maryland.gov with subject line 'Pre-K Expansion Application' for assistance. Upon award, grantees must submit signed MOU by September 30, 2026. MSDE provides monitoring and technical assistance throughout the grant period.

structured_extraction.program_description: A USDA Team Nutrition training grant that targeted middle schools to increase students' selection and consumption of vegetables and fruits through culinary training, food service operations, lunchroom environment strategies, food tasting events, and nutrition education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant-funded training and technical assistance in culinary and food service operations, Smarter Lunchrooms strategies, food tasting events, and nutrition education. Included development of family engagement wellness toolkit for families and parents supporting wellness policy implementation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Middle schools in participating school systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Culinary training, food service operations training, lunchroom environment improvements, food tasting events, nutrition education, and family wellness programming
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Five targeted school systems: Allegany, Baltimore City, Montgomery, Prince George's, and Wicomico counties
requirements_list: Participation in National School Lunch Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This program was implemented from 2016 through 2019 and is no longer active.

structured_extraction.program_name: Public-Private Partnership (PPP) — Nonpublic Special Education Partnership Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A funding agreement between a local school system and a Maryland State Department of Education-approved nonpublic special education program to serve students with significant and intensive needs in the least restrictive environment. The program enhances Individualized Education Program services for students in their community and is especially beneficial for students with short-term needs, requiring an alternative special education program, experiencing a crisis, or awaiting a more intensive placement. The PPP framework also includes a Preventive Service Partnership component, which is an initiative designed by a local school system to address the needs of individual students or groups of students at high risk of nonpublic placement by providing wrap-around supportive services within the public school setting, thereby building local capacity and avoiding more restrictive placements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State funding contribution to local school systems for partnership tuition agreements with approved nonpublic special education programs. Payment is based on full-time equivalent (FTE) seats utilized during the school year. The MSDE funds only the actual number of FTE seats used, calculated through end-of-year reconciliation of total enrollment days. The state's cost contribution cannot exceed the cost for equivalent placements through the traditional nonpublic tuition assistance program. Payment is cost-neutral to the State, and local education agencies are responsible for funding of any unused FTE seats. The Preventive Service Partnership component funds wrap-around supportive services within the public school setting to prevent students at high risk of nonpublic placement from requiring such placement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications submitted to MSDE by June 1 annually; new partnership proposals should initiate discussions with MSDE by February 1.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sheila F. Philip, JD / MSDE Division of Early Intervention and Special Education Services, Nonpublic Special Education Section Chief
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local school systems serving students with significant and intensive special education needs who require nonpublic special education programs, as well as school systems seeking to prevent students at high risk of nonpublic placement from requiring such placement through preventive wrap-around services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhancing Individualized Education Program services for students in their community through partnerships with nonpublic special education programs. Supports short-term placements, access to public school instruction and activities, and transitioning of students to less restrictive programs. Can also fund preventive services and wrap-around service interventions within the public school setting to avoid more restrictive nonpublic school placements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Partnership must be with a Maryland State Department of Education-approved nonpublic special education program
Services must address students with significant and intensive needs
Services must be provided in the least restrictive environment
Application must be submitted at minimum 30 calendar days prior to request for state funding
Annual application submission required by June 1
Must submit MSDE Public/Private Partnership Application
Must submit Public/Private Partnership Agreement or Contract
Must submit budget completed by nonpublic provider using MSDE budget packet
Must submit MSDE Public/Private Partnership Fiscal Worksheet
Biannual submission of monitoring data required
Reconciliation finalized at close of each fiscal year based on actual FTE seats used
State funding is cost-neutral; state cost cannot exceed equivalent traditional nonpublic tuition assistance
For Preventive Service Partnership: target students must be at high risk of placement in a nonpublic special education school
For Preventive Service Partnership: services must be delivered within the public school setting using wrap-around supportive services
For Preventive Service Partnership: partnership must address a targeted, immediate need of the student or school system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local school systems seeking to establish a new partnership should collect data supporting program need, outline a basic proposal with implementation timeline, identify potential location to house the partnership, and contact the MSDE Division of Early Intervention and Special Education Services, Nonpublic Special Education Section Chief to explore fund availability and finalize an action plan. For new proposals, local school systems initiate discussions with MSDE by February 1. Applications must be submitted to MSDE by June 1 annually and include the MSDE Public/Private Partnership Application, Partnership Agreement or Contract, nonpublic provider budget using MSDE packet, and Fiscal Worksheet. Mid-year enrollment and outcome data reports are due January 15, end-of-year reports due June 1. MSDE provides notice of intent to fund by July 15, with fiscal year reconciliation completed by July 30, and finalized signed contracts submitted prior to release of state funds. For Preventive Service Partnerships, local school systems develop a preventive service plan to be submitted upon request, outlining how wrap-around supportive services will be provided within the public school setting.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps child care providers expand their business and access state prekindergarten funding. The initiative provides guidance on meeting requirements for Pre-K grants and simplifies the grant application process by pairing providers with Pre-K Specialists who walk them through each step of the process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides access to state prekindergarten funding and offers technical assistance to help child care providers meet grant requirements and navigate the application process. Providers receive support from Pre-K Specialists who guide them through each step of the grant application process. A grant consideration checklist is available to help applicants determine if the grant is appropriate and to ensure readiness before beginning the application process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers seeking to expand their business and access state Pre-K funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expanding child care services to include state-funded prekindergarten programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a child care provider
Must meet state requirements for Pre-K grants
Organization must have technical expertise, personnel, and financial capacity to successfully provide services as described in the Grant Information Guide
All organizational stakeholders must be supportive of applying for the grant
Applicant must understand and meet eligibility criteria outlined in the Grant Information Guide
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Push to Pre-K Specialists walk providers through each step of the process, including meeting grant requirements and completing the application. A grant consideration checklist is available to help applicants determine if the grant is appropriate and to ensure readiness before beginning the application process. Applicants should review the Grant Information Guide, verify organizational eligibility, assess technical expertise and financial capacity, and confirm stakeholder support.

structured_extraction.program_description: The School Breakfast Program provides children with nutritious breakfasts that studies show are correlated with higher test scores, decreased emotional and behavioral problems, reduced food insecurity, less frequent visits to the nurse, and fewer school absences. The program reimburses schools and residential child care institutions with federal dollars for meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards and the Dietary Guidelines for Americans, helping cover the costs of producing breakfast meals. All 24 Maryland public school systems, 17 non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions participate, serving over 898,000 students with access to nutritious breakfasts each day.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses schools and childcare institutions with federal dollars for meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards and the Dietary Guidelines for Americans, providing direct payments to help cover the costs of producing breakfast meals. Students from families with incomes at or below 130-185% of the poverty level may receive meals at a free or reduced price. Students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits are eligible for free meals. The cost of school breakfast is determined by each school district.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools and residential child care institutions, including all 24 Maryland public school systems, 17 non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions; serves students enrolled in participating schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for nutritious breakfast meals for students and children that meet USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans; funds help cover the costs of producing breakfast meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties; available in all 24 Maryland public school systems, 17 non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions.
requirements_list: School or institution must be public, private non-profit, or a residential childcare institution
Must serve breakfasts meeting USDA nutrition guidelines and Dietary Guidelines for Americans
Students from families with incomes at or below 130-185% of the poverty level qualify for free or reduced-price meals
Students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits are eligible for free meals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and institutions participate through the Maryland State Department of Education's Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs. Students may qualify for free or reduced-price breakfast based on family income eligibility by applying through their school district. Applications are submitted annually.

Reimburses eligible institutions for milk served to children, including schools with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to school meal programs. Funds help lower the cost of milk served to children.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses schools, childcare centers, and eligible camps for milk served to children. Eligible institutions are those not participating in other federal child nutrition meal programs. Schools with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to school meal programs may also participate. Payments directly offset the cost of milk served to children.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for milk served to children; funds must be used to lower the cost of milk served to children.

requirements_list: Institution must not participate in other federal child nutrition meal programs
Must serve milk to children
Schools with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to school meal programs may participate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and institutions apply through the Maryland State Department of Education's Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs for reimbursement eligibility. Contact USDA for additional application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education provides annual grants to qualified non-profit organizations that offer enriching educational programs to Maryland students. Eligible programs provide learning experiences aligned with the state's curricular and educational priorities and cannot be replicated in a classroom. Programs emphasize experiential learning and one-on-one support services, including free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, and tutoring. Pre- and post-visit activities for teachers can connect experiences to classroom curriculum. Professional development for teachers that links SAI programs to the classroom is also funded.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants of approximately $6,706,449 are available to fund between 60-65 qualified non-profit organizations (501(c)(3) in good standing). Grant funds must be used to provide direct services to students and teachers within the fiscal year for which they are granted. Funds may be used for: salaries, wages, and stipends for direct service to students and educators; supplies and materials to implement the educational program; outreach, engagement, informational, and marketing tools to expand reach; equipment necessary for direct service to students and teachers; and contractual expenses. Funds may NOT be used for: construction or capital improvements; transportation of students; utilities or operating costs; and food. Organizations must demonstrate that less than 50% of their operating budget comes from state grants (except Baltimore Zoo). SAIs must serve primarily public school students (at least 80% of schools served must be public schools, with no more than 20% from nonpublic or homeschools).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, June 13, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified non-profit organizations that provide enriching educational programs to Maryland students. Applicants must be 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations in good standing and provide direct service to Maryland students and teachers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct services to students and teachers including: salaries, wages, and stipends for personnel providing direct service; supplies and materials to implement the educational program; outreach, engagement, informational, and marketing tools to expand reach; equipment necessary for direct service; contractual expenses; free or reduced admission for students; full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities; mentoring and tutoring services; pre- and post-visit activities for teachers to connect experiences to classroom curriculum; and professional development opportunities for teachers. Funds cannot be used for construction, capital improvements, student transportation, utilities, operating costs, food, indirect costs, or overhead.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to programs serving Maryland students statewide. For fiscal year 2027, between 60-65 programs are expected to be funded.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization in good standing and based in Maryland
Must be incorporated or registered under Maryland law and current in payment of all tax obligations to the State
Must provide direct service to Maryland students and teachers (not a new program; must show track record of success)
Educational programs must align with Maryland's curricular and educational priorities
Educational programs must not be replicated in a classroom setting
Programs must emphasize experiential learning and one-on-one support services
Must submit a Fiscal Impact Statement describing the educational program, amount of funds requested, populations to be served, educational goals and objectives, and anticipated outcomes
Must provide names of independent governing board members
Must submit proof of 501(c)(3) nonprofit status
Must submit copy of most recent independent annual audit or internally generated financial statements until audit is available
Must provide evidence of active liability insurance coverage
Must submit detailed operating budget indicating less than 50% comes from state grants (except Baltimore Zoo), specifying all sources of income and all expenditures

Must provide evidence of direct service to Maryland school groups or individuals with disabilities, including data on age levels of students and projected numbers of students and teachers to be served both statewide and by jurisdiction
Must submit plans to align educational programs with MSDE's educational and curricular priorities
Must provide student safety response plan
Must provide GEPA Section 427 response addressing barriers to equitable participation and steps to overcome them
No more than 20% of participants served may come from nonpublic or homeschools (at least 80% must be public school students)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through an electronic system via email. The application period opens May 1, 2025, and closes June 13, 2025, at 5:00 p.m. EDT. MSDE reviews applications on a rolling basis beginning May 1. Applicants must download the electronic application, complete it with all required appendices, save as one PDF file, and email to sai.applications@maryland.gov. MSDE holds customer service support sessions (May 5 and May 23, 2025) to help applicants understand requirements and complete the application. Applications are pre-screened for submission requirements and inclusion of all required sections. A review committee evaluates applications using a scoring rubric. For any section scored Level 1 (does not meet criteria), written feedback is provided and an opportunity to revise and resubmit is offered. Results are communicated to the State Superintendent in July, provided to the State Board of Education for review in August, and final approval for awards is determined in legislation. The Governor releases the draft budget bill including institutions and funding allocations in January-April 2026, which is voted on and finalized around April 2026. Grant period runs July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program that reimburses sponsors who serve free healthy meals to children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income or economically disadvantaged areas during the summer months when school is not in session. Summer meal sites can operate as SUN Meals programs that provide meals and activities for children consumed on-site, or SUN Meals To-Go programs that provide multi-day meal boxes for pickup and home consumption. The program aims to reduce summer food insecurity by ensuring continued access to nutritious meals for eligible youth throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses sponsoring organizations for nutritious meals served to children and teens 18 and under during the summer months in economically disadvantaged areas throughout Maryland. Sites may provide meals and activities for on-site consumption (SUN Meals) or multi-day meal boxes for pickup and home consumption (SUN Meals To-Go). Funding is federal and administered through the Maryland State Department of Education's Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income or economically disadvantaged areas during summer months when school is not in session; organizations including non-profits and government entities serving as sponsoring organizations or approved meal site providers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for free nutritious meals served to eligible children and teens during summer months
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all Maryland counties including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties; sites must be located in economically disadvantaged areas
requirements_list: Organization must be a sponsoring organization or approved meal site provider
Meals must be served in low-income or economically disadvantaged areas
Children and teens must be 18 years or younger
Meals must meet USDA nutrition guidelines and Dietary Guidelines for Americans
Program must serve children 18 and under
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in becoming a SUN Meals site should contact the sponsoring organization for their county. Baltimore City has an online application available. Contact information for each county's sponsoring organization is provided on the program page. Sponsors in economically disadvantaged areas apply through the Maryland State Department of Education's Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs. Call (410) 767-0199 or email scnp_mailbox.msde@maryland.gov to speak with OSCNP staff for information on site eligibility and participation.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training on SFSP regulations, meal standards, menu planning, and compliance

requirements_list: Participation in Summer Food Service Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs for annual training dates and locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides additional funding for Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022 to participate in a USDA Team Nutrition grant project. The goal is to build State capacity to create new, high-quality, appealing standardized recipes for Maryland schools using local agricultural products developed with chefs from Prince George's Community College. Through LEA grant awards, MSDE provides funding to support staff time for training and recipe tasting events, and to purchase food and supplies for these events. The feedback from tasting events will be used to modify recipes to align with students' flavor preferences and be realistic for schools to implement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSDE provides grant awards to Local Education Agencies to support staff time for training and recipe tasting events, and to purchase food and supplies for these events. Funds may be used for: salaries/wages to hire substitute school nutrition staff to allow staff to attend training; stipends for staff time to attend training activities outside of normal work hours; food and nutrition equipment and smallware costs (total value of equipment cannot exceed 5% of the LEA subgrant total); and food costs for grant-related training and taste tests (food expenditures cannot exceed 20% of LEA subgrant total). Schools must purchase food in accordance with the Agency's Buy American Provision. The grant period runs from May 1, 2022 to September 30, 2023. Approximately ten (10) grants will be awarded, with additional grants possible if funds are available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than 5:00 pm EST on April 22, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff time for training and recipe tasting events; purchase of food and supplies for these events; salaries/wages for substitute school nutrition staff; stipends for staff attending training outside normal work hours; food and nutrition equipment and smallware (crinkle cutters, peelers, food processors, knives, roasting pans, utensils); and consumable costs for training and taste tests. Equipment cannot exceed 5% of total subgrant and food expenditures cannot exceed 20% of total subgrant. Funds cannot be used for child nutrition program costs outside the scope of the grant, purchasing meals and snacks for training participants, foods used for reimbursable meals, foods as incentives or prizes, foods for home preparation, foods unrelated to standardized recipes, costs associated with prizes or incentive items, gardening tools or materials, or clothing items.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland counties. Selection criteria include bonus points for schools located in rural zones as defined by USDA map and schools located in IRS-designated Qualified Opportunity Zones.
requirements_list: LEAs must be participating in NSLP or SSO during 2021-2022 and in good standing
LEAs must commit to participation of up to three schools; if more than one school, at least two schools must serve different grade levels
Schools must be enrolled as Team Nutrition Schools and registered prior to application submission
LEAs must designate a Grant Coordinator to serve as primary liaison with MSDE and grant partners, manage subgrant funds, and ensure grant activities are implemented at participating schools
Grant Coordinator must participate in periodic virtual meetings with grant partners
Schools must prepare at least one chef-designed recipe and host two or more student taste tests per recipe between Spring 2022 and Spring 2023
Schools must ensure school nutrition staff attend required training events
LEAs must collect feedback from students and school nutrition staff after each tasting event
Grant Coordinator must submit quarterly reports on utilization of subgrant funds
LEA must menu and serve at least one of the final new recipes in a reimbursable meal at participating schools by end of grant period
Grant Coordinator must secure photographs, training attendance records, data, and success stories for MSDE quarterly progress reports to USDA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must: (1) Identify up to three schools to participate that are registered as Team Nutrition Schools and participate in NSLP or SSO; (2) Complete a School Agreement Form for each participating school requiring signatures from School Principal, Kitchen Manager, and a third school staff member; (3) Complete the Team Nutrition Grant Application, including all components (school listing, recipe selection, budget, and school agreements); and (4) Email the completed application (saved as PDF) along with all required attachments to NutritionTraining.MSDE@maryland.gov. MSDE will review applications for eligibility, score applications using selection criteria (based on free/reduced-price enrollment percentage, rural zone location, and Qualified Opportunity Zone location), and notify approximately ten LEAs of award status by May 1, 2022. The application period is from March 24, 2022 to April 22, 2022 at 5:00 pm EST. An informational webinar will be held on March 31, 2022 from 2:00-3:00 pm. Grantees must submit quarterly grant reports (narrative and fiscal updates) by June 30, 2022, September 30, 2022, December 30, 2022, March 31, 2023, and June 30, 2023, with a final report due September 30, 2023. Invoices must be submitted as costs are incurred.

structured_extraction.program_name: The Judith P. Hoyer Early Child Care and Education Enhancement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps at-risk children from birth to age six and their families prepare for school. It provides grants to child care providers to improve the quality and professionalism of child care programs and support children's school readiness. Funds help providers acquire training, supplies, materials, and equipment to create stimulating learning environments aligned with early learning standards. Providers who meet credentialing and quality standards are awarded funds as an incentive to enhance quality of care, including accreditation and staff professional development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds support projects that improve child care quality. Applicants can use funds to acquire supplies, materials, and equipment to create stimulating learning environments that support implementation of knowledge gained through professional training and education. Funds are also available for accreditation and professional development programs for staff. Funds are awarded as an incentive for providers who meet credentialing and quality standards and implement curricula aligned with early learning standards.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 06/ Annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and family child care homes in Maryland, particularly those serving at-risk children from birth to age six and their families, that operate quality programs and implement curricula aligned with Kindergarten Readiness and Early Learning Assessment (ELA) guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support accreditation, professional development programs for staff, and acquisition of supplies, materials, and equipment to create stimulating learning environments that support implementation of knowledge gained through participation in training and enhance quality of child care and children's school readiness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Possess a current license or letter of compliance
Currently operate a child care center or family child care home
Implement a curriculum which aligns with the standards established by the Kindergarten Readiness and Early Learning Assessment (ELA) guidelines
Meet additional requirements specific to either child care centers or family child care homes as outlined in program materials
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program is currently in the process of review and approval through the Grants Office. The revised Grant Information Guide and Application will be available soon and will be communicated through the IMPACT and Tidbits newsletter and posted on the MSDE website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Title IV, Part B Nita M. Lowey 21st Century Community Learning Centers (CCLC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Creates community learning centers that provide students with academic enrichment opportunities and services designed to complement their regular school programs. Community learning centers offer families of participating students literacy instruction and related educational development programs. Services target students and families who attend schools eligible for Title I schoolwide programs or schools serving a high percentage of students from low-income families. Programs provide out-of-school time services occurring before school, after school, during the summer, and on Saturdays, keeping students safe, assisting working families, and improving academic achievement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding is provided to eligible organizations to establish and operate community learning centers. Funding is available in three-year cycles with grants level-funded at 100% of the original award contingent on availability of funding and satisfactory performance. Total funds available: $22.6 million (FY25). MSDE uses 93% of received funds for out-of-school time programs. Grantees are required to attend bi-monthly networking meetings offering technical assistance from Maryland State Department of Education personnel, peer-to-peer technical assistance, and resources selected based on expressed needs. Grant funds must be expended in the grant year awarded; MSDE does not allow carryover of unobligated funds into the following grant year. Final expenditure reports are due 60 days after the end of the grant period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, August 29, 2025
structured_extraction.contact_name: Reginald Burke, Executive Director, Office of Federal Programs; Emily Katongole, Director, Youth Development Branch
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies (LEAs), non-profit agencies, city or county government agencies, faith-based organizations, institutions of higher education, and for-profit corporations serving students and families who attend Title I eligible schools or schools serving a high percentage of low-income students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic enrichment opportunities and services designed to complement regular school programs, including literacy instruction and related educational development programs for students and families. Allowable expenses include: intervention strategies and curriculum purchases meeting ESSA evidence criteria; salaries and fringe benefits for 21st CCLC staff; professional development and trainings; consultants and evaluators; classroom materials and supplies; remedial educational activities and academic enrichment learning programs; core academic subject educational activities; arts and music education; entrepreneurial education and career readiness programs; tutoring and mentoring services; programs for limited English proficient students; recreational activities; technology education programs; expanded library services; drug and violence prevention programs; counseling and character education programs. Unallowable expenses include: proposal preparation costs, pre-award costs, entertainment and refreshments, unapproved field trips, incentives, promotional items, decorative items, facility or vehicle purchases, capital improvements, supplanting existing funds, and any costs not allowable under federal guidelines per Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.400.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Participants must provide services to students and families of students who primarily attend schools eligible for Title I schoolwide programs or schools that serve a high percentage of students from low-income families. Programs available to all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Services must target students attending Title I eligible schools or schools serving high percentage of low-income students
Families of participating students must have access to literacy instruction and related educational development programs
Grantees must attend bi-monthly networking meetings
Any public or private organization may apply
Applicants are encouraged to collaborate with the schools the children attend
A consortium of two or more agencies, organizations, or entities may apply
Local education agencies, interagency, interdepartmental, community and faith-based, or other private or public organizations may apply
Demonstrate adequate progress toward achieving all measurable objectives
Meet or exceed 85% of proposed level of students served
Attend required out-of-school national and regional conferences, MSDE grantee meetings and trainings

Maintain and submit Government Performance and Results Act (GPRA) data to USED 21 Annual Performance Report database
Participate fully in statewide evaluation activities
Comply with all applicable state statutory and regulatory requirements
