Provide description of how program provides comparable opportunities for public and private school students
Describe efforts to provide timely notice of intent to apply
Provide evidence of compliance with federal, state, and local fire, health, zoning codes, and safety standards
Non-LEA subrecipients in non-public school facilities must submit copies of required licenses and certifications including Use and Occupancy permit and current Fire Inspection report per site
Address at least one Maryland Leads Strategy, Maryland Strategic Plan, or Blueprint for Maryland's Future Priority area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit grant renewal applications for their respective cohort through Qualtrics application portal. For the FY2026 cycle covering FY2024 or FY2025 Cohorts, applications released July 25, 2025 with deadline August 29, 2025. Applicants must submit electronically through the FY26 21st CCLC Grant Renewal Application in Qualtrics. Upon submission, MSDE reviews the renewal application and recent performance data including start-up reports, Critical Elements Monitoring reports, timely reimbursement submissions, and total amendments. Approved subgrantees receive risk assessment levels 1-5 reflected in Year Notification of Grant Award. Customer service support sessions are available to assist applicants. Required documents include Performance Goals and Indicators, Evaluation Plan, Management Plan, Partner Plan, and proposed FY2026 Budget Documents. Subgrantees must submit required exhibits by Friday, August 29, 2025, uploading final documents into the 2025-2026 Critical Elements Monitoring folder.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides eligible child care providers with up to $400 each year to help pay for approved training, conferences, and college coursework. Providers can receive funds either as a training voucher (paid directly to the training organization before training occurs) or as a reimbursement (paid to the provider after training is completed). Eligible activities include approved Core of Knowledge training, pre-service training, registration at statewide and national child care conferences, and approved college coursework in areas such as child development, early childhood materials and methods, special education, administration and management, infants and toddlers, school-age children, health and safety and nutrition, and language and literacy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $400 per year in training support. For training vouchers, MSDE pays the approved trainer or training organization directly before training occurs. Approved applicants download the training voucher from their Maryland OneStop dashboard, sign it, and forward it to the trainer or training organization to complete registration. After training completion, applicants upload their certificate of successful completion to their Maryland OneStop portal. For reimbursement, the provider pays for training, then submits documentation of payment and successful completion within 180 days of training completion, and reimbursement is issued directly to the credentialed child care provider. Applicants receive notification of approval or denial via email within 30 days of application submission.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Beginning December 29, 2025 applications will be accepted. Training voucher applications must be submitted at least 60 days before the conference or training. Training reimbursement applications must be submitted within 180 days of training completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers in Maryland who hold a Maryland Child Care Credential at Level 2 or higher, or who held a Level 2 or higher credential that expired between July 1, 2024 and August 30, 2025.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Approved Core of Knowledge training (minimum 2 clock hours), pre-service training, registration at statewide and national child care conferences, and approved college coursework in areas such as child development, early childhood materials and methods, special education, program administration and management, infant and toddler care, school-age children, health and safety and nutrition, and language and literacy. Cannot be used for training fees alone, association membership fees, or CDA credential/renewal fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Must hold a Maryland Child Care Credential at Level 2 or higher OR have held a Level 2 or higher credential that expired between July 1, 2024 and August 30, 2025
Training must be approved by MSDE according to COMAR 13A.14.09
For pre-service training or conference registration vouchers, application must be submitted at least 60 days before the training or conference
For reimbursement applications, training must have occurred less than 181 days before the application date and must be submitted within 180 days of training completion
Training must be at least 2 clock hours for Core of Knowledge training

Applicant must submit proof of successful completion such as transcript, grade slip, or certificate of successful completion that includes participant name, date of training, training title, hours completed, trainer or organization name, and OCC assigned approval number if applicable
For reimbursement, applicant must provide documentation (receipt) showing the amount paid for training
Must register for individual account on Maryland OneStop platform to submit application
Applications must be submitted through Maryland OneStop online platform only; faxed, scanned, or mailed applications will not be processed
Applicants will receive notification of approval or denial via email within 30 days of application submission
Cannot use funds for training fees alone, association membership fees, or CDA credential/renewal fees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit applications through the Maryland OneStop platform. For training vouchers, submit a completed application with required documentation at least 60 days before the training or conference. Within 30 days of submission, applicants receive an email notification of approval or denial. If approved, click the 'View Submission' button in the approval email, log into Maryland OneStop, access the dashboard, click into the application submission, and download the PDF training voucher from the 'MSDE Approved Training Voucher' section at the bottom of the application. Sign the voucher and forward it to the approved trainer or training organization to complete training registration. After training completion, return to the Maryland OneStop portal, navigate to the 'Verification of Training Completion' section, and upload the certificate of successful completion by clicking 'Choose File' and pressing 'Submit'. The trainer or organization submits the voucher to MSDE for payment. For reimbursement, submit a completed application with required documentation (receipt, proof of payment, and certificate of successful completion) within 180 days of training completion. Reimbursement is issued directly to the credentialed child care provider. For non-standard activities, complete the PAU Approval Form with activity details, explanation, and documentation of impact on professional growth and child care community benefit; PAU requests are reviewed and processed within 60 days of receipt.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that provides nutritionally balanced, low-cost, or free lunches and snacks to students each school day at participating schools, childcare centers, and residential childcare institutions. The program reimburses participating institutions with federal dollars for meals that meet USDA nutrition standards, which include expanded access to fresh fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and reduced sodium and saturated fat content. All 24 Maryland public school systems, 22 nonprofit private schools, and residential childcare institutions participate, serving over 900,000 students with access to nutritious lunches and snacks each day. The funds help cover the cost of making the meals.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools and childcare institutions receive federal reimbursement (direct payments) for nutritious lunches and snacks served to enrolled students. Free meals are provided to students whose families have incomes at or below 130 percent of the federal poverty level. Students from families with incomes between 130 and 185 percent of the federal poverty level receive reduced-price meals, which are provided free due to Maryland state funding under the Maryland Cares for Kids Act. Students attending Community Eligibility Provision schools, Maryland Meals for Achievement schools, or enrolled in Head Start or Even Start programs receive free meals regardless of household income. Categorical eligibility is also available for homeless, migrant, runaway, and foster children, and for children receiving Medicaid. Income eligibility guidelines effective July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024 vary by household size and income frequency. For example, a household of 4 with annual income at or below $39,000 qualifies for free meals, and those with income between $39,001 and $55,500 qualify for reduced-price meals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students enrolled in participating Maryland public and nonprofit private schools, childcare centers, and residential childcare institutions, as well as the schools and residential child care institutions themselves. Eligibility for free or reduced-price meals is based on household income, participation in federal assistance programs, categorical eligibility status, or enrollment in qualifying nutrition programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to provide nutritionally balanced school lunches and snacks that meet USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans, including fresh fruits, vegetables, whole grains, with reduced sodium and saturated fat content. Maryland Nutrition Standards for all foods sold in school include requirements for whole grain-rich foods, foods with fruits/vegetables/dairy/protein as first ingredient, calorie limits (200 calories for snacks/side dishes, 350 calories for entrees), sodium limits (200mg for snacks, 480mg for entrees), total fat limit of 35% of calories, saturated fat limit under 10% of calories, and sugar limit of 35% or less by weight.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties; available in all 24 Maryland public school systems, 22 nonprofit private schools, and residential childcare institutions statewide.
requirements_list: School or institution must be a public school, private nonprofit school, or a residential childcare institution
Must serve meals meeting USDA nutrition guidelines and Dietary Guidelines for Americans

For student free meal eligibility: household income at or below 130 percent of federal poverty level based on specific income eligibility guidelines (e.g., $39,000 annual for household of 4 as of July 1, 2023), OR categorical eligibility (homeless, migrant, runaway, foster child, receiving Medicaid, participating in SNAP or TANF), OR attending a Community Eligibility Provision school, OR attending a Maryland Meals for Achievement school, OR enrolled in Head Start or Even Start program

For student reduced-price meal eligibility: household income between 130 and 185 percent of federal poverty level (e.g., $39,001–$55,500 annual for household of 4 as of July 1, 2023); provided as free meals in Maryland under the Maryland Cares for Kids Act
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and institutions participate through the Maryland State Department of Education's Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs. Families seeking free or reduced-price meals should contact their Local Education Agency's school nutrition office. Direct certification may apply for children receiving Medicaid. Income is evaluated using household size and comparing reported income to the Income Eligibility Guidelines for the appropriate income frequency (annual, monthly, twice per month, every two weeks, or weekly). When households have multiple income sources at different frequencies, all income must be annualized before comparison to eligibility guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Tri-County Council for Western Maryland offers this revolving loan program to help small businesses locate or expand in Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties in the Appalachian region. The program provides gap financing, partnering with banks and other lenders to fund the portion of a project that a primary lender cannot cover. Borrowers repay loans and the money is returned to the fund to make additional loans, making it an ongoing revolving financial tool. The main goal is to create or retain jobs in the region.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides loans from $10,000 to $400,000 as gap financing. A bank or other private lender must fund at least 50% of the project. The program operates using a pool of money granted by federal and state entities; repaid loans are returned to the fund to make further loans. Interest rates are tied to the prime interest rate. Loan terms are up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets like real estate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses — including corporations, partnerships, and sole proprietorships — seeking to locate or expand in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County that cannot obtain all needed funding from traditional lenders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business acquisition and expansion, land and building costs, machinery and equipment purchases, start-up costs, and working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in or seeking to locate in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County, Maryland (Appalachian region).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a small business seeking to locate or expand in eligible counties.
A business plan is required.
A private lender must fund at least 50% of the total project cost.
Applicant must provide a denial letter from the primary lender for 100% of the project, along with their approval to finance a majority of the project.
One job must be created or retained for every $30,000 borrowed within the first 36 months of the loan.
A minimum equity injection of 10% is generally required for start-up businesses.
Personal guaranties of the debt are required from all owners with 20% or greater interest.
Applicants must provide a completed personal financial statement and 3 years of both business and personal tax returns.
A $250 non-refundable application fee is required.
Approved borrowers are assessed a 1.5% loan origination fee at closing.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, create a business plan and determine your funding needs. Second, apply for a loan from a private bank to determine how much they will finance. Third, complete the program's application form and submit it with the required documents and application fee.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed exclusively for agricultural businesses, farms, and farm owners in Washington County, Maryland. The program aims to support agricultural business growth and development through equipment and innovation investments. Funding of $300,000 was approved by the Board of County Commissioners in July 2023 from the Washington County Hotel Rental Tax Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding approved at $300,000 from the Washington County Hotel Rental Tax Fund to support agricultural innovation and equipment purchases for eligible agricultural operations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Check back in 2026 for the next round of updates
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural businesses, farms, and farm owners in Washington County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Agricultural innovation, equipment purchases, and agricultural business growth and development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are currently closed. Check back in 2026 for the next round of funding opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that encourages agricultural landowners in Washington County to restrict their land from development for a minimum of ten years. Participants receive protection from nuisance complaints through the Right to Farm Ordinance (County acknowledgement that farming is the preferred use of the land), a County property tax credit applied to farmland, farm buildings, and partial credit for the home, and eligibility to sell Development Rights Easements through the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Program (MALPP/MALPF). The agreement is notarized and recorded in County Land Records and remains in effect for at least ten years even if the property is sold or transferred. Restrictions cover development, subdivision, signage, dumping, and require implementation of soil erosion and water quality practices per an approved soil conservation plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners who voluntarily enter into a ten-year Agricultural Land Preservation District agreement receive: (1) a County property tax credit applied to farmland, farm buildings, and partial credit for the home; (2) protection from nuisance complaints through official County acknowledgement that farming is the preferred use of the land; (3) eligibility to apply to sell an agricultural preservation easement to MALPF/MALPP, subject to availability of state funds; and (4) ability to retain certain personal eligibility options including potential release of family, owner's, or child's lots. The agreement is notarized and recorded in the County Land Records and remains effective for at least ten years, binding on any new owner if the property is sold or transferred.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Planning Department Agricultural Land Preservation Office
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County who wish to voluntarily preserve their land from development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land preservation through voluntary ten-year development restrictions; land must be kept in agricultural use and cannot be used for commercial, industrial, or residential purposes except as permitted by County regulations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Land must be outside water and sewer service areas and outside growth areas.
requirements_list: Landowner must voluntarily agree to enter the program
Minimum 50 acres stand-alone or 20 acres if contiguous to other districts
Minimum 50% of soil must be classes I, II, and III
Property must be outside water and sewer service areas
Property must be outside growth areas
Land must be kept in agricultural use for minimum ten years from recording date
Land cannot be subdivided, divided, or have boundary lines moved without County written approval
Cannot construct non-agricultural buildings or structures without County approval
Soil erosion and water quality practices per approved soil conservation plan must be implemented within 10 years
No commercial signs or billboards except as specified (property name, home-based occupation, or sale/rental)
No dumping of trash or rubbish except agricultural materials
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners contact the Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning's Agricultural Land Preservation Office. Applicants submit an Agricultural District Intake Form providing information about the property including total acreage, address, map/grid/parcel information, soil characteristics, and farming operation details. Once reviewed and approved, the County prepares an Agricultural Preservation District Agreement which must be signed by all titled landowners, notarized, and recorded in the County Land Records. The agreement becomes effective upon recordation. After ten years, the agreement may be terminated at any time upon written request by all current titled landowners by recording a Release and Termination document.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program that provides grants to eligible entities for projects supporting economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure, natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity building in Appalachia.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided for projects in five strategic areas: Economic Opportunities (entrepreneurial and business development), Ready Workforce (education, skills, and health improvement), Critical Infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water/wastewater systems), Natural and Cultural Assets (community and economic development leveraging heritage), and Leadership and Community Capacity (building skills of leaders and organizations). All grants require a 50% match with matching funds identified and committed at time of application. Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact. Projects consistent with the ARC 2024 Strategy Statement are prioritized, including Technology Development, Broadband, Education and Workforce Development, Tourism, Energy, Recovery Ecosystems and Traditional Infrastructure.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 3, 2026 (Preliminary Project Submission); November 15 (Formal Application)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible entities in Washington County, Maryland seeking to support economic development, workforce readiness, infrastructure improvements, cultural heritage, or community capacity building initiatives.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects related to economic opportunities and entrepreneurship, workforce education and skills development, critical infrastructure including broadband and water systems, natural and cultural asset development, and leadership and community capacity building. Projects should be consistent with ARC Strategic Goals and Objectives and should be part of an overall plan for stimulating economic development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland and Appalachian Region. Projects are ranked at the county level by Washington County Commissioners, then regionally by the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland.
requirements_list: 50% match funding must be identified and committed at time of application
Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact
Eligible entities must submit preliminary project description and budget forms by April 3, 2026
All outputs and outcomes must be quantifiable with associated numeric values and defined in the context of project activities
Projects should be consistent with ARC 2024 Strategy Statement
Projects should reference any plan and/or economic documents showing the project is part of an overall plan for stimulating economic development
Matching funds must be in place and committed at time of application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Submit the Preliminary Project Description (PPD) and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources Worksheet forms to the Office of Grant Management by April 3, 2026. The PPD must include project description, organizational capacity to administer a federal grant, goals and objectives aligned with ARC Investment Goals and State Objectives/Strategies, and quantifiable performance measures with timeframes. Step 2: Washington County Commissioners review and rank submitted projects. Step 3: County-ranked projects are submitted to the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for regional ranking. Step 4: Top-ranking projects receive a letter in early fall inviting them to submit a formal grant application to the Appalachian Regional Commission, with the formal application due by November 15.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial support to charitable organizations within Washington County that provide services improving the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual financial grants awarded to recognized non-profit organizations on the Board of County Commissioners' Recognized Non-Profit List (Section 1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws). The Board of County Commissioners determines the annual allocation set aside for the Community Organization Fund during the budgeting process. For FY 2027, $1,200,000 is allocated across six priority service areas: Families and Children ($494,400), Domestic Violence ($386,400), Arts & Cultural ($135,600), Seniors ($136,800), Recreation ($33,600), and Other ($13,200). Grant awards are disbursed in four quarterly installments (25% each quarter) and all funds must be expended within the fiscal year period (July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027). Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of the total request amount.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Tuesday, January 6, 2026, by 3:00pm
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maria Kramer, Director; Carsten Ahrens, Senior Grant Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charitable organizations within Washington County that are on the Board of County Commissioners' Recognized Non-Profit List (Section 1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws) and are recognized by the IRS as 501(c)(3) organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating and capital expenses and projects that improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. Eligible for funding targeting one of six priority service areas: Families/Children, Domestic Violence, Cultural/Arts, Seniors, Recreation, or Other. Funds cannot be used to benefit an individual or to fund an endowment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County only. Organizations must have an office located within Washington County and provide services within Washington County.
requirements_list: Must be included on the Board of County Commissioners' Recognized Non-Profit List (Section 1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws)
Must be a charitable organization providing services that improve the community
Must be recognized by the Internal Revenue Service as a 501(c)(3) with Valid status
Must be incorporated as a business entity with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and be In Good Standing at the time of application submission with proof required
Must have an office in and provide services within Washington County
Must have a recent audit (preferably) or recent detailed financial statement
Must not have unpaid liens or judgments against the corporation or association
Must not have unpaid or past due obligations to the Washington County Treasurer or any other government entity
Must not have outstanding obligations to the County from previous grant awards
Must not request funds intended to benefit an individual or to fund an endowment
Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of the total amount requested
If not on the 1-108 list, must apply to be added before applying for funding in the following year's cycle
Application must be completed in its entirety including signature of authorized representative
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland at the time of application
Must impact at least one of the prioritized service areas
Must submit both six hard paper copies and one electronic copy by the deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List receive a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) each year during the annual funding cycle. Applicants must submit a completed application packet including: Community Organization Funding Application Overview, Statement of Need (1 page max), Past Performance (1 page max), Organizational Capacity and Staffing Plan (2 pages max), Program Plan (4 pages max), Collaborating Partnerships and Coordination of Services (1 page max), letters of support (highly encouraged), authorized representative signature, Budget Spreadsheet (FY27 format), copy of IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter, SDAT Proof of Organization In Good Standing, most recent audit or financial statement, copy of most recent IRS Form 990, and W-9 form (if organization has not received County funds previously or has address change). Submit six hard paper copies (unsecured with staples, clips, or bands only - no binders or tabs) and one electronic PDF copy combined in order by the deadline. Paper copies mailed to: Washington County Office of Grant Management, 100 W. Washington Street, Room 1601, Hagerstown, MD 21740, Attn: Julie Mackereth, Senior Office Associate. Electronic copy emailed to cahrens@washco-md.net and cc jmackereth@washco-md.net. Applications received after the deadline will not be accepted. OGM staff will not check applications for accuracy or completeness at submission; applicants must verify completeness against the submittal checklist. Applications are rated using a 100-point scoring rubric evaluating: Application Submission (10 pts), Statement of Need (20 pts), Past Performance (5 pts), Organizational Capacity and Staffing (10 pts), Program Plan (30 pts), Collaborations/Partnerships/Coordination (10 pts), and Budget/Narrative (15 pts). The COF Committee reviews applications and makes funding recommendations considering total allocation, service area allocations, geographic distribution, and previous performance. Applicants notified in writing after BOCC approves County budget allocations (May-June 2026). Grant report submission is not required as part of FY27 application, but organizations funded in FY26 must submit grant report with full expense documentation by June 30, 2026 or risk jeopardizing FY27 funding if awarded. Two optional informational workshops offered Tuesday, December 2nd from 9:00-10:30 am or 3:00-4:30pm via Zoom with limited in-person option.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund reinvests cannabis sales tax revenue into communities that were disproportionately impacted by cannabis prohibition enforcement before July 1, 2022. It supports community-based initiatives that benefit low-income communities and areas identified as disproportionately impacted.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded by cannabis sales tax revenue and cannabis business conversion fees. Funds are distributed to support community-based initiatives. The amount and specific terms depend on the funding plan and application process developed by Washington County. Funds must supplement, not replace, existing local government funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations, non-profits, and government agencies serving low-income communities and disproportionately impacted areas in Washington County, specifically ZIP code 21740 which includes portions of Hagerstown and surrounding unincorporated areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based initiatives that benefit low-income communities and disproportionately impacted areas, including mental health and substance use services, education and after-school programs, small business grants and economic development initiatives, parks and recreational opportunities, criminal justice reform and re-entry programs, and housing assistance and homelessness prevention. Administrative expenses necessary to implement and manage the program are also eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: In Washington County, restricted CRRF cannabis sales tax funds may only be used for initiatives serving ZIP code 21740, which includes portions of the City of Hagerstown and surrounding unincorporated areas of the County.
requirements_list: CRRF funding must supplement, not replace, existing local government funding for programs and services
Funds may not be used for law enforcement agencies or law enforcement activities
Programs must serve communities disproportionately impacted by cannabis prohibition enforcement
Programs must benefit low-income communities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Washington County is developing application procedures and guidelines for eligible organizations. The County is establishing a funding plan in consultation with community stakeholders and will hold a public hearing prior to adopting the plan. Applications will be processed by the Grant Management office at Washington County Administration Complex.

Facing continued financial impacts from Coronavirus

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded program that works in conjunction with the Federal Farm Service Agency's CREP Contract Program. The program makes CREP Contracts permanent through state-funded conservation easements, allowing landowners to preserve land in perpetuity. A matching component allows landowners to add up to ten times the acreage of their CREP Contract to their easement, maximizing both land preservation and easement value.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program purchases conservation easements on land enrolled in FSA CREP Contracts, making the contracts permanent. Landowners can add up to ten times the acreage from their CREP Contract to their CREP easement to maximize both land preservation and easement value. Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners with existing FSA CREP Contracts seeking to make their contracts permanent through conservation easements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of conservation easements on land enrolled in FSA CREP Contracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must have an existing FSA CREP Contract
Landowner can add up to ten times the acreage of their CREP contract to the easement
Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must have an existing FSA CREP Contract to apply for the easement program. Landowners apply to convert their FSA CREP contracts to permanent state-funded easements. Once the easement is sold, it remains effective in perpetuity. Interested landowners should contact the Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning.

structured_extraction.program_name: Enterprise Zone Tax Credits (Washington County / Hagerstown)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides qualifying businesses with state income tax credits and local real property tax credits in return for job creation and capital investments made in designated Enterprise Zones in Washington County. Zones include the City of Hagerstown/Washington County Enterprise Zone and the Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credits based on new jobs created: $1,000 one-time maximum for most employees; $3,000 first year, $2,000 second year, $1,000 third year for economically disadvantaged employees certified by Maryland Department of Labor. Local real property tax credits on increased assessment: 80% for years 1-5, declining to 30% by year 10. Exemption from commercial building excise tax on new construction. Credits available for 10-year period from Zone designation date.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No ongoing deadline; applications accepted year-round
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses locating or investing in designated Enterprise Zones in Washington County, including proprietorships, partnerships, and corporations engaged in manufacturing, warehousing, research and development, corporate or regional headquarters offices, service industries, or mercantile/retail businesses (retail only in Central Business District or Hancock Zone).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State income tax credits for qualifying new jobs created; local real property tax credits on increased property assessments from capital investments; exemptions from commercial building excise tax on new construction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Three state-designated Enterprise Zones in Washington County: (1) City of Hagerstown/Washington County Enterprise Zone (approximately 4,000 acres, includes Hopewell Valley Industrial Park, Washington County Business Park, CSX Valley Park, City Business Park, and Central Business District); (2) Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (1,500 acres). Designation dates: Hagerstown-Washington County Zone - December 15, 1982; Hancock Zone - December 15, 1995.
requirements_list: Business must be located within Zone boundaries on designation date, relocated to Zone after designation date, or started construction/expansion after designation date
For income tax credits: minimum of 1 new job in Central Business District or Hancock Zone; 5 new jobs outside Central Business District
For real property tax credits: minimum of $5,000 capital investment in Central Business District or Hancock Zone; $50,000 capital investment outside Central Business District
Employees must be hired after Zone designation date (not replacement hires)
Employees must work at least 35 hours per week for at least 6 consecutive months
Employees must earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage
Employees must spend at least 50% of working time in the Enterprise Zone or in activities directly related to the Zone

Business types limited to: manufacturing, warehousing, research and development, corporate or regional headquarters offices, service industries, mercantile or retail businesses (retail only in designated areas)
For property tax credits: application must be submitted before project completion and issuance of Use/Occupancy permits
Capital improvements must be certified to Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation during calendar year of construction completion (by December 31)
For economically disadvantaged employee credits: employees must be certified by Maryland Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Determine that business property is located in an Enterprise Zone by contacting Washington County Department of Business Development. 2. Verify eligibility criteria for job creation or capital investment minimums. 3. Complete Request for Enterprise Zone Qualification form. For property tax credits: submit form before project completion. For income tax credits: submit form after hiring new employees and complete 'New Jobs Created' form listing qualifying employees. 4. For income tax credits: Maryland Job Service Office contacts applicant to review employee list and determine individual eligibility as 'disadvantaged' or 'non-disadvantaged'. 5. Washington County Department of Business Development sends approval letter. Copies submitted to appropriate local and state agencies. 6. For property tax credits: credits automatically appear on Washington County and Town of Hancock tax bills in July; City of Hagerstown issues credit voucher. Credits appear on July 1 tax bill of year following project completion qualification. 7. For income tax credits: claim credits using Maryland Tax Form 500CR with approval letter. Contact Maryland Job Service (301-393-8200, 14 North Potomac Street, Hagerstown) to identify any disadvantaged employees. 8. After initial approval, no reapplication needed for additional job credits.

Receiving an ExportMD Award

structured_extraction.program_description: The Washington County Gaming Commission distributes grants from the Washington County Gaming Fund to eligible charitable organizations. The Commission reviews applications and awards funds in accordance with state statute and county regulations. Monies collected from tip jars are deposited into a dedicated Gaming Fund account. By statute, 50% of the Gaming Funds are allocated to the Washington County Volunteer Fire & Rescue Association, with the remaining allocated to local charitable organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are distributed from the Washington County Gaming Fund to qualified 501(c)(3) charitable organizations. Maximum distribution per application is $100,000. Organizations may apply for multiple projects by submitting separate applications. Funds must be used exclusively in Washington County and cannot be distributed outside of the County. The grant performance period is one year from award announcement (typically early in August). Any funds not spent within the performance period must be returned to the fund.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Susan M. Buchanan, Director; For general questions: J. Mackereth; For other questions: S. La Pole or S. Buchanan
structured_extraction.contact_email: jmackereth@washco-md.net (general/technical questions); slapole@washco-md.net or sbuchanan@washco-md.net (other questions)
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) charitable organizations located in Washington County that provide services in health and human services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, educational and cultural activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants from the Washington County Gaming Fund for charitable purposes benefiting health and human services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, educational and cultural activities within Washington County.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are released each April. Applicants must submit a complete electronic application via email to jmackereth@washco-md.net copying slapole@washco-md.net by the deadline (3:00 p.m. on May 6, 2020). Application packet includes: (1) REQUEST - complete Request for Funding application signed by authorized official; (2) FINANCIALS - most recent annual financial statement; (3) GRPT - 2019 Gaming Fund Grant Report and evidence of how previously received funds were expended; (4) DOC - additional documentation such as estimates, quotes, and partnership letters (if applicable); (5) NORP - Notice of Responsible Person Form (required only for unincorporated associations); (6) W-9 - completed IRS Form W-9 and Washington County vendor forms. A Public Funding Hearing is held in June (scheduled for June 23, 2020), where applicants may appear and the Commission asks clarifying questions; early scheduling of hearing time is recommended. The Gaming Commission reviews all applications and makes funding recommendations after the public hearing. Funding awards are announced during the Board of County Commissioners meeting in August, with award letters sent and funds disbursed several weeks after announcement.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides one-time funding to organizations operating in Washington County for projects or events that were not previously budgeted or anticipated. It addresses current financial issues or situations that require prompt response and resolution, assisting organizations with projects that do not qualify for other general fund programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Board of County Commissioners appropriates a portion of the General Fund Contingency annually and awards it to targeted organizations meeting the funding goals. The available funding portion may be adjusted annually at the discretion of the Board of County Commissioners. Grant awards are limited to a maximum of $2,000. Grants are paid to the applicant, not to vendors for products or services. Unused funds must be returned to the Office of Grant Management within 30 days of the completion of the event.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding. Submit the General Fund Contingency Funding Grant Application through the County's website at www.washco-md.net, or print and mail or email it in. The application packet includes guidelines and instructions that must be carefully read. The application must be saved to your computer before completion to avoid loss of information. Upon receipt, the Office of Grant Management will: (1) Determine if the applicant is qualified to receive funding; (2) Determine if the event or project is qualified to receive funding; (3) Determine if the request meets the funding goals of the County Commissioners; (4) Approve or deny the request with the concurrence of the County Administrator; (5) Notify the applicant in writing as to the approval or denial of their request. All organizations receiving grant funding must complete a General Fund Contingency Grant Report and submit it with supporting documentation within 60 days of the completion of the event or project.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credits available for property owners who undertake qualified rehabilitation work on historic properties in Washington County. The program provides a reduction in County property taxes through a 25% county tax credit, with potential for additional state (20%) and federal (20%) credits, plus a 5% additional credit for new construction attached to existing historic structures.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides property tax credits ranging up to 70% when combining county, state, and federal credits. The 25% county tax credit is available for rehabilitation, restoration, or preservation work that minimizes destruction of historic fabric and has sympathetic design. An additional 5% credit is available for new construction attached to existing historic structures. Work eligible for credits includes roof repair/replacement, chimney repair/replacement, window restoration, storm doors/windows, masonry repointing, structural repairs, and architectural/engineering/consulting fees. Unused credits can be carried over for up to 5 years or until expended. Applications must be submitted before work begins.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application must be submitted before rehabilitation work begins
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Historic District Commission / Washington County Department of Planning and Zoning
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial property owners with historic structures in Washington County seeking to rehabilitate their properties. Properties must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified rehabilitation expenses for historic structures including roof repair and replacement, chimney repair and replacement, window restoration, new storm doors and windows, masonry repointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties located within the Antietam Overlay (AO1 or AO2) districts; contributing structures to surveyed and adopted Historic Rural Villages (Antietam, Cavetown, Fairplay, Highfield, Leitersburg, Pen Mar, Ringgold, Rohrersville, Sandy Hook, or Tilghmanton); properties with Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay zoning applied through rezoning process; or contributing structures within Towns listed on the National Register of Historic Places with appropriate zoning and design guidelines. For structures under Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) Easement, a copy of the easement document must be included.
requirements_list: Property must be located in an eligible historic district, overlay zone, or historic village
Property must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties
Residential or commercial property owners qualify
Rehabilitation work must meet Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and Washington County Design Guidelines for Historic Structures
Application must be submitted and approved before rehabilitation work begins
Multi-part application must be completed with detailed expense documentation
All work must be consistent with historic preservation standards
Invoices and receipts with proof of payment required for all expenses
Photography documentation required before, during, and after project completion
If applicant is not fee-simple owner, Owner's Representative Affidavit required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process consists of three parts submitted to the Washington County Historic District Commission. Part I (Evaluation of Significance): Determine if structure qualifies and is in a qualifying area. Includes property details, physical appearance description, statement of significance, and before photos. Properties with HP Overlay zoning do not need to complete Part I unless there is a question about overlay inclusion. Part II (Description of Rehabilitation): Submitted before work begins. Includes detailed description of all proposed exterior work, consistency with Secretary of Interior's Standards, estimated costs, and supporting photos and plans. Must be approved by HDC before work starts. Part III (Certification of Completed Work): Submitted after project completion. Includes itemized expense spreadsheet with invoices and proof of payment, after photos, and certification that work was completed as approved. Staff may conduct site visits. Applications can be submitted by mail to: Washington County Historic District Commission, c/o Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning, 747 Northern Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21742, or by email to askplanning@washco-md.net. All applications require wet or digital signatures. Questions during application process should be directed to askplanning@washco-md.net.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to help Washington County organizations, agencies, and businesses develop tourism attractions, enhance economic development, and support cultural and recreational projects. The program aims to assist organizations and agencies in undertaking activities that would not be possible without special funding, with the goal of helping activities eventually become self-sustaining.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded by a 6 percent county hotel rental tax. Funds are invested back into the community through the Convention and Visitors Bureau, local municipalities, and designated local projects to support tourism attractions, economic development, and cultural and recreational projects. Grant classifications include: (1) Develop Tourism Attraction: advertising, publicizing or distributing information for developing tourism attractions, attracting tourists, strategic planning and research, marketing special events and festivals, support of tourism-related facilities including conference centers and visitor information centers; (2) Economic Development: projects that enhance the vitality of Washington County's economy by retaining and creating job opportunities, retaining business, or assisting in expansion of local companies; (3) Cultural: projects relating to the county's culture or history that benefit local residents or draw visitors; (4) Recreational: projects that promote recreational activities or events and promote tourism and lodging or provide benefit to county residents. Grant applications requesting $25,000 or less are reviewed and approved by the Office of Grant Management with concurrence of the County Administrator. Applications requesting more than $25,000 are reviewed by the Office of Grant Management and County Administrator, with final approval by the Board of County Commissioners. Grants are paid to the applicant, not to vendors. Any changes exceeding 10% of approved line items require Office of Grant Management approval. Unused funds must be returned within 30 days of project completion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Office of Grant Management
structured_extraction.program_audience: Washington County local municipalities, businesses, organizations, residents, and visitors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing tourism attractions, enhancing economic development, and supporting cultural and recreational projects. Eligible expenses include personnel, operating costs, equipment, advertising, facility rental, and contracted services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding. Applications can be accessed from the County's website under the Office of Grant Management, submitted by email, or printed and mailed. All applications are received by the Office of Grant Management (OGM). Upon receipt, the OGM will: (1) Determine if the applicant is qualified to receive funding; (2) Determine if the event or project is qualified to receive funding; (3) Determine if the request meets the funding goals of the County Commissioners and the purpose of Hotel Rental Tax Funding; (4) For requests of $25,000 and below, approve or deny the request with concurrence of the County Administrator; (5) For requests of more than $25,000, process the application and forward to the County Administrator for review, and upon favorable review, the County Commissioners will hear the request and may take action; (6) Notify the applicant in writing of approval or denial. All organizations receiving grant funding must complete a Hotel Rental Tax Grant Report and submit it with supporting documentation (budget itemizations and receipts) within 60 days of project completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A county-funded program designed to accelerate land preservation easement purchases by providing an alternative payment method. Agricultural landowners can sell Development Rights Easements (Agricultural Preservation Easements) to the County and receive payment through an Installment Purchase Agreement over a ten-year period at a fixed interest rate. Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases Agricultural Preservation Easements (Development Rights Easements) from eligible agricultural landowners through an Installment Purchase Agreement. Ten percent of the principal is paid at settlement plus interest, and ten percent of the principal is paid annually for the remaining nine years at a fixed interest rate. Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County seeking to sell development rights and receive payments over time.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of Agricultural Preservation Easements (Development Rights Easements) on contiguous agricultural land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property owner must own agricultural land meeting minimum qualifications
Easement can cover all contiguous acreage less one acre per existing dwelling on the property
Program is competitive and dependent on current economic climate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners should contact the Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning. Once an owner agrees to sell development rights, an Installment Purchase Agreement is written between the County and the landowner detailing total payment amount and payment terms including the fixed interest rate and payment schedule.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded program administered locally by Washington County that permanently preserves high-quality agricultural properties by purchasing Development Rights Easements from willing farmers. Properties are ranked competitively based on soil quality, proximity to other easements, agricultural operation intensity, and proximity to growth areas and Priority Preservation Areas. Funds are provided by the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF). Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity. Enrollment in the County's Agricultural District program is a prerequisite.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases Development Rights Easements from qualifying agricultural properties, providing financial compensation to landowners while permanently protecting the agricultural land from development. Funds are provided by MALPF. Properties are ranked competitively by the local Agricultural Land Preservation Advisory Board based on soil quality, proximity to other easements, agricultural operation intensity, and proximity to growth areas and Priority Preservation Areas. Approved applications are sent to MALPF prior to July 1st of each cycle year. Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of Development Rights Easements to permanently preserve agricultural land from development.

structured_extraction.program_name: Next Generation Farmland Acquisition Program (Next Gen)
structured_extraction.program_description: A MARBIDCO-funded program providing down payment assistance to young and beginning farmers purchasing agricultural properties that qualify for Washington County's Agricultural District program. The program offers 51% of a land-only Fair Market Value appraisal, capped at $500,000. After settlement, the landowner must actively pursue a different permanent easement through an approved program and enroll in the County's Agricultural District program. If no permanent easement is procured within seven years, the land becomes preserved through a MARBIDCO permanent easement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MARBIDCO provides down payment assistance equal to 51% of the land-only Fair Market Value appraisal of the property, capped at a maximum of $500,000. Buyers receive assistance toward purchasing qualifying agricultural properties that qualify for Washington County's Agricultural District program. After real estate settlement, the landowner must actively pursue a different permanent easement through an approved program and enroll in the County's Agricultural District program. If after seven years no permanent easement can be procured for the property, the land becomes preserved through a MARBIDCO permanent easement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young and beginning farmers seeking to purchase agricultural properties in Washington County that qualify for the County's Agricultural District program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for the purchase of agricultural properties that qualify for Washington County's Agricultural District program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Properties must qualify for the County's Agricultural District program.
requirements_list: Buyer must be a young or beginning farmer
Property must qualify for Washington County's Agricultural District program
Buyer must provide a signed sales contract for the farm
After settlement, landowner must actively pursue a permanent easement through an approved program within seven years
Landowner must enroll in the County's Agricultural District program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Buyers must provide a signed sales contract for the farm and fill out the application in conjunction with the County's Land Preservation Office to submit to MARBIDCO. The process takes roughly six months to complete after submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded program focused on protecting Maryland's best natural, agricultural, historical, and cultural areas and most significant rural landscapes. The program encourages local governments and private land trusts to identify Rural Legacy Areas and apply for competitive funds to preserve land through easements from willing landowners. DNR and local land trusts purchase easements from willing landowners within specified Rural Legacy Areas to protect areas vulnerable to sprawl development, preserving the economic value of farming, forestry, recreation, and tourism. Easement payments are based on property characteristics including property size, number of development rights, proximity to other permanent easements, agricultural characteristics, historic characteristics, and environmental characteristics. Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financing to small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses, with funds derived from video lottery terminal proceeds and distributed through a targeted allocation system.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Under Maryland law, 1.5 percent of proceeds generated from video lottery terminals (slots) are contributed to the State Lottery Terminal (SLoT) Account for distribution to targeted businesses. At least 50 percent of allocations are deployed to targeted businesses within a 10-mile radius of five casinos (Hollywood Casino Perryville, Ocean Downs in Worcester County, Maryland Live! in Anne Arundel County, Rocky Gap Casino in Allegany County, and Horseshoe Casino in Baltimore City). The other 50 percent is available to eligible businesses throughout Maryland. Loans range between $10,000 and $500,000.

structured_extraction.program_name: Washington County Business Incentives Program (Comprehensive Overview)
structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive tax incentives and assistance programs designed to support business development, expansion, and relocation in Washington County, including real property tax credits, job creation incentives, workforce training grants, and specialized programs for brownfield revitalization and clean energy projects. This overview document covers the full suite of Washington County and City of Hagerstown business incentive programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple tax incentive programs available: (1) Job Creation & Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit Program - 6-15 years of county real property tax credits for qualified businesses expanding or locating in Washington County with options including 52% credit years 1-2/39% years 3-4/26% years 5-6 (Section 4a); 30% years 1-2/20% years 3-4/10% years 5-6 (Section 4b); or 100% years 1-5/75% years 6-10/50% years 11-15 (Section 4c); (2) New Jobs Tax Credit Program - 6 year tax credit at 52% years 1-2/39% years 3-4/26% years 5-6 for businesses meeting employment and wage requirements; (3) Pad-Ready Site Commercial Stimulus Program - 3 year tax credit at 0.4% of construction costs; (4) Brownfield Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) - 5-10 year real property tax credits of 50-70% on increased site value; (5) C-PACE Program - Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy loans for energy efficiency and renewable energy projects with long repayment periods and low interest rates; (6) Enterprise Zone credits - state income tax credits and local real property tax credits for job creation and capital investments; (7) Research & Development Equipment Tax Exemption; (8) Manufacturing Machinery & Equipment Tax Exemption; (9) Business Inventory Tax Exemption. City of Hagerstown programs include: CDBG Microenterprise Grant Program for businesses with 5 or fewer employees; Hagerstown Revolving Loan Fund (HRLF) - loans up to $200,000 for small businesses; Invest Hagerstown Grant Programs offering redevelopment and homeownership grants. Workforce programs provide apprenticeship training grants, training reimbursement up to $4,500 per worker through Western Maryland Consortium, and workforce development services at no cost.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing/Rolling basis
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Department of Business Development and Economic Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses opening, expanding, or relocating in Washington County; small businesses with 5 or fewer employees; real estate developers; manufacturing and technology companies; nonprofits and commercial entities seeking clean energy financing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business operations, expansion, relocation, equipment purchases, machinery and manufacturing equipment, research and development, capital improvements, land improvements, building construction and renovation, energy efficiency and renewable energy projects, employee recruitment and training, code compliance, façade enhancement, working capital, and redevelopment of vacant and under-utilized properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland including: Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone (5,000 acres in City of Hagerstown including Hopewell Valley Industrial Park, City of Hagerstown Business Park, Central Business District); Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (1,500 acres); Foreign Trade Zone #255 (1,700 acres across Hagerstown Regional Airport, Williamsport, Hopewell Valley, Lakeside Corporate Center at Cascade, and Hancock); Priority Funding Areas as designated; City of Hagerstown corporate boundaries for city-specific programs

structured_extraction.program_name: Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides up to fifteen years of tax credits on the county portion of real estate taxes for qualified businesses that expand or locate in Washington County and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds. The program is designed to attract new companies and support existing companies that expand in Washington County, incentivizing well-paying jobs and capital investments in the community. Businesses located in Enterprise Zones are not eligible and must apply under the Enterprise Zone Program instead.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to fifteen years of tax credits on the county portion of real estate taxes for qualified businesses. Three tiers based on investment and job creation: TIER ONE provides 3 years of credits (55%, 40%, 25% rates) for businesses with 1,500 sq. ft. expansion and 5 new full-time employees within 12 months; TIER TWO provides 6 years of credits (55%, 55%, 40%, 40%, 25%, 25% rates) for businesses with 2,500 sq. ft. expansion and 25 new full-time employees within 24 months; TIER THREE provides 15 years of credits (75% for first five years, then reduced by 5% annually until reaching 25%) for businesses with $20 million investment and 200 new full-time employees within 24 months (with 80% of new employees earning 200% of Maryland State minimum wage). Tax credits are applied to the increased assessed property value. For leased properties, the lessor must reduce the tenant's tax liability by the credit amount.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, before project construction is complete
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified for-profit businesses expanding or locating in Washington County that meet investment and job creation requirements. Businesses in Enterprise Zones are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property tax credits for businesses that create jobs and make capital investments in newly constructed, renovated, expanded, or previously unoccupied properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. The business property must be located in a Priority Funding Area in Washington County. Businesses located in Enterprise Zones are not eligible for this program and must apply under the Enterprise Zone Program instead.
requirements_list: Must be located in a Priority Funding Area.
Cannot be located in an Enterprise Zone.
Submit an application before construction is complete and before occupying space or hiring employees.
Meet specific investment thresholds (varies by tier: no minimum for Tier 1-2, $20M for Tier 3).
Meet specific job creation thresholds (5 new FTEs for Tier 1 within 12 months; 25 new FTEs for Tier 2 within 24 months; 200 new FTEs for Tier 3 within 24 months).
Tier 1: Expand by at least 1,500 sq. ft. and create at least 5 new full-time jobs.
Tier 2: Obtain at least 2,500 sq. ft. of space and create at least 25 new full-time jobs.
Tier 3: Invest at least $20,000,000 in capital improvements and create at least 200 new full-time jobs, with 80% of all new full-time employees paid 200% of Maryland State minimum wage.
Property must be newly constructed, renovated, expanded, or previously unoccupied; can be owned or leased.
Submit letter of intent and official application before completing construction.
Submit Annual Employment and Certification Report by February 1 each year.
Continue to meet all applicable program requirements each year to retain tax credit.
Cannot have received another tax credit or exemption for the same property in the same taxable year under any other state or county law.
Submit documentation including payroll records, employee timesheets, and supporting documents for the taxable year the credit is claimed and three subsequent years.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Businesses are strongly encouraged to engage with the Department of Business and Economic Development early in the planning process. 2. Submit a letter of intent on company letterhead addressed to the Washington County Board of County Commissioners outlining the project scope, location, and employment plans. 3. Submit the completed Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit Application with all required information including company details, property information, land owner information, and project details. 4. Receive certification from the Washington County Department of Business and Economic Development. 5. After construction completion, notify DBED and provide square footage documentation. 6. Create the required number of full-time employees within the specified timeframe. 7. Each year by February 1st, submit an Annual Employment and Certification Report listing employee information including name, last four digits of Social Security Number, hire date, home city/state, benefits provided, pay rate, and hours worked. 8. Submit a Sample Employment Certification Statement on company letterhead certifying the accuracy of employment data. Failure to apply before hiring or occupying new premises may result in ineligibility for the tax credit.
